Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has become the latest high-ranking U.S. military official to leave the Pentagon amid reports of tensions with Secretary Pete Hegseth.

No official reason has been offered for Driscoll’s departure following 18 months in the role but it comes after CNN and Reuters said he had been butting heads with Hegseth for several months.

According to sources cited by The Atlantic, Driscoll recently “brought up concerns with the administration surrounding Army transformation and readiness and Hegseth’s blocking those efforts specifically by firing the generals who were responsible.” His mission was seemingly unsuccessful.

Nevertheless, President Donald Trump was said to be “surprised and concerned” about the number of the cuts to the department and the seniority of those who have left, The Atlantic reports. The department now has fewer generals than any point in recent history, the outlet adds.

open image in gallery Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has endured a turbulent period in charge of the Department of Defense, defined by culture war vendettas and high staff turnover ( AP )

White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said in a statement addressing the latest exit: “Secretary Driscoll has been highly effective in advancing President Trump’s agenda to Make America Strong Again at the Department of the Army by providing outstanding leadership during historic military operations, restoring an emphasis on readiness and lethality, assisting with negotiations between Russia and Ukraine, and more.

“The United States Army is more powerful than ever thanks to his work alongside the commander-in-chief and secretary of war.”

The Independent has reached out to the Pentagon and the U.S. Army for further comment.

Driscoll is an Iraq War veteran, tech investor and former adviser to Vice President JD Vance, whom he befriended while they were contemporaries at Yale Law School.

When nominating Driscoll in 2024, President Donald Trump hailed him as “a disruptor and change agent.” He went on to make good on that reputation by championing the development of drone warfare technology – only for Hegseth to shut down a European unit focused on that field last month and order it to return to its “core” mission of airborne infantry.

open image in gallery Army Secretary Dan Driscoll, a close friend of Vice President JD Vance, is the latest official to pass through the revolving door ( Getty )

The secretary’s tenure at the Department of Defense has been defined by upheaval, with Hegseth pursuing culture war vendettas against DEI appointments and “woke” values while insisting on loyalty and on the need to nurture a high-testosterone “warfighter” mentality, culminating in an unpopular war the administration was warned against starting and which threatens to dangerously diminish U.S. munitions stockpiles.

Despite the secretary’s attempts to control the narrative, there has also been a steady stream of negative stories about “petty middle-school drama” carrying on at within a department said to be crippled by paranoia, officials claiming they were dismissed for questioning orders and Republican lawmakers losing faith.

It also comes amid growing concerns about how long the war with Iran has gone on for, recently entering its seventh month with no end on sight.

A recent Pentagon assessment warned Hegseth that maintaining the current level of military operations against Tehran could leave the U.S. less able to respond to threats elsewhere and protect the homeland, according to a Washington Post report last week.

Here’s a look at some of the other high-profile figures who have left their jobs at Hegseth’s instigation.

Gen. Charles Q Brown Jr

open image in gallery Gen. Charles Q Brown Jr was one of the first to be dismissed by Hegseth ( Getty )

The first casualty of Hegseth’s tenure was the 40-year Air Force veteran, who was replaced by Lieutenant General Dan “Razin’” Caine as chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff in February 2025.

Brown, who had made history as the Air Force’s first African American chief of staff, had been in the post for 16 months and had expected to continue his term until the fall of 2027.

Trump said in a statement announcing Caine’s nomination that he had been “overlooked” by his predecessor Joe Biden, an apparent slight on Brown, who was nevertheless praised as “a fine gentleman and an outstanding leader.”

Adm. Lisa Franchetti

open image in gallery No reason was given for the removal of the trailblazing Amd. Lisa Franchetti ( Getty )

Hegseth also fired Franchetti – the first woman to serve as chief of naval operations and the first female member of the Joint Chiefs – that same month without explanation.

Biden had nominated her over the preference of his own defense secretary, Lloyd Austin, convinced by her vast experience in command and executive decision making.

Hegseth’s opposition invited concern from other women in the service, who feared they too could be blocked from advancing.

Gen. Tim Haugh

open image in gallery Gen. Tim Haugh was reportedly dismissed under the influence of MAGA influencer Laura Loomer ( Reuters )

Next to go was the director of the U.S. National Security Agency, who was fired along with his deputy Wendy Noble in April last year.

Haugh and Noble’s departures reportedly came after consultation with MAGA influencer Laura Loomer, who beamed on X that they had been dismissed because they had been “disloyal to President Trump” and “handpicked” by former chairman of the Joint Chiefs, Gen. Mark Milley.

Loomer’s role in the firings led to expressions of concern on Capitol Hill.

Vice Adm. Shoshana Chatfield

open image in gallery Vice Adm. Shoshana Chatfield was axed after reportedly appearing on a ‘woke’ list ( AP )

Four days after Haugh’s axing, the former Navy helicopter pilot and combat veteran was fired from her role as U.S. representative to the NATO Military Committee.

That came after she reportedly appeared on a “woke” list drawn up by the Trump administration, which took exception to her past advocacy for diversity in the Armed Forces.

According to the Associated Press, Chatfield was informed by Admiral Christopher Grady, the then-acting chairman of the Joint Chiefs, that the administration wanted to go in a different direction.

Gen. David Allvin

open image in gallery Former Air Force chief of staff Gen. David Allvin was persuaded to take retirement two years early ( Getty )

The following August, the Air Force chief of staff was dismissed with the same message as Chatfield, prompting him to retire two years into his four-year term.

Allvin was thanked for his “transformational” efforts in the role but an insider told The Washington Post his early retirement was “certainly not his choice.”

The general nevertheless issued a statement in which he said: “More than anything, I’m proud to have been part of the team of airmen who live out our core values of integrity, service and excellence every day as we prepare to defend this great nation.”

Lt. Gen. Jeffrey Kruse

open image in gallery Lt. Gen. Jeffrey Kruse led the Defense Intelligence Agency, which angered President Trump by undermining his rhetoric on Iran ( Getty )

There were to be more departures that month, including that of Kruse as head of the Defense Intelligence Agency, which had determined that the administration’s Operation Midnight Hammer airstrikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities were less effective than Trump and Hegseth had claimed.

While the president and his secretary had repeatedly insisted Iran’s capabilities had been “obliterated,” the DIA put out a report suggesting they had only been set back by a matter of months, infuriating Trump.

Also leaving their posts at this time were Vice Adm. Nancy Lacore and Rear Adm. Milton Sands, departing as chiefs of the Navy Reserve and Naval Special Warfare Command respectively.

Gen. Randy George

open image in gallery Army chief of staff Gen. Randy George’s dismissal a matter of weeks into the war was met with concern ( Reuters )

After a period of relative calm – other than the loss of three-star Lt. Gen. Joe McGee from the Pentagon’s Joint Staff in October – Hegseth dismissed the Army’s chief of staff in April this year, perhaps his most controversial call coming a little over a month into the Iran conflict.

The decorated veteran’s firing reportedly came after another clash with Hegseth and was met with solemn scenes when he broke the news to colleagues and indignation in Congress, where the Senate Armed Forces Committee pressed the secretary for an explanation.

The Army’s top uniformed officer has since been replaced on an acting basis by Gen. Christopher LaNeve, who has yet to be confirmed by the Senate.

Navy Secretary John Phelan

open image in gallery Navy Secretary John Phelan came after Hegseth determined new leadership was needed ( Getty )

Three weeks after George was let go, Hegseth ousted the head of the Navy, replacing him with then-undersecretary Hung Cao on an acting basis, shortly after Iran’s move to shut off the Strait of Hormuz caused a spike in global oil prices.

“President Trump and Secretary Hegseth agreed new leadership at the Navy is needed,” a senior administration official told The Independent at the time.

The plight of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, diverted to the Gulf because of the war and starved of necessities, has since come to light, drawing attention to the strain being placed on U.S. military resources by the war.

Gen. Christopher Donahue

open image in gallery Gen. Christopher Donahue is a legend in the U.S. military for being the last U.S. soldier to leave Afghanistan in 2021 ( U.S. Army Europe and Africa )

Prior to Driscoll, the most recent departure from the military’s hierarchy was the commander of U.S. Army forces in Europe and Africa.

Donahue was famously the last American soldier to leave Afghanistan in 2021 and enjoyed a distinguished career leading Delta Force units in Iraq and Afghanistan before commanding the 82nd Airborne Division.

Maj. Gen. Christopher Norrie, Donahue’s deputy, has since stepped in as his interim replacement.

News.title: Dyson launches a new £420 toothbrush – I asked a dentist their opinion
News.content:
After six years in development, Dyson has launched its first toothbrush: the Dyson CameraJet. Given this is the company that brought us bladeless fans and bagless vacuums, it was never going to be a standard brush – if anything, it could risk being over-engineered.

In early July, I was one of the first in the world to see the brush. In a secret briefing at Dyson’s press office in London, a locked silver briefcase sat on the table, shortly to be opened. My first impressions of the brush? It had the same aesthetic as many Dyson products – bulkier than necessary, but distinctive and exciting.

It brushes, flosses and mouth-washes in one, with the help of a camera (that you can also pair with a smartphone app and watch a live feed, if you so wish). It’s available to buy for £419.99 in Dyson Demo Stores and selected retailers. While expensive, it’s surprisingly not an outlier in the market – with top Oral-B and Philips toothbrushes costing up to £800.

News.title: Arsenal maintain perfect start but lack firepower of rivals
News.content:
Bukayo Saka maintained Arsenal’s perfect start to the season, but Mikel Arteta appeared to acknowledge that the Premier League champions are in danger of leaving themselves short in attack.

There is still time for Arteta to add another forward to his squad and whether he does so or not could be important, with the transfer window closing on Tuesday night.

Having sold Leandro Trossard and with Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus on the verge of moves away, Arsenal appear light of forward options.

Lyon winger Malick Fofana has been offered to the club, but he is an underwhelming target given Morgan Rogers and Vinícius Júnior were pursued earlier in the summer.

“We are trying to improve the squad,” Arteta, the Arsenal head coach, said. “Until Tuesday night, we’re going to try to do that. I’ve been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match. I will give it [my energy] now.”

Asked if he currently has enough depth in forward positions, Arteta added: “It depends if everybody is fit or not. We know that the depth has to be really big when you are fighting for four competitions. So we’re going to try to do that.”

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

Sports.content:
Man Utd tease two transfers as squad decisions made ahead of deadline

Manchester United have teased two transfers before the window slams shut on Monday evening. Neither Harry Amass nor striker Chido Obi were included in the Red Devils' under-21 side to face Leicester on Monday evening.

‌



Adam Lawrence's side came away 4-1 victors against Leicester without the help of Amass and Obi, who did not feature in the squad. Shea Lacey, who has impressed in the first team of late, bagged a brace while talented prospect JJ Gabriel scored after Amir Ibragimov got on the scoresheet.

‌



Amass, who spent last season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday and Norwich City in the Championship, is understood to have seen Burnley fail to follow through on earlier interest. The defender is still expected to leave on loan before 11pm, however.

‌



United selling the 19-year-old has not been ruled out. Wolverhampton Wanderers have also been linked with a move for the England youth international.

Obi, meanwhile, is in search of first-team experience. The 18-year-old made his debut for United less than 12 months after joining the club's youth ranks from Arsenal.

Follow the latest updates, rumours and done deals with our Deadline Day Live Blog

‌

Last term, opportunities were harder to come by for the forward, who became United's youngest-ever Premier League starter against Brentford in 2025. That was a conscious decision to aid his development.

Under-21 boss Lawrence revealed that Obi's progress would dictate the club's plans for him this summer, and it appears they feel he would benefit from his first loan.

‌



"It was a conscious decision at the start of the season [last season] for Chido to concentrate his development in the academy environment," Lawrence said earlier this year. "The club were right to do what they did in the window just gone, for Chido to stay in the building.

View 2 Images Chido Obi is planning a loan move (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

"Chido has a group of coaches who believe in his potential and are working hard to help him fulfil it. Obviously, the player must turn up every day hungry to improve.

‌



"We're pushing Chido and challenging him. He has a great programme of games ahead of him and ultimately his level of progression and performance will dictate what happens in the summer."

Speaking at the weekend, Michael Carrick suggested he wouldn't rule out more transfer business before the deadline. The former midfielder is happy with the additions of Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, Karlow Darlow and Carlos Baleba thus far.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"It's always difficult to say, to be honest, when there's so little time left," Carrick said. "I think the situation that we're in, I think the business that we've managed to do, I'm pleased with.

"I think we're a better group, a better squad, potentially a better team, you know. Adding Marcus [Rashford] into that feels like a new signing.

"So, in that respect, we're quite happy. We're always open to if there's something else to be able to add, so I wouldn't shut that down, but as it stands, we'll have to wait and see."

Sports.title: Arsenal's Julian Alvarez Plan B emerges in transfer deadline day rush
Sports.content:
Arsenal's Julian Alvarez Plan B emerges in transfer deadline day rush

The Julian Alvarez transfer saga looks set to end in more frustration for Arsenal and now it appears they may need a Plan B

View 3 Images Julian Alvarez looks set to stay at Atletico Madrid (Image: Angel Martinez, Getty Images)

Arsenal are assessing new transfer targets in the event they are unable to sign Julian Alvarez. The Gunners have been pursuing the Atletico Madrid forward throughout the month.

‌



Mikel Arteta's side have already seen Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior choose not to move to the Emirates Stadium, and it's becoming increasingly likely Alvarez will follow suit. Recent reports have even claimed Alvarez has informed Mikel Arteta he does not want to move to north London.

‌



It appears Arsenal are beginning to accept Alvarez will not be leaving, as reports understand they are drawing up alternative plans.

‌



FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Guardian understands a list of alternative targets, which reportedly includes Everton forward Iliman N'Diaye, has been drawn up. The Senegal international was linked with a move to the Premier League champions earlier in the summer.

He may, however, prove equally difficult to sign, with Manchester City said to be in advanced negotiations over a £65million deal to secure his services. The reigning Premier League champions are continuing to weigh up further options.

‌



Arsenal's forward line is beginning to look increasingly thin on the ground. Leandro Trossard departed for Besiktas earlier in the window, while Gabriel Martinelli is poised to join Al-Hilal in a club-record £56m deal.

View 3 Images N'Diaye is also being chased by Atletico Madrid (Image: Mike Hewitt, Getty Images)

Gabriel Jesus has also agreed a transfer to Barcelona this summer, while fringe player Fabio Vieira is also expected to join Hamburg. On the left wing front, summer recruit Christos Tzolis is anticipated to lead the line, though Eberechi Eze was utilised in the role from the substitutes' bench during the 1-0 away win at Aston Villa.

‌



One potential addition, though, is Malick Fofana from Lyon, but the £35m asking price is currently proving too high for the Gunners.

When pressed on the possibility of signing Julian Alvarez on transfer deadline day, Arteta curtly responded: "I don't know. That's for the people upstairs."

The Gunners' manager did hint that the club will look to tie up further signings on Transfer Deadline Day, saying: "We are trying to improve the squad and until tomorrow night we are going to do that.

‌



View 3 Images Arteta said the club could make some deadline day moves (Image: 2026 Molly Darlington)

"I have been disconnected from the world for 24 hours because I think my energy and focus has to be on the match, but I will get back on it now."

Throughout this summer, Arsenal have splashed in excess of £200m on Tzolis, Bruno Guimaraes, Ezri Konsa, Piero Hincapie and Illan Meslier.

Sports.title: Liverpool's deadline day plan with Ismalia Sarr after transfer collapse
Sports.content:
Liverpool's deadline day plan with Ismalia Sarr after transfer collapse

Liverpool are poised to press on with their squad as it is following Cody Gakpo's failed move to Manchester City - with the Reds ready to end their pursuit of Ismaila Sarr

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo's move away from Liverpool has not materialised (Image: Gaspafotos/MB Media/Getty Images)

Liverpool are ready to stick with their squad as it is on deadline day despite their interest in adding another winger.

‌



The Reds have completed the £123million signing of Bradley Barcola to bolster their attack and had been keen on adding more firepower in the final third. Yankuba Minteh had been on their radar but Brighton rejected their offers, forcing them to look elsewhere.

‌



Liverpool then pivoted to Ismaila Sarr, who top scored for Crystal Palace last season. But Sky Sports reports that Andoni Iraola will not push for any late business after keeping hold of Cody Gakpo, who was linked with a move to Manchester City.

‌



Talks over an £85m deal were underway, but Liverpool later decided to retain the Dutchman. With Gakpo now staying at Anfield Liverpool's need to add to their attack has lessened.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Those at Anfield have poured money into their frontline over the last 12 months and Iraola now has three players who have cost in excess of £100m. Barcola will look to link up with Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, who are both still trying to unlock their best football since moving to the Reds.

‌



Liverpool also added Victor Munoz earlier this summer. The Spaniard scored their equaliser in Saturday's draw with Nottingham Forest. Rio Ngumoha is looking to push his case for more involvement whilst Hugo Ekitike will eventually return from injury. The Frenchman was the Reds' top scorer last season.

Gakpo has started both games for Liverpool this season, scoring against Newcastle and providing an assist against Forest.

View 2 Images Ismaila Sarr has been linked with a move to Liverpool (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Iraola had refused to give any assurances that players who arrive or depart, but did claim that Liverpool were short in the wide areas. Now though it appears as if Liverpool will stick with the options they already have.

"As you know we are trying to sign in that position [wingers] and we cannot talk about players that right now are not ours but it is evident we are trying to improve and fill or trying to fill that position because we don't have the numbers," he said last week. "I hope we can have good news soon but we are still not there."

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Ismaila Sarr transfer update as winger gives green light to move
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Ismaila Sarr transfer update as winger gives green light to move

Liverpool will be looking to add to their squad on the last day of the summer transfer window

View 3 Images Liverpool have been linked with a late move for Crystal Palace's Ismaila Sarr. (Image: PA Wire)

Liverpool have had a stuttering start to the season but they have a chance to bolster their squad on transfer deadline day and overcome their recent woes. The Reds were held to a 2-2 draw with Newcastle United on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season.

‌



They followed that up with yet another frustrating 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest at Anfield on Saturday. Time is ticking away for the Reds to shore up their squad with the deadline at 11pm tonight (Tuesday).

‌



Andoni Iraola has the added bonus of Bradley Barcola joining his squad after he officially signed from PSG on Monday, but the Reds are light on the right flank and in midfield. While it doesn't look like they're going to address all their priorities this window, the Reds are interested in Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr.

‌



Elsewhere, Liverpool have made inroads to secure their future on the flanks with the capture of a young, up-and-coming star.

Sarr stance

Palace are said to remain steadfast in their ambition to keep Sarr this summer, despite interest from Liverpool. The Reds had a £50million bid rejected for the Senegal international last week, but remain interested in the right winger.

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Late Julian Alvarez transfer twist as deadline day talks emerge
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Late Julian Alvarez transfer twist as deadline day talks emerge

There has been some transfer activity involving Arsenal late in the summer window

View 3 Images Mikel Arteta and Arsenal will want to end the summer transfer window in strong fashion (Image: David Price, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

Transfer deadline day is here and Arsenal are still expected to be active before the window shuts at 11pm. With the exception of signing a marquee forward, Gunners sporting director Andrea Berta has addressed each and every one of Mikel Arteta’s squad needs.

‌



The Premier League champions have signed Illan Meslier as a back-up for David Raya in goal and strengthened their defence by bringing in Ezri Konsa as cover for William Saliba. They have also signed Christos Tzolis as an upgrade on Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, while Bruno Guimaraes’ arrival means the former Newcastle captain can take some of the burden off Declan Rice this season.

‌



Where the Gunners have fallen short is their pursuit of a world class player who either plays on the wing or as a striker, having failed to land Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior. They have since turned their attention to long-term target Julian Alvarez, whose future remains uncertain heading into the final hours of the window.

‌



The north Londoners also made progress on the sales front over the weekend, which means Gabriel Jesus and Fabio Vieira have finally moved on. Now, Mirror Football takes a look at two of the latest transfer developments involving Arsenal.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The early signs showing new Premier League season will be very different to last year READ MORE :

Julian Alvarez transfer twist

View 3 Images Atletico Madrid are interested in another striker (Image: Irina R. Hipolito/Europa Press via Getty Images)

‌



Arsenal received a boost to their pursuit of Alvarez on Sunday after it was reported that Atletico Madrid are planning for life after the Argentine striker. The 26-year-old, who the Gunners are still keen to make their record signing at around £128m, has still not given Arteta the green light that he wants to join.

Yet, Fabrizio Romano claims Atletico have lodged a formal offer to sign Jonathan David on loan from Juventus, and the two clubs are now in talks. The offer, which is said to include an option to buy, may indicate that the La Liga side are eyeing David as a replacement for Alvarez, which suggests good news for Arsenal fans.

Given Atleti have blocked Alvarez’s dream move to Barcelona, Arsenal are the likeliest team to sign the forward if he decides to leave the Spanish capital. It was reported at the weekend that the player was given until Sunday to inform Atletico of his decision in order to end the saga once and for all.

‌



Alvarez missed three team training sessions last week because of what the club called an “indisposition”, before training alone on Friday. However, he was seen back on the training pitch with his team-mates on Sunday, with no announcement made yet regarding his future.

Fenerbahce open talks for Nwaneri

View 3 Images Fenerbahce are interested in Ethan Nwaneri (Image: Getty )

Fenerbahce have reportedly opened talks with Arsenal over a deadline day move for Ethan Nwaneri. Turkish outlet Fanatik reports that the 19-year-old has been eyed as a potential signing by the Turkish giants, as they look to bolster their midfield.

‌



Fenerbahce see Nwaneri as the ideal player to fill their U23s quota. It remains to be seen what kind of deal transpires for the Hale End product, as recent reports claimed Arsenal did not want to sell their talented youngster.

Arteta, who admitted the player needs to further his development by playing regular football earlier this month, would prefer a loan deal. However, the Gunners could be swayed to part ways on a permanent basis if a huge offer comes in.

The links with Fenerbahce come after Sky Sports claimed over the weekend that Nwaneri prefers to stay at Arsenal, or to join another Premier League team, as opposed to a move abroad. That’s believed to be due to his miserable loan stint at Marseille in the second half of last season.

Sports.title: Chelsea close to agreeing deal for Roma's Kone
Sports.content:
Chelsea are close to an agreement with Roma to sign France midfielder Manu Kone, but Roma boss Gian Piero Gasperini is trying to keep hold of the player according to Sky in Italy.

A deal worth £52m was understood to have been discussed, with talks also advancing to see winger Jamie Gittens head in the other direction on loan.

Kone is being lined up as a replacement for Enzo Fernandez, with talks ongoing over a move to Manchester City for the Argentina international.

Chelsea's negotiations continue for both Kone and Gittens, but Gasperini's reluctance to let Kone go is an obstacle to overcome.

Gapserini pushed for Kone to stay when he arrived as head coach and was instrumental in securing the France midfielder's immediate future there.

Roma are working on either AC Milan midfielder Youssouf Fofana or Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg to replace Kone.

Could Kone fill Fernandez shoes?

Analysis by Sky Sports' Nick Wright:

Kone has pedigree as a 19-cap France international who, at 25, and with his peak years still ahead of him, has already impressed in Italy, Germany and his homeland, demonstrating a capacity to adapt which could serve him well in the Premier League.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink explains what Chelsea could expect from Manu Kone

The former Borussia Monchengladbach midfielder has good athleticism and technical quality. Like the player he is in line to replace at Chelsea, he can operate at both No 6 and No 8, although it is at the base of midfield that he is most comfortable.

That may suit Alonso given his favoured, three-at-the-back system leaves little room for the No 8 role in which Fernandez previously excelled for the club. It may also suit Kone, who can defend, pass and carry but doesn't offer the same level of attacking threat.

Fernandez thrived in that sense at Chelsea. The Argentina international contributed an impressive total of 16 goals and 11 assists in the last two Premier League seasons.

Chelsea might need to find those goals and assists elsewhere in his squad if he goes, with Kone, a player who has different strengths, having provided only two and five respectively in league games for Roma in the same timeframe.

Sports.title: Why is Antonelli taking grid penalties on home soil in Italy?
Sports.content:
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is highly unlikely to be in contention for victory on home soil at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix.

Antonelli will start at the back of the grid as he will exceed the limit of four power units that can be used in a season before incurring grid penalties.

It means the Mercedes driver could see his 59-point lead over team-mate George Russell and Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton cut significantly, while a third consecutive win for McLaren's Lando Norris could enable the reigning world champion to make major inroads into his 83-point deficit to Antonelli.

With Mercedes having confirmed that Antonelli is taking a grid penalty for changing his engine at this weekend's Italian Grand Prix, Sky Sports F1 explain why the world championship leader has opted to do so at his home race.

Why does Antonelli need to take a penalty?

Mercedes have generally had the car to beat for most of this year, particularly earlier in the season, but the W17 has suffered from reliability issues.

In Antonelli's case, he suffered an electrical shutdown when running in second at the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix in June, which damaged one engine.

Then Mercedes discovered an issue with his engine after July's British Grand Prix, which led the team to fit Antonelli with a fourth engine at the Belgian Grand Prix three races ago, meaning he was already on the limit of the number of power units that can be used before suffering from grid penalties.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kimi Antonelli goes past Mercedes team-mate George Russell before retiring from the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix with an engine failure

Why is Antonelli starting at the back?

F1 power units are split into different components. Had Mercedes only changed the internal combustion engine, which would be Antonelli's fifth of the season, the Italian would only have a 10-grid place penalty.

But Mercedes boss Toto Wolff says Antonelli will "take the full thing", meaning they will change other components that will take him above their respective limits, including the energy store and control electronics. They will both be worth five-grid places each, thus taking Antonelli to 20 grid places.

Once a driver has a 15-grid place penalty or more, the FIA automatically puts you at "the back of the grid", which will happen to Antonelli in Monza.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on The F1 Show podcast, Bernie Collins believes Lando Norris is still in the title fight after his recent improvement with two back-to-back wins

Why have Mercedes chosen Monza?

Monza is known for its long straights, so overtaking is relatively easy compared to other upcoming tracks such as Madrid and Baku, which are street circuits.

At the 2021 Italian Grand Prix, Valtteri Bottas powered through from the back to the podium after an engine change, while Max Verstappen won from 14th at the 2022 Belgian Grand Prix.

"Monza is an energy-starved circuit with four overtaking zones. A driver cannot defend all of them, so a faster car should be able to make progress relatively straightforwardly," said Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin on the team's Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show.

"The primary factor is when the hardware is needed. We have lost internal combustion engines at relatively low mileage, so we know we must introduce new components by a certain point. If that falls at a circuit where starting at the back would be particularly costly, we may choose to bring the change forward."

Formula 1 2026 remaining races Italy September 4-6 Mexico Oct 30-Nov 1 Madrid September 11-13 Brazil November 6-8 Azerbaijan September 24-26 Las Vegas November 20-22 Malaysia October 2-4 Qatar November 27-29 Singapore* October 9-11 Abu Dhabi December 4-6 USA October 23-25 *denotes Sprint weekend

Currently, 12 more rounds remain of the 2026 F1 season - although that could be reduced to 11 depending on whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix take place.

Shovlin also hinted Mercedes would rather take grid penalties with Antonelli now, compared to later in the year when the title race could be closer.

"We also lead both championships, so there is logic in taking the pain now rather than adding pressure if the margins tighten later in the season," he continued.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mercedes team-mates Kimi Antonelli and George Russell reflect on their Dutch Grand Prix race

What about Russell's engine situation?

Russell is in a similar position to Antonelli and will also have grid penalties for exceeding his engine allocation later this season.

Sky Sports News understand that Russell will definitely not join Antonelli at the back of the grid this weekend, as Mercedes continue to assess the British driver's situation.

"We must manage the remaining events so that both cars reach the end of the season with the freshest and best-performing hardware possible," said deputy team principal Bradley Lord.

"It is a constant trade-off between the risk of running high-mileage components and the points cost of taking a grid penalty and recovering through the field."

Sports.title: Osaka's look inspired by NBA legend Iverson in opening US Open win
Sports.content:
Naomi Osaka made her usual fashionable entrance as she channelled former NBA superstar Allen Iverson at the US Open.

The two-time US Open champion emerged from the tunnel onto the court in Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing a long, white skirt and a hooded robe featuring newspaper clippings about her.

When she removed that to reveal her black outfit, Osaka had her hair styled in cornrows, just as Iverson did when he was the NBA MVP while playing for the Philadelphia 76ers.

She advanced to the second round after overcoming a stern challenge from ‌Anastasia Zakharova to secure a 7-6 (8-6) 7-6 (7-3) victory.

"It's my, I guess, my tribute to Iverson. I really like him a lot," Osaka said. "I mean, Nike said basketball, so I said, 'OK, you want basketball, I'll give you basketball.'"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Naomi Osaka made her latest fashion statement ahead of her first round match against Anastasia Zakharova at the US Open.

She wore a shirt with Iverson's picture when she met with the media on the eve of the tournament and called him a "trailblazer".

"I think he's also someone that I look up to a lot, because he's kind of done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not, but he's shifted the way that NBA players dress," Osaka said Saturday.

"I also think the whole conversation around clothes in sports and also just expressing yourself through style, I feel like he's someone that I look up to in that regard."

Osaka added that they'd never communicated, but Iverson posted a message for her on his Instagram page Monday, writing: "Wow, what a honor!! BIG FAN can't wait to meet you."

Sports.title: Saka earns hard-fought win for Arsenal at Villa
Sports.content:
Bukayo Saka's goal just before the hour mark was enough for champions Arsenal to maintain their perfect start with a 1-0 win over Aston Villa at Villa Park.

This fixture was one of the few matches that the Gunners lost in winning the Premier League title last season but Saka's close-range effort decided what was a tight game despite an improved showing from Unai Emery's much-changed Aston Villa line-up.

Villa were four down after 31 minutes in that astonishing capitulation at Brighton on the opening weekend but they showed far more resilience against the Gunners from the outset. Emiliano Buendia crashed the ball against David Raya's crossbar on 12 minutes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bukayo Saka breaks the deadlock

Mikel Arteta's men, unchanged from the win over Coventry, were their usual probing selves, asking searching questions from set pieces and controlling possession for long periods. But Gabriel's mistimed header was as close as they came in the first half.

Christos Tzolis was substituted at half-time having been booked and running the risk of a red card after that, but the introduction of Eberechi Eze worked out well. Arsenal ramped up the pressure in the second half with the ever-impressive Saka to the fore.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emi Buendia's 20-yard effort smashes the bar – but was there a foul just before?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player VAR overturns an Arsenal penalty as contact is ruled to be outside the box

Arsenal's talisman thought he had won a penalty early in the second half but Ian Maatsen's foul was ruled to be outside the box following a VAR review. It mattered not because he forced in Riccardo Calafiori's centre from close range soon afterwards.

The home side, who included debutants Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson in their starting line-up, pushed for an equaliser but Arsenal, who brought on former Villa man Ezri Konsa late on, stayed strong to claim the win. A show of strength by the champions.

Still no shot on target for Villa Aston Villa are not only without a point from their opening two games but they are yet to register a shot on target.

The key moments from Villa Park

12 - BAR! Buendia lashes the ball against Raya's crossbar

56 - VAR! Saka denied penalty as Maatsen's foul is outside box

59 - GOAL! Calafiori's low cross is forced into the net by Saka

75 - MISS! Suzuki saves one-on-one from Havertz but he is off

Arteta hails 'massive win'

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta speaking to Sky Sports:

"Really happy. A massive win. A tough place to come and earn the three points. We deserved it. A great squad performance - because when 11 wasn't enough the finishers came in and did a magnificent job to finish off the game.

"Last year we lost here in a really difficult way, with the last kick of the game. And that was still in the tummy.

"We are in the second game and it's like, 'we have to win this game!'

"We know that last year was the same. We know the level, we know how difficult it is for every team to earn points in this league, so we have to be really proud tonight."

Emery focuses on the positives

Aston Villa manager Unai Emery speaking to Sky Sports:

"We've lost. We competed well. We are trying to rebuild the team but a lot of positive things after the result. How we compete defensively, with the ball. We didn't create clear chances but we didn't concede clear chances. It was so equal, the match.

"Some players made their debut, fantastic. Suzuki, Jackson both very good work. The first step forward, Today is positive for the next matches.

"To lose one match is painful but after we must try to get positive things. This is the reason I am being optimistic. There are 38 matches, we played two matches and didn't achieve points but hopefully we can get better."

Arsenal's depth stands out

Tzolis has made a promising start to his Arsenal career but this was a more difficult evening for him. The response from Arteta? Bring on Eze. He helped open it up for Arsenal to win. When Villa pushed, the Arsenal boss turned to Bruno Guimaraes and Mikel Merino to battle it out.

"Guimaraes demonstrated already with a couple of passes he's going to be something very different to what they've already got," said Gary Neville on co-commentary for Sky Sports.

"He cuts through with his passing; he always looks for that furthest forward pass. Arsenal sometimes are guilty of recycling it too much - he won't do that."

But just as significant was how robust Arsenal looked in seeing this out. As well as the physical midfield trio, Konsa came on for Cristhian Mosquera. Villa did not even manage a shot on target. Rock solid.

With different players for different situations and back-to-back wins, the Gunners have already shown why they are still the team to beat in the Premier League. And they might just have got better.

Suzuki impresses on debut

As Premier League debuts go, replacing World Cup-winning goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez for a game against the champions Arsenal right in front of the Holte End must be among the more daunting. Suzuki acquitted himself impressively for Aston Villa.

The Japan goalkeeper failed to claim one early cross but when he tipped over a near-post header soon after, the Villa fans were chanting 'the world's number one' - a playful reference to the popular chant that was traditionally directed at Martinez at Villa Park.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville hails Ederson-esque pass from Zion Suzuki for Aston Villa

There was a little more lustre to the chant later in the first half when Suzuki pinged a pass out to George Hemmings on the left wing - arrowing the ball with extraordinary power. His distribution with both feet already looks likely to be a weapon for the team.

Suzuki did spill one fiercely struck shot in the second half but he denied Kai Havertz when one-on-one - not knowing that the offside flag would go up. Even in defeat, it was an encouraging showing by the new Villa goalkeeper.

Sports.title: Alcaraz impresses on return from injury as Sabalenka also wins
Sports.content:
Carlos Alcaraz impressed on his return to tennis with a straight-sets win over Russia's Roman Safiullin in the first round of the US Open.

Alcaraz has not played a competitive singles match since withdrawing from the Barcelona Open in April with a wrist injury that forced him to miss the French Open and Wimbledon.

The severity of the injury, which did not require surgery, meant Alcaraz was a doubt for the US Open but he entered Flushing Meadows and showed with his 6-4 6-4 6-4 win over Safiullin that he cannot be dismissed from defending his title from last year.

Henman: Alcaraz got the game he wanted Sky Sports Tennis' Tim Henman



"If you’d have asked Alcaraz how he’d have liked this game to go, he would have signed up for a straight-sets victory, a few pressure moments, and just over two hours work.



"That is exactly what he got today. He and his team will be delighted with all aspects of this game."

"There were some doubts in the match, I'm not going to lie. Thinking about if I would last the match, best of five, playing four or five sets," said Alcaraz, who will play Portugal's Jaime Faria in the next round.

"I had a little bit of doubt, but I tried to forget everything and focus on the things I needed to improve. I thought about what would happen in the match and physically I felt really well."

Watched on by rapper Travis Scott, who helped design Alcaraz's brown outfit for the US Open, there was plenty of attention on the seven-time Grand Slam champion's serve and groundstroke speed, given he had not played competitive singles for over four months.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Carlos Alcaraz reflected on his US Open round one win. against Roman Safiullin

He needed to save two break points from Safiullin in his opening three service games before breaking himself in the eighth game which proved enough to claim the opening set.

Alcaraz was broken at the start of the second set but broke back immediately and upped his intensity to break in the eighth game again and go on to win the second set.

After an early break in the third set, Alcaraz never came under threat on his serve and continued to move well while maintaining a high level on both wins to see off the tricky Russian.

One of the biggest threats in Alcaraz's half was Arthur Fils, after he won the Cincinnati Open title last week, but he was knocked out of the tournament by Stefanos Tsitsipas in a 4-6 7-6 (7-3) 6-1 6-4 defeat.

Sabalenka overcomes Osorio test

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Aryna Sabalenka and Camila Osorio

Like Alcaraz, Aryna Sabalenka started her US Open title with a straight-sets win as she beat Colombia's Camila Osorio 6-2 6-4.

Sabalenka is bidding to become the first player to win three consecutive US Open titles since Serena Williams in 2014 and was put under serious pressure by Osorio in the second set.

"Camila is a tough opponent but I was ready to do whatever it takes to get the win," she told Sky Sports Tennis.

"I really enjoyed the atmosphere and support. A fun and tough match but happy to get through in straight sets."

Sabalenka's form has been questioned after losing in the last 16 in her last three tournaments - Wimbledon, the Canadian Open and Cincinnati Open.

It means she could lose her status as world No 1 for the first time since October 2024 with Elena Rybakina, Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula all having the chance to knock Sabalenka off her perch.

But Sabalenka's best surface is the hard court, having won her four Grand Slam titles on hard, and her raw power will always make the Belarusian difficult to beat.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Aryna Sabalenka hits back at critics, saying she is tired of the negativity surrounding her with everything she does both on and off the court

Elsewhere, Wimbledon runner-up Karolina Muchova will be looking for another big run and she got off to a great start by beating Austria's Sinja Karus 6-3 6-0.

Last year's US Open runner-up Amanda Anisimova defeated compatriot Ashlyn Krueger 6-1 6-3 and was joined by three more victorious Americans in the women's draw on Monday as Emma Navarro, Taylor Townsend and Cate McNally also won.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player How many previous US Open winners could you name in 20 seconds?

Brits Dart and Fearnley fight back to progress; Wendelken out

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the US Open first-round match between Jacob Fearnley and Martin Landaluce

Britain's Harriet Dart and Jacob Fearnley both fought back from losing positions to reach the second round of the US Open.

Dart was a set and a break down before roaring back to a 3-6 6-3 6-2 win over American Peyton Stearns.

Her coach and Sky Sports Tennis pundit Marion Bartoli said: "I'm really pleased for her. Such a great effort and mentally it's so hard to come back but she fought so hard. It's absolutely brilliant."

That was followed by a superb win for Jacob Fearnley after he beat Spain's Martin Landaluce 4-6 6-2 4-6 7-5 6-3.

Landaluce served for the match in the fourth set but Fearnley won three games in a row to take the match to a deciding set and continued that momentum in the fifth.

Despite missing a routine smash to win the match, Fearnley kept his composure and ensured he made the second round at Flushing Meadows for a second successive year.

Sports.title: Football transfer deadline day: latest on Fernández, Álvarez, Ndiaye and more – live
Sports.content:
6m ago 06.09 EDT Doug Fenner gets in touch to say: “I realise the world, or the universe, revolves around the Premier League, but who on Earth thought it was a good idea to have transfer deadline day on a day where there is almost a full slate of EFL fixtures (or vice versa)? “L1 and L2 clubs in particular aren’t overburdened with support staff and so are those that are available supposed to be in two places at once, getting points and players at the same time? “Fans will be scouring the team sheets before kick-off tonight to see which if their favourites are strangely missing from line-ups, perhaps for ever.” It does feel like a naive decision but at least everyone has had plenty of time to plan. Share

7m ago 06.08 EDT We are beyond 11am BST, so there are fewer than 12 hours to go of this rollercoaster window. Anything can happen [in the next half hour]. Share

29m ago 05.47 EDT Billy Munday Billy Munday is on La Liga duty today, with plenty of transfer-related notions. double quotation mark If Raphinha has any misgivings about playing as a makeshift No 9 for Barcelona, he is doing a good job of hiding it. Julián Álvarez would have been proud of the Brazilian’s two neat finishes that inspired the Spanish champions to a 5-2 victory against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night, 24 hours before the transfer deadline. Lamine Yamal scored two wonderful goals of his own in a performance that reassured everyone he is back to his best. Add Anthony Gordon to the mix – impressive again in his link-up play – and you have a fluid, fearsome front three. Yet after the departures of Ferran Torres, Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford this summer, there is no doubt Barcelona not only still want a centre-forward but require one – at least one. Hansi Flick was very happy to see Gabriel Jesus, an £8.6m arrival from Arsenal, in the stands. “He’s a top striker,” the coach said. But Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez is the ultimate prize. Barcelona breeze past Rayo but all eyes in Spain remain on Julián Álvarez Read more Share

33m ago 05.42 EDT Kevin Wilson writes: “Crazy amounts of money spent by the three promoted clubs. They’ve outspent most of the other established clubs outside of the Champions League clubs (and Spurs!) A huge gamble, least of all as most of the signed players have no experience of English football. I suppose they will sell or loan them out if the worst happens.”



I think it is the nature of the modern game, namely because the difference between the Championship and Premier League is growing. Without spending, there is zero chance of staying up. Share

Sports.title: Football transfer rumours: Manchester United and Liverpool eye Kroupi? Vardy to Wrexham?
Sports.content:
The final day of the men’s transfer window is here, but there is still time for some rumourmongering, before a Supermarket Sweep-style trolley dash for 11th-hour signings.

Going wild in the aisles? Manchester United’s interest in a new left-back has been known all summer long, yet here they stand without one on the final day of the window. While many are claiming United’s business could be done, RB Leipzig’s David Raum, Fulham stalwart Antonee Robinson and Fenerbahce’s English left-back Archie Brown have all been mentioned as possible last-minute acquisitions. Jorge Salinas of Racing Santander has been tracked by United throughout the window and some are reporting that deal could be done today for €16m (£13.7m). Burnley are keen on United’s own youngster Harry Amass, but his departure may depend on a left-back coming in.

Speaking of United, remember Jadon Sancho? Well, the one-time £74m Old Trafford signing is still a free agent after his contract expired, with his former club Borussia Dortmund ready to take a chance on him providing he signs a heavily incentivised contract.

United and Liverpool are also credited with an interest in Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, though they may not have much time to press on with the transfer. Arsenal have also glanced admiringly in the direction of 20-year-old Frenchman, who is one of the jewels in the Cherries’ crown.

It appears Liverpool knocked back an audacious approach by Nottingham Forest for their young midfielder Trey Nyoni. The 19-year-old is rated highly by Andoni Iraola, and not even a £30m Forest bid tempted the Reds to sell.

Which midfielder will Chelsea sign if and when Manchester City’s pursuit of Enzo Fernández finally bears fruit? Alex Scott, Lamine Camara and Manu Koné have all been identified as targets for the Blues, but only one of those deals can feasibly be achieved on deadline day. Alternatively, is Eduardo Camavinga still attainable for Chelsea or someone else? Noises are coming out of Madrid suggesting Real could listen to offers of around £60m today.

Let’s move on to Everton, who look to have missed out on Richarlison and Stuttgart’s Jamie Leweling but should be able to bring Jack Grealish back on loan, as well as Kenny Tete from Fulham. Tim Iroegbunam is off to Hull and Iliman Ndiaye looks destined for Manchester City after their deal for Cody Gakpo hit the rocks.

The Championship is often where the juiciest deadline-day activity takes place, and Derby are battling Blackburn to re-sign Brighton defender Eiran Cashin on loan. Meanwhile, Wrexham, who were accused by Sheffield United’s Chris Wilder of “blanket bombing” in their bid to sign his player Callum O’Hare, are also considering Portsmouth’s Adrian Segecic and Bristol City’s Scott Twine, while an eye-catching free transfer for Jamie Vardy remains a possibility.

Sports.title: Barcelona breeze past Rayo but all eyes in Spain remain on Julián Álvarez
Sports.content:
If Raphinha has any misgivings about playing as a makeshift No 9 for Barcelona, he is doing a good job of hiding it. Julián Álvarez would have been proud of the Brazilian’s two neat finishes that inspired the Spanish champions to a 5-2 victory against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night, 24 hours before the transfer deadline. Lamine Yamal scored two wonderful goals of his own in a performance that reassured everyone he is back to his best. Add Anthony Gordon to the mix – impressive again in his link-up play – and you have a fluid, fearsome front three.

Yet after the departures of Ferran Torres, Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford this summer, there is no doubt Barcelona not only still want a centre-forward but require one – at least one. Hansi Flick was very happy to see Gabriel Jesus, an £8.6m arrival from Arsenal, in the stands. “He’s a top striker,” the coach said. But Atlético Madrid’s Álvarez is the ultimate prize.

While Mikel Arteta has apparently attempted to speed up a possible deal with a phone call to Álvarez, the Barcelona president, Joan Laporta, has conducted his interest largely in public. He stirred the pot again last Wednesday after Arsenal’s interest was firmed up. “This whole situation has created a lot of noise,” said Laporta, who specialises in creating a lot of noise, in a video on Barça’s social channels. “Atlético told us they were not selling [Alvarez]. However, it looks like, from what we hear now, they are trying to reach agreements with other clubs.”

Laporta left little to the imagination: “We are very interested in buying Julián Álvarez. We would like our offer to be accepted.” Atlético are not playing ball – and who can blame them? Barcelona’s courting of Antoine Griezmann, who announced he was staying at Atlético in a TV documentary in 2018 only to move to the Camp Nou in 2019, still leaves a sour taste. Again they have shown disapproval at Barcelona’s behaviour in their pursuit of Álvarez. “This situation isn’t about money, it’s about dignity,” an embattled Atlético said in a statement the day after Laporta’s video message.

After the hostile reception he received from Atlético’s fans at the Metropolitano when coming on as a substitute against Villarreal the previous weekend, Álvarez missed some training sessions and Saturday’s 3-1 win at Sevilla. Atlético said the striker was unwell. He returned to training on Sunday, with Arsenal appearing his only route out by the end of Tuesday – “there is zero consideration of an Álvarez transfer to Barcelona,” Atlético said.

Álvarez’s absence was felt keenly at the Camp Nou on Monday – for about 20 minutes. After some sloppy Barcelona finishing and an emphatic strike from Rayo’s Sergio Camello, a striker who came through Atlético’s academy, the headlines were obvious. But the narrative did not come to the rescue of the Rayo centre-back Pathé Ciss, who ended up on his backside after Raphinha skipped past him and slotted in the equaliser.

View image in fullscreen Gabriel Jesus gestures upon arrival at the airport in Barcelona on Monday. Photograph: Enric Fontcuberta/EPA

On an evening when Argentina’s footballers were writing Instagram posts about international retiree Lionel Messi, Barcelona’s current No 10 paid tribute in his own way. Lamine Yamal cut inside and whipped a shot past the flying Dani Cárdenas, high at his near post, to establish a lead that was never surrendered. After rumours about the 19-year-old’s fitness and wellbeing circulated after his sluggish start to the season, Flick reminded everyone that the kid had only three weeks’ holiday since beating Messi and Argentina in the World Cup final. Lamine Yamal was reaching his “top level” in training, Flick insisted, and it was hard to argue with him.

It was also hard to argue with Florian Lejeune when the Rayo defender said in a half-time interview that Barcelona “are very good”. Six minutes after the restart, he turned the ball into his own net. Gordon, the most expensive outlay at the Camp Nou this summer except perhaps for the new roof that is still under construction, provided the cross for that own goal and a great deal more from the left wing. The England forward’s selfless passing and running has quickly endeared him to supporters and there were chants of “Gordon, Gordon, Gordon” from behind the goal. His backheel set up Raphinha’s second and Barça’s fourth to make it three assists in three games.

View image in fullscreen Raphinha (right) celebrates scoring Barcelona’s fourth goal with Lamine Yamal. Photograph: Lluís Gené/AFP/Getty Images

After an hour of chasing after Pedri, Dani Olmo and Marc Bernal, Rayo’s midfield had to contend with Rodri off the bench. The marquee arrival from Manchester City did not have the chance to parade the World Cup he had won as Spain’s captain before his Barcelona debut in last Thursday’s win over Athletic . Barça snubbed the trophy presentation following a row over the arrest of one of their supporters who was carrying an Estelada flag – a symbol of the Catalan independence movement – outside the stadium before their season opener at Elche. Athletic’s Spain players had faced whistles from some Basque fans when they presented the trophy in Bilbao. Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella and Real Sociedad’s Mikel Oyarzabal were given a warm reception at the Bernabéu last week.

Lamine Yamal’s second against Rayo, another Messi-esque finish from the edge of the box, put the result beyond doubt. Barcelona and Real Madrid – the only teams with 100% records after three games – are yet to blink as the title race begins, but all eyes on transfer deadline day, you expect, will be on the exit door at Atlético’s training ground.

Talking points

While Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé were on the scoresheet in Real Madrid’s 4-0 home win against Málaga, it was the performance of Trent Alexander-Arnold that was perhaps most striking. The former Liverpool right-back was a creative force, setting up Madrid’s third for Mbappé, in his first start under José Mourinho. Mbappé, tipped for the Ballon d’Or by Mourinho last week, topped the scoring charts for a day or so after his sweeping finish from Alexander-Arnold’s low cross.
