McLaren's solution isn't too dissimilar to how it fixed Norris last year, working with Piastri behind the scenes to make adaptations both from a car and driving style point of view. If it succeeds, it has its two aces back for what is shaping up to be a closely-fought second half of 2026, and a potential title challenge next year.

McLaren's end goal is still for both drivers to be fighting each other for wins and titles, which would involve Piastri following a similar trajectory towards a long-term contract extension. It is up to the Australian's camp to decide whether that's in his interest, or whether it might be time to explore new horizons. In any case, Piastri's current deal until the end of 2028 means time is on his side. The same can be said for McLaren.

In the meantime, McLaren has its reigning world champion tied up for the entirety of the current rules cycle. It's one less puzzle piece on the board as the Woking squad aims to retain and even reinforce its title-winning team.

Sports.title: Norris extends McLaren deal until F1 2030
Sports.content:
Lando Norris and McLaren have agreed to a long-term contract extension, keeping the world champion at the Formula 1 team until at least 2030.

On Saturday morning McLaren announced it had tied Norris to the team until 2030, with multi-year options to further extend the 26-year-old's stay. Norris personally announced the news to the Woking factory staff during the team's annual family and friends open day.

"McLaren is my home, and I’m very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030," Norris said. "When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win championships.

"We’ve achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we’re capable of achieving it. I can’t wait to get back in the car in Monza and I’m very excited about what the future holds for us, both over the rest of this season, and in the coming years.”

Norris' previous deal ran until the end of 2027, effectively increasing the Briton's stay at Woking for at least four more years. Team-mate Oscar Piastri is still under contract until the end of 2028 after extending his deal at the start of last year.

Salaries are rarely revealed in F1, but it stands to reason Norris is in line for a bumper pay rise off the back of his world title and his all-round progress as a driver, which has carried through into a strong first half of 2026. Norris capitalised on McLaren's car upgrades to win the last two grands prix in Hungary and the Netherlands.

Lando Norris, McLaren Photo by: Pauline Ballet - Formula 1

In addition to the new contract extension, Norris was also gifted with his championship-winning 2025 car, the MCL39.

Team principal Andrea Stella was "delighted" to continue working with Norris for the foreseeable future. "He is an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren, but above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team," Stella said.

"Since joining McLaren as part of our junior programme, he has grown with us and played a central role in bringing the team back to the front of Formula 1. This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together. With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1."

Norris started his McLaren journey as a junior driver in 2017, before being promoted to a race seat in 2019. He has since exclusively raced for the papaya squad and amassed 13 grand prix wins, 18 poles, and 48 podiums.

The team's CEO Zak Brown, who has played an integral role in bringing Norris through the ranks, said: “His journey with the team is a fantastic example of our commitment to identifying, developing and supporting world-class talent, and his achievements speak for themselves.

"Together with Andrea, Oscar and the wider team, Lando has helped drive McLaren into a new papaya era of success, helping us go from the back of the grid, to double consecutive constructors’ titles in 2024 and 2025 and our first drivers’ championship in 17 years.

"We are extremely excited about what lies ahead and remain fully focused on continuing to compete for wins and championships.”

Sports.title: Mercedes still searching for answers on why it was “rubbish” through high-speed corners in Dutch GP
Sports.content:
Mercedes trackside engineering director Andrew Shovlin rated the team’s pace through Zandvoort’s high-speed corners as “rubbish” and is looking for answers on its inconsistency between both stints and drivers in the Formula 1 Dutch Grand Prix.

After a strong start to the Zandvoort weekend, with George Russell taking pole and victory in the sprint race, Mercedes dropped behind McLaren’s Lando Norris, who secured pole and victory in the grand prix.

While Mercedes still took 2-3 in qualifying and the race, with Kimi Antonelli getting the better of team-mate Russell in the race to extend his championship lead to 59 points, the team was at a loss on why its early pace didn’t carry through the weekend relative to its main competition.

“We've got a few things on the performance side to try and dig into,” Shovlin said on Mercedes’ Nu Silver Arrows Radio Show. “We're going to be getting on with that this week and see what we learn.

“But there were a few corners where we were pretty rubbish, like that combination of [Turns] 7, 8, 9. You could see [it in] the faster-speed [curves]. And it also gives the tyres on the left-hand side of the car a tough time. And we don't really understand yet fully what's causing that.

“We've got some ideas, but that's not a problem that we've suffered with so far this year. And there's plenty of circuits that have got kind of continued corners in one direction.

“We were a bit off the pace in the fastest of those [turns]. And then our problems kind of grew a bit as we went through. All the other corners look solid.”

James Allison, Mercedes, Andrew Shovlin, Mercedes Photo by: Sam Bloxham / LAT Images via Getty Images

What added to Mercedes’ confusion was that minimal changes were made to the cars between the sprint race and grand prix, as well as during the race itself. While Shovlin accepts a level of expected pace deviation per tyre compounds and life, seeing each driver suffer at different times during the grand prix left Mercedes uncertain about the cause.

“We didn't change the car. We obviously had different compounds at different stages. But again, we need to understand a bit,” he said.

“George's first stint was a bit lacklustre compared to his later ones. And then with Kimi, first stint was good, and then dropped a bit on the second, dropped a bit more on the third, a bit came back on the third. It wasn't like we were playing around with electronic settings or up and down on flap angles. And for him, the balance of the car was quite different stint on stint.

“The two drivers, normally they report similar things with a car at the end of the race. Both of them, their perception of the balance, and probably the reality is George had a more understeery car, Kimi had a more oversteery car. If we look at how they were set up, we don't yet know quite why we got such a big difference.

Read Also:

“So, though, really good to have a strong point-scoring weekend when we weren't at our best in terms of performance. It was actually good fun, sat on the pitwall and having to make decisions in a hurry. I think the whole team enjoyed that and rose to the occasion. And it was definitely a good result, given where we were.

“But yeah, a bit of head-scratching to do over the next few days.”

As Shovlin pointed out, Mercedes still picked up its second-highest points score as a team this season – 46 points, only behind the 55 points it notched up at the Chinese GP – granted both were sprint race weekends with more points on offer.

Sports.title: Ukraine appeals to FIA Court of Appeal over lifting of Russia ban | Formula 1
Sports.content:
The Ukrainian Automobile Federation is reportedly appealing against the FIA’s decision to reverse its ban on Russians competing in motorsport and displaying their flag at its events.

The federation is bringing an appeal to the FIA Court of Appeal over the U-turn.

The FIA’s decision came into effect on August 3rd, though the governing body did not announce it for another 10 days. The federation formally objected to the decision three days later and subsequently requested the FIA’s ethics committee.

The governing body originally announced the ban, which also applies to Belarussia, in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022. The war continues and the FIA’s announcement of its decision did not give any reasons for its change.

Until 2022, Russian racer Nikita Mazepin competed in Formula 1 and his father’s company sponsored Haas, which ran in Russian colours. F1 also held a race in Russia, at Sochi Autodrom, from 2014 to 2021. F1 cancelled its contract in response to the invasion and the FIA has not relaxed its ban on events taking place in Russia or Belarussia.

In 2023, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem said he had opposed taking action against Russia over the war. The BBC reported Ben Sulayem proposed relaxing the ban on Russian participation in motorsport, and stated the FIA said its decision followed a similar announcement by the International Olympic Committee in July.

The Ukrainian Automobile Federation is challenging the FIA’s decision as it claims the Russian Automobile Federation is operating offices in parts of Ukraine which Russia has invaded, in Sevastopol, Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia. The federation’s website prominently displays names of its members who have been killed in the war since it began.

Sports.title: Ferrari reveals 1996 Schumacher tribute livery for home race at Monza | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari will run a special livery for their home race at Monza commemorating Michael Schumacher’s 1996 Italian Grand Prix victory.

The team called the design “a special livery inspired by the Ferrari F310” which Schumacher drove during his first season with the team 30 years ago. He won three races for them, the Spanish, Belgian and Italian grands prix.

Ferrari described their livery for this weekend’s race as “predominantly red, with some white on the wings, together with black.”

“The wheels, from BBS as was the case back then, have a hint of gold, recalling the original colour of the magnesium rims used that season,” they added.

The design also incorporates Schumacher’s ‘MS’ logo and the seven-starred helmet design he wore later in his career. He arrived at Ferrari as a two-times world champion and won five titles with them in consecutive seasons from 2000 to 2004.

Ferrari drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc will also wear special overalls for this weekend’s race.

The team will arrange two demonstration runs during the event using an F2002 chassis which Schumacher raced in 2002. Four-times world champion and former Ferrari driver Sebastian Vettel will demonstrate the car before the grand prix on Sunday and Rubens Barrichello, Schumacher’s team mate from 2000 to 2005, will do the same on Saturday.

Sports.title: Argentina ready to host Formula 1 again, says president | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Argentina’s president Javier Milei says the country is ready to host the Formula 1 world championship again.

Milei made the claim while opening the FIA American Congress in Buenos Aires.

“The Automovil Club Argentino has made an enormous contribution to national motorsport, and Argentina is a country that loves cars,” said Milei. “The Argentine passion for racing is timeless.

“That is why I invite you to dream with me. Argentina has all the conditions necessary to once again welcome Formula One and the World Rally Championship onto its calendar.

“We have the tradition. We have the drivers. And now we are once again developing the institutional seriousness that these categories demand before choosing a country. We have absolutely everything.”

Franco Colapinto became Argentina’s first Formula 1 driver since 2001 when he joined the series two years ago. Alpine recently extended his contract to drive for them again next year.

Colapinto’s huge popularity in Argentina was demonstrated when he performed a demonstration run in Buenos Aires before hundreds of thousands of fans in April.

Last week the FIA condemned the abuse of its stewards after being inundated with complaints on social media from Colapinto’s supporters over two penalties he received in the previous round. The FIA did not mention Colapinto by name.

Argentina last hosted the world championship in 1998. F1 first visited the country in the fifties when Argentina’s Juan Manuel Fangio won his home grand prix four times on his way to claiming a then-record five world championship titles.

All 20 Argentinian grands prix took place at the Autodromo de Buenos Aires Oscar y Juan Galvez. A plan to redevelop the circuit and bring it up to F1 standards was proposed in 2017, but did not go ahead.

Sports.title: Social Media: “The car of my dreams” – Hamilton gets a Ferrari F40 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Lewis Hamilton has a new addition to his road car collection: a Ferrari F40.

The seven-times world champion, who joined Ferrari last year, said the F40 is “the car of my dreams and has been for as long as I can remember.”

Ferrari began producing the F40 in 1987. It was the last road car created by the company under the guidance of its founder, Enzo Ferrari.

“As a kid I dreamt of having one,” said Hamilton, who was two years old when Ferrari first began producing the F40. “When I joined Ferrari last year I made sure to have one with me on my first day at Maranello. That’s how much it means to me.”

The car has a three-litre V8 twin-turbo engine producing around 351kW. Ferrari claims the car can hit a top speed of 324kph.

“These cars are works of art and incredibly rare,” Hamilton continued, “so when I found this one, covered in dust after being sat in a garage for over thirty years, I knew I had to bring her home. First to Maranello, where the master engineers and mechanics at the factory worked for weeks to bring her back to life.

“Massive thank you to everyone who had a hand in this project. This has truly been a dream come true. I can’t wait to share more with you all.”

Sports.title: Palou clinches fifth IndyCar championship title in seven years | IndyCar
Sports.content:
Alex Palou continued his domination of the IndyCar series by clinching his fifth title on Sunday.

The 29-year-old has won the championship in all bar two of the seven seasons he has contested it. He debuted in the series at Dale Coyne in 2020 before moving to Ganassi the following year. He has delivered the title for his current team every season except 2022, when Penske’s Will Power won the championship.

Palou claimed his latest title with one round remaining. He has claimed six victories so far this season – two fewer than last year. He took pole position for the series’ blue riband race, the Indianapolis 500, but was unable to repeat his 2025 victory.

His latest championship triumph came in unusual circumstances during the series’ double-header race weekend at the Milwaukee Mile oval. Saturday’s first race was halted due to rain, and not resumed until after the completion of Sunday’s second race.

Andretti’s Kyle Kirkwood was Palou’s closest threat heading into last weekend, but finished behind him in both races. Palou clinched the title with a 100-point lead over McLaren’s Christian Lundgaard by the end of the weekend.

McLaren’s Pato O’Ward took back-to-back victories, moving him into the thick of a close fight for the runner-up spot behind Palou. Lundgaard, Kirkwood and O’Ward are separated by just four points.

Palou will defend his latest championship title next year as the most senior driver in Ganassi’s line-up. His team mate, six-times champion Scott Dixon, who scored his last victory over a year ago at Mid-Ohio, will join O’Ward at McLaren.

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Expect a quiet ‘silly season’ after Verstappen deal | Brief
Sports.content:
Does Max Verstappen’s decision to stay at Red Bull mean we will see few changes in the driver market for next year and beyond?

It does probably mean that the drivers market is going to be stagnant in the top teams for the next four seasons potentially. No change at McLaren likely now, or Red Bull or Mercedes.

Okay, it’s quite likely Lewis will retire before 2030. But that still means we will have the same teams with the same driver line ups for 2026 to 2028 or 2029?

This may not add to the excitement of F1. A major team driver change always spices things up a bit.

Phil Norman (@Phil-f1-21)

Sports.title: Roberto Durán Outclasses Carlos Palomino at Madison Square Garden
Sports.content:
Palomino represented the right test. The former WBC welterweight champion had lost his title to Wilfred Benítez by split decision five months earlier and remained frustrated over not receiving a rematch. He believed Durán had looked soft in previous welterweight appearances, although the Panamanian arrived at the weigh-in looking sharp at 146 pounds. Palomino weighed 145.

Although the 7-5 favorite, Durán did not fight like a lightweight depending solely on aggression. He mixed pressure with feints, jabs, counters, and subtle changes of distance. His head and shoulders were rarely still, allowing him to slip punches without giving up his place inside the pocket.

That upper-body movement disrupted Palomino’s straight punches. Durán kept his head away from the center line, letting the jab pass before answering. At other times, he parried it with his rear hand or stepped inside with a right over the top. Palomino was accustomed to using the jab to set his rhythm, but Durán turned the punch into an opening for his own offense.

Speed soon became decisive. Palomino wanted to time Durán between combinations, yet his counters arrived too late. Durán could step in, finish his work, and change position before Palomino answered. He occasionally smiled, seemingly enjoying the freedom of competing without draining himself to 135 pounds.

Along the ropes, Durán’s work was just as measured. He did not waste energy throwing wide punches when Palomino covered up. He placed hooks into the ribs, brought short right uppercuts through the guard, and used his head and shoulders to keep Palomino from creating room.

Those clinches also answered questions about Durán’s ability to handle a natural welterweight. He did not try to overpower Palomino with muscular strength. Shoulder nudges, forearm leverage, and superior head position allowed him to turn his opponent or free one hand for short punches. His effectiveness there came from balance and technique, not size.

A right hand dropped Palomino early in the sixth round. Some accounts described the knockdown as the finish to a left-right combination, while others credited an overhand right to the chin. Palomino rose immediately and took referee Arthur Mercante’s mandatory eight-count. He survived despite cuts near his right eye and below his left ear.

The former champion produced his best work in the seventh, landing hooks at close range. Durán responded by sweeping the final three rounds. Freed from the severe lightweight cut, he maintained his pace and punch output through the tenth instead of slowing after building a large lead.

Palomino later said Durán’s hand and foot speed had surprised him. He also maintained that Durán thumbed him twice in the right eye during the inside exchanges, neither seen by Mercante.

Mercante and Harold Lederman each scored it 99-90, while Tony Castellano had it 99-91. The cards reflected Durán’s dominance. The contest was one-sided without becoming dull because he continued creating exchanges instead of protecting his advantage.

On HBO, promoter Don King placed the bout beneath Larry Holmes’ WBC heavyweight title defense against Mike Weaver. The card drew 14,136 spectators and a gate of $771,982, with many fans particularly interested in Durán against Palomino. After television networks and Madison Square Garden passed on Holmes-Weaver, King rented the building for $150,000. Durán and his manager reduced their original $250,000 guarantee to $100,000 against a later bill to help keep the promotion together.

Such a thorough victory established Durán as more than a dominant lightweight, carrying his reputation into a larger division. Palomino had been a world champion only months earlier and had never previously been handled in that fashion. Durán showed that his aggression worked because it was supported by defensive movement, timing, balance, and faster feet.

The performance also supplied an early version of the tactics Durán would use against Sugar Ray Leonard in Montreal the following year. Against both men, he slipped his way into punching range, interfered with their jabs, and used technical infighting to keep them from working comfortably. Palomino could not escape that attack. Leonard would later discover how difficult it was to impose his own rhythm once Durán dictated the terms.

Durán and Palomino embraced after the decision. Durán then appeared alone on the July 2, 1979, cover of Sports Illustrated, pictured in action against Palomino beneath the headline “Durán the Boxer.” Palomino retired shortly afterward, while Durán continued toward the defining welterweight victory of his career.

Sports.title: Andy Ruiz Jr. Races Toward Heavyweight Title Shot
Sports.content:
Under a three-fight agreement with Matchroom, Ruiz does not necessarily expect to complete the entire deal before challenging for a belt.

“It could take one fight. It could take two fights. I don’t know. God willing, just take this fight and then I’ll get to fight any of the champions,” Ruiz told Ariel Helwani.

Beating Knyba should not place Ruiz near the front of any championship line. Agit Kabayel stopped the 6’7” Polish heavyweight in three rounds, and Ruiz would merely be defeating someone who has already been exposed below the elite level.

Ruiz still has a reason to move quickly. Daniel Dubois and Filip Hrgovic represent the type of champions who would generate a major payday without presenting the commercial obstacles attached to the division’s biggest names. Neither man may hold his belt for long, leaving Ruiz with a limited period to turn his reputation into a lucrative championship opportunity.

A fight against Dubois or Hrgovic would also give Matchroom an immediate return on its investment. Ruiz can be sold as a former champion attempting one last run rather than spending several seasons rebuilding against modest opposition. His 2019 upset of Joshua remains valuable enough to market, even if his recent results do not warrant preferential treatment.

Winning a belt would serve another purpose. Ruiz has repeatedly expressed interest in a third fight with Joshua after splitting their first two meetings. Joshua has little competitive need to revisit a loss he decisively avenged, but Ruiz becoming champion would change the value of that matchup. A trilogy containing a heavyweight title would be easier to sell than one based almost entirely on memories of Madison Square Garden.

That possibility adds urgency to the Knyba fight. Ruiz does not simply need another win. He needs to look convincing enough for Matchroom to place him near Dubois, Hrgovic, or another champion before the available belts change hands.

The reunion with Manny Robles offers Ruiz a familiar selling point. Robles trained him for the first Joshua fight, when his compact combinations, quick hands, and ability to close distance produced the defining performance of his career. Six years later, a trainer cannot restore lost activity or guarantee that Ruiz still possesses the same physical tools.

Questions also remain about his durability. Chris Arreola dropped Ruiz hard in 2021, while Miller’s constant pressure forced him into a draining fight three years later. Ruiz broke his hand during that draw and eventually required surgery. Elite heavyweights will test that hand, force him to maintain a higher output, and find out how much punishment he can still absorb.

A traditional rebuilding process would consume much of Ruiz’s remaining career. Taking three or four fights to restore his ranking may require another year or longer. Yet the championship queue contains younger contenders who have remained active and beaten better opposition. Mandatory defenses and existing title obligations leave little justification for Ruiz jumping ahead of them.

That explains the hurry, but it does not make Knyba a title eliminator. Ruiz first needs to show that his hand is healthy, his conditioning holds up, and the return to Robles has produced more than another temporary burst of discipline. His name may shorten the climb, but defeating Knyba would not prove he belongs with the division’s best.

Sports.title: Abel Sanchez Says Hrgovic Needed Knockout Against Itauma
Sports.content:
“We weren’t going to win a decision. I don’t care how close the fight was; we were not going to win a decision because boxing has a tendency to do what’s best for boxing financially. I expected to be down. I expected not to win any rounds. I expected Filip to be the 9-to-1 or 8-to-1 underdog. I expected all that, but it was a 12-round fight, and we were going to capitalize on it being a 12-round fight,” Sanchez said to Fight Hub TV.

The crowd made Itauma’s advantage feel wider than it was. Every clean punch brought a loud reaction, while much of Hrgovic’s quieter work passed without the same recognition. Itauma deserved the rounds, but the applause created the impression that he was dominating a fighter who remained competitive and began coming on from the sixth.

Sanchez’s expectation of trailing on the scorecards shaped the tactics. Chasing rounds would have forced Hrgovic to trade combinations with the faster southpaw, giving Itauma the explosive exchanges he wanted. Sanchez instead repeatedly told Hrgovic to make Itauma initiate the action and spend energy closing the distance.

The difference in efficiency became decisive. Itauma threw fast four- and five-punch combinations, while Hrgovic answered with measured jabs and absorbed much of the incoming work on his gloves, arms and shoulders. Even when Itauma scored, he was paying a far greater physical price for each exchange.

A jab did not have to dominate every sequence. Its purpose was to interrupt Itauma’s approach, force another setup and prevent him from planting his feet comfortably. Every reset required the younger fighter to begin again.

That pattern also changed the use of space. Itauma controlled the center initially while Hrgovic willingly gave ground. Once Itauma’s output dropped, the older heavyweight began advancing more consistently. Areas that had provided Itauma room to attack and leave gradually became places where Hrgovic could hold him under pressure.

Abel compared the bout to taking Andy Ruiz Jr. to New Zealand for his 2016 fight with Joseph Parker. He told Ruiz they were already three points behind before boarding the plane. The trip reinforced why he could not depend on favorable scoring when his fighter was facing the home attraction.

The judges became irrelevant when Hrgovic stopped Itauma in the ninth round. Sanchez’s prediction that his fighter would trail was understandable because Itauma had legitimately won most of the earlier rounds. What the scorecards could not show was the changing direction of the fight. Hrgovic was allowing Itauma to spend himself while waiting for the portion only one of them had been prepared to handle.

Sports.title: Frank Sanchez Deserves His Shot at Filip Hrgovic
Sports.content:
Sanchez stepped aside with a guaranteed shot at the winner. Now Hrgovic wants unification fights against Agit Kabayel or Daniel Dubois, with another payment offered as the solution. Sky Sports confirmed Sanchez’s guarantee before the fight.

“Frank Sanchez will wait, get another step-aside, make money without fighting and everyone’s happy,” Hrgovic said after his victory, as quoted by The Ring.

Everyone being happy is Hrgovic’s interpretation. A payment compensates Sanchez for a delay. It does not give him the championship or the earning power that comes with winning it.

There is a competitive cost, too. Waiting without fighting offers no opportunity to sharpen distance judgment and counterpunch timing under pressure. Taking an interim bout carries its own risks: an injury or defeat can damage his claim. Neither option makes a postponement harmless.

His style also gives this defense sporting value. Against Efe Ajagba, Sanchez used movement and quick counters to frustrate a bigger puncher rather than trading on his opponent’s terms. PBC’s fight report documents that performance.

Applied against Hrgovic, that approach would test the champion’s ability to close distance, establish his jab and create exchanges. He cannot build a strategy around Sanchez exhausting himself the way Itauma did. A patient opponent willing to score and move presents a different task from surviving an early assault.

That does not make Sanchez tougher than Kabayel or Dubois. Limited commercial appeal is still a poor reason to dismiss him as an opponent.

The IBF has a role beyond approving whatever deal generates the largest purse. In 2023, it stripped Terence Crawford after his contractual rematch obligation to Errol Spence Jr. prevented a mandatory defense against Jaron Ennis. That was a rematch dispute, not a unification request, so it does not settle Hrgovic’s case. The decision nevertheless demonstrates that commercial plans need not override a challenger’s position. ESPN’s report explains the decision.

The appeal of another belt is understandable. Hrgovic wants to maximize his remaining years, but Sanchez’s career clock is running as well. Further delays leave him dependent on other fighters’ results, recovery periods and negotiations.

There is nothing wrong with voluntarily accepting an offer he considers worthwhile. The choice, however, should remain his. Insisting on the promised fight would not make him an obstruction to heavyweight unification.

Hrgovic deserves credit for beating Itauma. Sanchez deserves the opportunity that was agreed upon before the winner was known.

Sports.title: Oleksandr Usyk Targets Deontay Wilder for Late Career Victory Lap
Sports.content:
The historical attraction is easy to understand. Having beaten Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua twice each, Usyk can complete his collection of victories over the three heavyweight names that dominated discussion before his arrival in the division.

But the date belongs alongside the name. Defeating Wilder in 2027 would not carry the significance of beating him during his WBC championship reign. Completing that list gives promoters a neat career retrospective without necessarily adding much to Usyk’s strongest accomplishments.

Wilder brings recognition and a right hand that supplies the promotional clips. His defeats against Joseph Parker and Zhilei Zhang exposed the weakness in relying on one decisive punch. Parker denied him clean opportunities, while Zhang punished his hesitation.

Against Usyk, he would struggle to find room to set his feet and throw that right hand. The southpaw changes angles, draws reactions with feints and makes opponents adjust before they can punch. Wilder must process those changes before committing.

That is where his reduced output becomes especially costly. Waiting for a clear target allows Usyk to score and leave. Throwing without properly setting the attack risks missing, losing balance, and taking counters. Wilder needs to create openings with his jab and positioning rather than spend rounds hoping one arrives.

Age offers the strongest qualification to that prediction. Usyk would be 40 by the proposed March date. His movement depends on repeated small adjustments, and any decline in his legs might leave him within reach for longer.

Yet a slower Usyk would still require Wilder to recognize those opportunities and act immediately. Punching power cannot compensate for an opening noticed too late. The American’s chance depends as much on his willingness to throw as on the force behind the shot.

Taking the event to the United States offers a commercial explanation. Wilder supplies a familiar home fighter, while Usyk gets another opportunity to headline there. That familiarity may help attract attention, but converting it into ticket purchases requires convincing buyers that the contest remains competitive.

Lapin has discussed Zuffa as a potential partner, without confirming an agreement. Those talks do not establish who will finance the event, and an American venue does not rule out Saudi involvement. Boxing Insider

A broadcaster or promoter may pay for the names. Fans would still be buying the versions who enter the ring in 2027.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Must Fire Ben Davison After Filip Hrgovic Disaster
Sports.content:
Davison failed his fighter in two critical areas.

First, the physical conditioning was inadequate for a twelve-round championship fight. You cannot put a twenty-one-year-old puncher in against a seasoned heavyweight without building an elite gas tank. Itauma trains inside a comfortable camp, but he clearly lacked the gritty cardiovascular foundation required for a war.

Second, the corner work was nonexistent when the crisis hit. When a young fighter starts burning energy throwing every shot with bad intentions, the coach must pull back the reins. Davison should have instructed Moses to establish the jab, circle the ring, and take full minutes off to recover his breath. Instead, Davison watched his fighter empty his arsenal into Hrgovic’s iron chin. There were no technical adjustments, no tactical wisdom, zero control over the pace.

Promoter Frank Warren knows how to rescue promising careers after devastating defeats. He rebuilt Daniel Dubois; he will do the same here. But the first move must be immediate and decisive.

Moses Itauma needs to cut ties with Ben Davison today. The ideal replacement is Abel Sanchez, the veteran coach who stood across the ring orchestrating Hrgovic’s victory. Sanchez knew Itauma would blow his engine. He told Hrgovic to stay calm, absorb the early barrage, take over the moment the youngster started gasping for air.

Sanchez would take Itauma up to Big Bear, strip away the hype, build an engine capable of throwing punches all night. Moses has unbelievable hand speed, exceptional natural gifts. What he lacks is an old school trainer who demands relentless discipline.

Someone has to take responsibility for the disaster against Hrgovic. Itauma paid the price with his unbeaten record inside the ring. Davison needs to pay the price with his job.

Sports.title: Daniel Dubois Calls Wardley Win Dominant Despite Knockdowns
Sports.content:
“Of course, another dominant victory and, you know, amazing performance. I can’t wait,” Dubois said during the ring announcement. When reminded of the knockdowns in rounds one and three, he replied: “When you get in the water, you’re going to get wet.”

Getting dropped is an expensive version of getting wet. Treating those early rounds as an unavoidable part of the contest risks overlooking openings Wardley can exploit again.

Establishing his jab immediately would allow Dubois to apply pressure while making the challenger work harder to reach him. Walking into punching range without occupying Wardley’s gloves leaves him relying on his chin before his own heavier work has taken effect.

A body attack offers another investment in the later rounds. Wardley needs his legs underneath him to launch explosive attacks and get clear afterward. Making him defend downstairs would also divide his attention, creating opportunities for Dubois to bring the right hand upstairs.

The challenger’s adjustment starts with what happens after he lands something big.

A knockdown creates urgency, but it also gives the hurt fighter a count to recover. Wardley cannot assume Dubois will be as vulnerable when the action resumes as he was when he fell. Measuring the next attack behind a jab, using shorter combinations and leaving enough energy to defend would help him maintain control.

Loading up on every right hand risks spending that advantage. Wide punches give a recovering opponent chances to duck, hold or answer through the middle. Wardley needs accurate follow-up work more than greater effort.

Getting out safely is just as vital. After throwing a lead hook, bringing his glove back and moving his head off the center line would reduce the opening for a straight right counter. Hurting Dubois does not make the return fire harmless.

Wardley cited the changes between his two Frazer Clarke fights and his performances against Justis Huni and Joseph Parker as evidence that he can adapt. That confidence now faces a tougher test: correcting his mistakes against the man who punished them.

There is also only about five months between the fights. That interval alone tells us nothing definite about his recovery, but the punishment from an eleven-round stoppage adds weight to the need for better defense.

Dubois has proved he can survive a dangerous start. Wardley needs a plan that still works when the early knockout doesn’t come.

Sports.title: James Toney vs. Mike McCallum: Closer Than the Cards
Sports.content:
Their first meeting had ended in a draw eight months earlier. Between the two, Toney survived a heavily disputed decision against Dave Tiberi. Beating McCallum offered a chance to put a better performance beside that damaging result. At 35, the challenger still had the technique to make the younger champion work for his openings.

McCallum’s jab and body punching gave him a way to compete without matching Toney’s hand speed. Working downstairs reduced his dependence on finding a head that was constantly slipping or rolling away. His persistence also made Toney pay for stretches when he waited to counter.

Fighting at close range carried its own risk. Getting near Toney did not take McCallum safely past the champion’s offense. Short counters remained available at distances where a wider punch needed too much room. The tactical challenge was to attack the body without staying exposed afterward. Neither man had the luxury of treating the inside as a place to rest.

The champion’s case rested on the quality of his replies. His harder, sharper punches drew attention, and rewarding those shots was reasonable. The difficulty came in deciding how much of a round a brief successful attack should outweigh. McCallum kept collecting scoring punches between those bursts.

Defensive economy was useful only up to a point. Catching a punch on the gloves saved Toney from taking it cleanly, but a successful block did not score for him. McCallum’s steady output forced the judges to distinguish between successful defense and actually winning an exchange. Looking comfortable under pressure was not enough by itself.

Punch totals illustrate the dispute without settling it. McCallum was credited with 332 landed punches to Toney’s 232. Those numbers do not measure impact or tell us who won each round. They do, however, challenge any easy description of the challenger being comprehensively outboxed. A fighter can land more across twelve rounds and still lose, but his contribution deserves to be judged beyond the most memorable counter.

Joe Cortez deducted a point from McCallum in the eighth for hitting behind Toney’s back while holding him in a headlock. The penalty widened the deficit; it did not determine the winner. Removing it still leaves Toney ahead on two cards. The real argument concerns how those judges distributed the rounds.

Trainer Eddie Futch treated the closing rounds as essential, telling McCallum: “It’s very close, Mike. You’ve got to get the next round.” That instruction fits the competitive fight far better than the eventual margins. It also underlines the danger of leaving close rounds to the judges: each corner can see opportunities that the scorecards have already denied.

Toney deserved credit for beating an opponent whose skill survived the difference in age. Yet treating the result as a rout diminishes the achievement. McCallum forced him to solve a difficult fight, and a narrow Toney victory is a much easier argument to defend than seven points of separation.

Ghana News.title: UMB becomes first bank approved by BoG and SEC to offer virtual accounts
Ghana News.content:
Universal Merchant Bank (UMB) has become the first bank in Ghana to receive approval from both the Bank of Ghana (BoG) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to offer virtual accounts to eligible businesses operating within the emerging virtual asset ecosystem.

The approval marks a significant step in Ghana’s evolving financial landscape, where regulated banking, digital finance and new technology-driven business models are increasingly converging.

For UMB, however, the significance extends beyond the introduction of a new banking capability. It reflects a deliberate strategy to identify emerging opportunities, build the infrastructure required to serve them and work with regulators to ensure that innovation develops within a sound and sustainable regulatory framework.

The development comes as Ghana strengthens its regulatory architecture for virtual assets and virtual asset service providers (VASPs), providing greater clarity on how businesses in the sector can participate in the formal financial system.

Positioning UMB at the front of Ghana’s digital economy

The global virtual asset industry continues to evolve, driven by developments in blockchain technology, digital payments, tokenisation and broader financial innovation.

Ghana is responding to these developments with a more structured regulatory approach to create space for innovation while safeguarding the integrity and stability of the financial system.

Mensah Thompson, Acting Deputy Director-General Finance at the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), emphasised the importance of responsible participation by financial institutions as the sector develops.

“As the virtual asset ecosystem develops, collaboration between regulators and financial institutions will be important in ensuring that innovation takes place within a properly regulated environment.

"Institutions that are prepared to understand the requirements and build the appropriate controls will be well positioned to support the development of the sector.”

Against this backdrop, UMB’s dual regulatory approval gives the Bank an early position from which to engage eligible virtual asset businesses, Fintechs, technology companies and other participants seeking access to regulated banking infrastructure.

The virtual account offering remains subject to applicable regulatory requirements and eligibility criteria.

The approval nonetheless establishes an important foundation for UMB to participate in the development of Ghana’s emerging virtual asset market and to support businesses operating within the formal financial system.

Banking for What Comes Next

For UMB Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Dr Philip Oti-Mensah, the development aligns with the Bank’s broader ambition to anticipate evolving customer and market needs.

“The financial services landscape is evolving, and our responsibility as a bank is to understand where our customers and the economy are heading and build the capabilities to support that future.

Receiving approval from both the Bank of Ghana and the Securities and Exchange Commission to offer virtual accounts to eligible businesses is an important milestone for UMB.

It demonstrates that innovation and responsible banking can move together, and reinforces our commitment to building a modern, relevant and competitive Ghanaian bank.”

Since assuming leadership of UMB, Dr Oti-Mensah has placed transformation, innovation, customer experience and sustainable growth at the centre of the Bank’s agenda.

The virtual account approval reflects that direction in practice: identifying an emerging market early, developing the necessary banking capabilities and working within the regulatory framework to create opportunities for the Bank and its customers.

Digital Capability as a Business Strategy

UMB’s move into the virtual asset ecosystem builds on wider investments in digital banking and technology.

Through platforms such as SpeedApp and internet banking, and products such as Legacy Care Plus, the Bank has continued to expand the ways customers and businesses interact with its services.

For Tubuor Ofei-Agyemang, Head of E-Business at UMB, the virtual account capability is part of this broader digital evolution.

“Digital transformation is no longer simply about moving existing banking services onto digital platforms. It is about understanding how customers and businesses are evolving and developing the infrastructure to support them.

"The virtual account capability is part of that journey and reflects our focus on building secure, scalable and relevant digital banking solutions.”

The strategy increasingly positions technology not simply as a channel for delivering conventional banking services, but as an enabler of new forms of business and financial activity.

The virtual account approval extends that approach into an emerging segment of Ghana’s digital economy, giving UMB an opportunity to develop solutions around businesses whose financial needs are evolving alongside the regulatory landscape.

A Stronger Platform for Growth

The approval also comes at an important point in UMB’s institutional journey.

In July 2026, Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson announced the completion of the Ghana Amalgamated Trust’s full recapitalisation of Universal Merchant Bank, strengthening the Bank’s capital position and providing a stronger platform for its next phase of growth.

Combined with continued investment in technology, customer experience and operational capabilities, the recapitalisation strengthens the foundation from which UMB can pursue new opportunities and respond to emerging areas of economic activity.

The Bank is therefore entering Ghana’s evolving virtual asset space with growing institutional, financial and technological capacity.

More Than Being First

UMB’s position as the first bank in Ghana approved by both the Bank of Ghana and the Securities and Exchange Commission to offer virtual accounts is significant. But the greater opportunity lies in what that position enables.

As Ghana’s virtual asset regulatory framework develops, regulated financial institutions will play an important role in connecting legitimate businesses in the digital economy to the formal financial system.

That creates potential for deeper collaboration across banking, fintech, payments, technology and virtual asset businesses, while allowing financial institutions to develop expertise in a rapidly changing market.

For UMB, being early is therefore about more than just claiming first place. It creates an opportunity to understand the sector, build relationships, develop institutional expertise and design solutions for businesses operating within a clearly defined regulatory environment.

It is also consistent with the Bank’s wider transformation agenda: anticipate change, invest ahead of the curve and build banking solutions around where customers and the economy are heading.

As Ghana’s financial ecosystem continues to evolve, UMB is positioning itself not simply to participate in that transformation, but to help build the financial infrastructure that enables it.

Ghana News.title: Maximus Attah writes: Vacancies that never hire
Ghana News.content:
Behind the polished job s crowding Ghana's newspapers and news sites lies a quieter, more cynical machine — one that exists not to hire, but to be seen to have tried.

You have felt it before. The  reads as if it were written for you; the qualifications, the experience, the tone of the role; as though someone had studied your CV before drafting the job description. You apply. You wait. You refresh your inbox the way a farmer studies the sky in a dry season.

And then: nothing. Not a rejection. Not an acknowledgment. Just silence, stretching into weeks, then months, then a quiet understanding that the silence itself is the answer.

In Ghana, this is not misfortune. It is design.

Talk to enough job seekers; the fresh graduate, the mid-career professional, the returnee with a foreign degree and a folder full of certificates and a pattern emerges with the regularity of a national ritual.

Adverts appear in the newspapers and on recruitment sites, dressed in the full formal language of merit: “equal opportunity employer,” “only shortlisted candidates will be contacted,” “apply before the deadline.” The language promises a fair contest. The outcome, more often than the country cares to admit, was decided before the advert ever went to print.

A Ritual of Appearances

Ghana’s procurement law offers an unflattering mirror for what happens in recruitment. Just as public contracts are sometimes advertised only to satisfy a legal requirement; the winner already chosen the bidding process a formality staged for the record; so too are many job vacancies.

The  is not an invitation. It is an alibi. It exists so that, if ever questioned, an institution can point to the newspaper clipping and say: we advertised. We followed the process. The fact that no outsider ever stood a real chance is beside the point; the appearance of fairness has been manufactured, and that is all the exercise was designed to produce.

“It was impossible to secure employment there without the right connections. You had to know someone who knew someone who knew someone.”

Consider the case of a once prominent, privately owned Ghanaian bank – a household name until its collapse in 2019. Long before the crisis that ended it, friends inside the institution, people with no reason to lie, described a workplace where merit was theatre and connections were currency.

One expatriate employee, who resigned before the walls came down, put it more bluntly still: the bank was thriving on cronyism. And yet, month after month, its middle- and top-level positions appeared in the Ghanaian press, complete with deadlines and application instructions, as though the outcome were genuinely in question.

Apply, and you would learn otherwise. Not through a rejection letter, those rarely came, but through the silence that has become its own genre of Ghanaian correspondence.

The Email that Bounced

Sometimes the theatre is not even convincing enough to hide its own seams. A major Ghanaian company once advertised a set of top-level positions, directing applicants to submit their materials through a stated email address. Among those applicants was this writer, whose profile fit one of the vacancies closely enough to justify the effort of applying.

The application pack was assembled, checked, and sent. It bounced. It was sent again. It bounced again. Every attempt returned, undelivered, as if the position existed only in the  and nowhere else.

A contact inside the company eventually made a call on the applicant’s behalf, reaching the human resource department directly. The explanation offered was almost disarming in its casualness: the email address had contained an error; the company would readvertise with the correct one; interested applicants could try again.

And with that, the matter closed. No re followed. No correction was published. The vacancy simply evaporated, having done whatever quiet work it was placed there to do.

Who is Really Being Hired?

It is worth asking the question more Ghanaians ask only in private: how do the country’s major corporations actually source their staff? Not through the recruitment agencies and human resource consultancies that exist precisely for this purpose; most vacancies, tellingly, never reach them. Not through the open, searchable channels the adverts imply.

The honest answer, uncomfortable as it is, is that a great many positions in Ghana are filled the way they have always been filled: through relationships, referrals, and the informal architecture of who-knows-whom that predates any  and will outlast it.

The public notice, in this arrangement, is not a search. It is a formality, a piece of institutional theatre performed for regulators, for boards, for the appearance of due process, and, not least, for a labour market hungry enough to keep applying regardless of the odds.

A Country’s Quiet Complicity

None of this is a secret. It is, if anything, an open secret – the kind everyone half-knows and no one is required to admit. Job seekers whisper about it in queues and WhatsApp groups. Human resource officers acknowledge it, off the record, with the resigned shrug of people executing a script written above their pay grade. Employers rarely deny it outright; they simply decline to discuss it.

What is missing is the discomfort that should accompany an open secret this corrosive. Every fake vacancy is a small tax on hope, levied against people who can least afford it, young graduates burning through printing money and transport fares to chase openings that were never open, professionals sacrificing the goodwill of current employers to pursue opportunities elsewhere that do not, in truth, exist. Multiply that by the scale of Ghana’s job market, and the fake vacancy stops being an inconvenience and becomes something closer to a structural drain on the country’s most valuable resource: the ambition of its young people.

An Overdue Reckoning

To the recruiters and hiring managers who know exactly what they are doing when they place these s: the desperation of Ghana’s young jobseekers is not raw material to be spent on paperwork. If a preferred candidate already awaits behind the scenes, say so, or better still, stop pretending that a public search is underway when it is not.

The dignity of the process matters as much as its outcome, and Ghana’s employers, public and private alike, owe their applicants at least that much honesty.

Until then, the vacancies will keep appearing, polished, plausible, and, for a very particular kind of Ghanaian jobseeker, entirely beside the point.

Ghana News.title: ‘When the time comes, I will speak’ – Kurt on third-term GFA presidential bid
Ghana News.content:
Ghana Football Association president Kurt Okraku has refused to reveal whether he will seek a third term in office when the next elections are held in 2027.

The GFA approved an amendment to its statutes allowing presidents to serve for up to three terms.

The amendment was done in 2025 after 114 of the 124 members present at their General Assembly voted in favour.

Kurt took over as GFA president in 2019 following the work of the Normalisation Committee.

He secured a second term in 2023 without facing competition after aspirant George Afriyie was disqualified by the Election Committee.

When asked whether he would contest for a third term, Okraku told 3Sports: “I don't know.”

“We have close to 18 months before an elective General Assembly.

“There is a lot of work to be done. I want to concentrate on my tenure as the President and see how best we can reposition our football.

“When the time comes, I will speak. When the time comes, the football family will speak.

“At the end, I can't never stay here forever and I do not intend to stay here forever. When the time is due, Kurt will fly away.”

Reports have also linked former Black Stars captain Andre Ayew with a potential bid for the GFA presidency.

The next GFA presidential and Executive Council elections are scheduled to take place in 2027.

Ghana News.title: UMB S.P.E.E.D. Stars lift Bankers Football Gala trophy
Ghana News.content:
Universal Merchant Bank’s S.P.E.E.D. Stars are champions of the 2026 Bankers Football Gala, topping a field of eight banks after a campaign built on discipline, composure and a refusal to blink under pressure.

The title was sealed on Saturday, August 29, 2026, capping a tournament that tested every team in Ghana's banking sector — and left UMB standing at the top.

Across the competition, the UMB S.P.E.E.D. Stars found their edge in the moments that mattered: holding their shape when games tightened, staying patient through knockout pressure, and pulling together as a unit when it counted most.

That composure carried them past strong competition from rival banks and into the final reckoning as champions.

"Grit, teamwork and the UMB spirit" — that's how the Bank summed up the run, and it's hard to argue with a trophy as the evidence.

More than a trophy

The Gala is billed as a platform for camaraderie and healthy competition across the financial sector, but for UMB, the win lands as something bigger: proof that the values it champions in the workplace — discipline, collaboration, resilience — translate directly onto the pitch.

It's also the latest marker in a year where football has become a genuine strategic thread for the Bank. In May 2026, UMB signed a three-year partnership with the Ghana Football Association, backing the national teams, domestic competitions, women's football and youth development.

The Gala title now sits alongside that commitment as further evidence that the bank isn't just sponsoring the game from a distance — it's playing it too.

For the S.P.E.E.D. Stars, Saturday was a victory earned point by point. For UMB, it's a reminder that the same spirit driving its people at work is just as alive on the pitch — and that the Bank's investment in football, from grassroots to gala day, continues to pay off.

Ghana News.title: MMFL makes strong showing at JoySports Invitational 2026
Ghana News.content:
MobileMoney Fintech Limited (MMFL) joined 33 other companies and institutions at the 2026 JoySports Invitational Tournament, as Corporate Ghana traded boardrooms for sporting competition at the University of Ghana Sports Stadium on Saturday, August 29.

The annual corporate sporting fiesta brought together executives, employees and sports enthusiasts for a day of competition, networking and camaraderie.

MMFL participated in a number of disciplines, including football, table tennis, lawn tennis, ladies’ penalty shoot-out, unisex sack race, Tug of Peace, Lime and Spoon Relay and the CEO’s penalty shoot-out.

The company’s participation provided employees with an opportunity to strengthen teamwork and interact with clients and customers in a relaxed environment.

Speaking to the media, Mrs Dzifa Romano Mensah, Head of Human Resources at MMFL, said the company was delighted to be part of the event.

“We are very excited to be part of the JoySports Invitational. These tournaments bring us closer to our clients and customers while also allowing our employees to bond and promote healthy living.

"We will compete fairly, but in the disciplines where we have the advantage, we will definitely be looking to win,” she said.

The event began with a health walk at 6 a.m., followed by aerobics and a series of competitive and recreational activities, including football, swimming, table tennis, chess, Scrabble, Ludo, draughts and novelty events.

Ayawaso West Wuogon MP John Dumelo was among the notable personalities who attended the event.

At the time of going to press, Piwak Natural Health had won the football competition after beating McDan 2-0 in the final, bringing another successful edition of the JoySports Invitational to a close.

For MMFL, the tournament offered more than competition—it was an opportunity to build stronger teams, deepen relationships and celebrate the spirit of healthy competition.

Ghana News.title: MTN Media Republic, Ghana Wildlife Society embark on bird, butterfly walk
Ghana News.content:
The MTN Media Republic, in collaboration with the Ghana Wildlife Society (GWS), has organised a bird and butterfly walk at the Legon Botanical Gardens as part of efforts to promote environmental sustainability and appreciation of nature.

The exercise, held on Saturday, August 29, brought together media practitioners and environmental enthusiasts for an educative, interactive and refreshing experience aimed at deepening participants’ understanding of biodiversity and the need to protect the environment.

The walk was led by the Executive Director of the Ghana Wildlife Society, Dr Sandra Owusu-Gyamfi, who urged Ghanaians to reduce their reliance on plastics and explore environmentally friendly alternatives in their homes, offices and other public spaces.

She cautioned that plastic waste, particularly microplastics, poses a serious threat to marine life and the wider ecosystem, stressing the need for individuals, businesses and institutions to take deliberate steps to reduce plastic pollution.

Dr Owusu-Gyamfi also highlighted the importance of birds as unique creations, noting that their freedom and way of life offer valuable lessons to humans about nature and peaceful coexistence.

She encouraged participants to develop a deeper appreciation for birds and other wildlife, saying protecting biodiversity was a shared responsibility.

Acting General Manager of Sustainability at MTN, Mrs Georgina Asare Fiagbenu, said the exercise formed part of the company’s Sustainability Month activities, describing the experience as an opportunity to reconnect with nature and strengthen relationships among colleagues and media partners.

She expressed gratitude for the support for the initiative, saying the experience of breathing in the fresh air, listening to the chirping and singing of birds, and simply being surrounded by nature was refreshing and therapeutic.

“The feeling is healing, and we feel good doing small actions to create big impact,” she said.

Mrs Fiagbenu said the walk provided a valuable opportunity for participants to reconnect not only with nature but also with one another.

She explained that MTN was putting sustainability into practice through initiatives such as installing solar panels to generate electricity at its offices and at MTN House, as well as waste-recycling programmes supported by strong governance and ethical standards.

She expressed appreciation to the media community for participating in the exercise and said MTN looked forward to more initiatives that would promote sustainability, wellbeing and positive impact in society.

Senior Manager of Corporate Communications at MTN, Ms Efua Falconer, said the company, as an innovative organisation, continued to keep pace with emerging trends and developments.

She said MTN also wanted its media partners to remain abreast of such developments and share in initiatives that promoted sustainability and responsible environmental practices.

Ms Falconer noted that bringing media practitioners into such experiences was important because it created opportunities for them to better understand and appreciate the sustainability agenda and the role of businesses in protecting the environment.

President of the MTN Media Republic, Naa Dzagble Ago Quaye, commended members who turned up for the exercise, describing it as educative, interactive, exotic, inspiring and physically beneficial.

She said the experience provided members with an opportunity to step away from their usual routines, connect with nature and gain a deeper understanding of the importance of protecting Ghana’s rich biodiversity.

The bird and butterfly walk offered participants an opportunity to observe different species in their natural surroundings while learning about the importance of conservation and responsible environmental practices.

The initiative also strengthened the bond between MTN and members of the media community, providing a relaxed environment for networking, interaction and shared learning.

The organisers expressed optimism that the experience would inspire participants to adopt more environmentally responsible practices and become advocates for the protection of Ghana’s natural environment.

Ghana News.title: Fuel Prices: Star Oil holds petrol at GH¢14.97, raises diesel to GH¢16.97
Ghana News.content:
Some Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs) have begun reviewing fuel prices at the pumps from Tuesday, September 1, 2026, with Star Oil leading the latest adjustments.

Star Oil has maintained the price of petrol at GH¢14.97 per litre. However, the company has increased the price of diesel from GH¢16.47 to GH¢16.97 per litre.

JOY BUSINESS understands that other OMCs are expected to review their prices during the day.

While some companies are preparing to adjust prices, others are monitoring competition before making a decision.

There are more than 200 OMCs operating in Ghana, with companies expected to take different approaches to the latest market developments.

Reasons

The Chamber of Oil Marketing Companies (COMAC) attributed the expected price adjustments to rising crude oil prices and higher prices of finished petroleum products on the international market.

According to COMAC, crude oil prices increased by 1.75%, from US$90.53 per barrel to US$92.11 per barrel.

Finished petroleum products also recorded increases. Petrol prices rose by 8.86%, diesel by 5.51% and LPG by 3.31%.

COMAC said the increases came despite the cedi’s appreciation against the US dollar.

The cedi appreciated by 3.64% to GH¢11.3697 to the dollar, based on average bank rates between August 12 and 27, 2026.

The appreciation reversed three consecutive depreciation windows and reached the cedi’s strongest level since June 2026.

Despite the stronger cedi, rising international crude and refined product prices are expected to put upward pressure on fuel prices.

Government Subsidy

JOY BUSINESS checks indicate that diesel prices could have been higher without government intervention.

A government source told JOY BUSINESS that the government has extended its GH¢2-per-litre reduction in the regulatory margin on diesel into the first pricing window of September.

The intervention is intended to cushion consumers against the impact of rising international fuel prices.

Ghana News.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak surges past 6000 cases as death toll nears 3000
Ghana News.content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo faces the fastest-growing Ebola epidemic in recorded history. Official figures released Monday confirm more than 6,000 cases and 2,911 deaths. Health authorities noted a small positive sign amid the crisis. More than 1,360 people have successfully recovered from the virus.

Deep Roots of Insecurity and Displacement

Eastern Congo provides fertile ground for the epidemic to spread rapidly. Armed conflict, mass displacement, and population movements hinder containment efforts. A concurrent strike by local health workers compounds the crisis. Displacement sites present the most acute danger due to severely precarious living conditions. The virus recently breached two additional health zones in the region.

Global Health Alarm

The World Health Organisation warns the outbreak remains entirely out of control. Current transmission trajectories threaten to surpass the devastating 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic. That disaster claimed over 11,000 lives across Guinea, Liberia, and Sierra Leone. Officials trace the current contagion back to February, despite formal declarations arriving in May. The virus has now crossed from three initial zones into nearly 60 areas. Most infections and fatalities occur inside local communities rather than monitored contact networks.

Frontline Violence and Burial Tensions

Response teams face immense hostility while attempting to contain the spread. Armed assailants recently stormed an Ebola burial site outside Mambasa in Ituri province. Attackers wielding machetes injured one response worker and forced the entire team to scatter. Floribert Magene addressed the constant threat of violence faced by medical personnel. "We demand greater security so we can operate in the field and do our work without endangering our lives," said Floribert Magene, a member of the response team. Traditional funeral practices complicate containment because deceased victims remain highly contagious. Authorities mandate state-managed burials for suspected cases to prevent transmission. These protocols frequently spark friction and protests from grieving families and communities.

Treatment Gaps and Experimental Defences

The current epidemic stems from the Bundibugyo strain, a rare viral type lacking approved treatments or vaccines. Officials launched a vaccination campaign last week targeting health workers and front-line staff. This campaign utilises the Ervebo vaccine, proven effective against the distinct Zaire strain. Clinical trials continue in an urgent race to secure a licensed vaccine for the Bundibugyo variant.

Broader Regional Fallout

Emergency containment measures paralyse daily life across six affected provinces. Restrictions target public gatherings, enforce social distancing, and mandate airport closures. Ituri province bears a double burden from both the epidemic and persistent rebel violence. Advocacy groups urge authorities to deepen community engagement and build local trust. Meanwhile, the World Health Organisation warns that cross-border transmission risks persist despite neighbouring Uganda declaring itself Ebola-free last month.

Humanitarian Crossroads

Balancing immediate epidemiological containment with enduring community trust remains the central challenge for international health bodies and local administrations alike.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
