World.title: Orlando Pirates vs La Cure Waves: CAF Champions League first round preview
World.content:
Orlando Pirates open their CAF Champions League campaign on 5 September 2026 in Mauritius. Image: Wikimedia Commons

Orlando Pirates will kick off their 2026/27 CAF Champions League campaign this weekend with an “easy” match – on paper at least.

The Buccaneers face Mauritius champions La Cure Waves in the first-leg of the first preliminary round on Sunday, 6 September.

Kick-off at the Côte d’Or National Sports Complex in St Pierre, Mauritius is at 13:30 (SA time).



While the Soweto giants are expected to dominate, their path to the main tournament will only get trickier from here.

Here’s what you need to know ahead of Orlando Pirates’ clash this weekend.

Why must Orlando Pirates go through CAF Champions League qualifying?

The Confederation of African Football (CAF) Champions League and Confederation Cup utilise club rankings to place (seed) teams.



According to this ranking, Orlando Pirates were listed as 19th on the continent.

This means the reigning South African champions still need to earn their spot in the CAF CL group stage.

Mamelodi Sundowns, who dominated the PSL until last season, received a bye into the second preliminary round.



Esperance de Tunis and RS Berkane will also bypass the first preliminary round, according to the CAF website.

Who are La Cure Waves?

La Cure Waves, who are based in Port Louis, are making their first appearance in the CAF CL, after winning their first Mauritian National Super League title in 2025/26.

They also won a pre-season cup, facing the country’s under-20 side and fellow league club AS Port-Louis 2000.



One of the comparisons has been the preparation gap between the clubs.

Mauritius’s league only returns in November, meaning La Cure Waves have not faced truly strong opposition in some time.

While anything can happen, Orlando Pirates are overwhelming favourites to win on Sunday, and again at the Orlando Amstel Arena next Saturday, 12 September in the second leg (15:00).



Orlando Pirates need to balance squad rotation

Squad management will be crucial for coach Abdeslam Ouaddou.

He will need to rotate his players effectively to keep the team fresh and to maintain Orlando Pirates’ domestic ambitions.

Fortunately, the Buccaneers have been strengthened during the transfer window, with 10 new signings confirmed.



The biggest questions for Orlando Pirates should come in the second CAF Champions League preliminary round.

If the team advances, as expected, they will face either AS Mangasport of Gabon or African Stars of Namibia.

Both of those teams will provide a much stiffer challenge.



AS Mangasport have won the country’s Championnat National D1 10 times since 2000, having defended the title last season.

African Stars won the Namibia Premiership for the fourth time, and bolstered their squad with the signing of South Africa’s Lyema Dopolo last month.

CAF CL first preliminary round details

Orlando Pirates vs La Cure Waves



First leg: Sunday, 6 September, Côte d’Or National Sports Complex – 13:30 (SA time)

Second leg: Saturday, 12 September, Orlando Stadium – 15:00

How far will Orlando Pirates progress in this season’s CAF Champions League?

World.title: El Niño warning: How a warming Pacific could affect your next phone
World.content:
Experts warn El Niño-driven climate shocks could disrupt the power and water systems semiconductor production depends on: Image ChatGPT

A warming Pacific Ocean doesn’t sound like it should affect your next phone or laptop, but according to the World Economic Forum, this year’s El Niño carries a risk that could stretch that far.

Why a climate pattern threatens computer chips

Robert Muggah, founder of the Igarapé Institute, warns that climate shocks in general can disrupt power grids, water systems, and logistics corridors.

Semiconductor production and data centres depend on all three, and this El Niño counts among the climate shocks he means.



Chip fabrication plants use enormous volumes of ultra-pure water and stable electricity. Drought, flooding, or heat can strain regional infrastructure and put both at risk.

Semiconductors have become central to the broader AI economy. A disruption here doesn’t stay contained to one industry.

It’s worth being clear: this is a forward-looking risk assessment, not a report of disruption that’s already happened.



Why this feels different from past El Niño warnings

Muggah’s core argument is blunt: “Crises no longer arrive neatly or sequentially. They overlap, compound, and amplify one another.”

That’s the real shift here.

El Niño isn’t just a standalone weather risk anymore. It’s one variable among several that could ripple into an already fragile, hyper-connected global tech supply chain most of us rely on without a second thought.



It’s actually wild thinking a warming ocean could end up connected to something as unrelated-sounding as chip production, hey, but that’s exactly the kind of layered risk experts are now warning this El Niño could trigger.

Did you expect climate risk and tech supply chains to be connected like this, or does it seem like a stretch?

Let us know in the comments below, Mzansi…

World.title: Hawks target more suspects in Tembisa Hospital corruption probe
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - More suspects are being sought in the Tembisa Hospital theft case, says the Directorate for Priority Crime Investigation, also known as the Hawks.

Spokesperson Katlego Mogale says several investigations are running in parallel, tracing the money to identify the beneficiaries of the systematic looting of R2-billion.

The money was meant for the healthcare facility in Ekurhuleni. Gauteng Department of Health Chief Director of Financial Accounting Babita Deokaran blew the whistle when she discovered the looting under her watch in 2021.

Her murder outside her Johannesburg home blew the lid wide open, exposing the extent of the rot. Businessmen Hangwani Maumela and Vusimuzi ‘Cat’ Matlala are among those who have been linked to the theft.

World.title: Tsitsipas says Kyrgios's positive cocaine test 'kind of expected'
World.content:
NEW YORK - Stefanos Tsitsipas said that he was not surprised that his old rival Nick Kyrgios tested positive for cocaine and was suspended.

"I kind of expected it, to be honest," the world number 53 from Greece said at the US Open after defeating French 10th seed Arthur Fils in four sets in the opening round.

The former Wimbledon finalist Kyrgios has been provisionally suspended and last month admitted to making "a huge mistake" after failing a test for cocaine.

The 31-year-old Australian, who has hardly played singles tennis in recent years, apologised and said injuries had taken "a huge toll on me both physically and mentally".

After defeating Fils 4-6, 7-6 (7/3), 6-1, 6-4 in New York, Tsitsipas -- who briefly played doubles with Kyrgios but has had a turbulent relationship with him -- was asked about the positive drugs test.

"I'm not going to try and cover up someone that I know the truth for," the 28-year-old replied.

"I'll consider myself a nice person with everyone, but these were behaviours that I personally heard on the tour and heard other people in that same environment saying those sort of things to me.

"Again, when I saw it, I was, like: Well, pretty much expected, to be honest. I am surprised it came so late, though."

Boasting a big serve and booming groundstrokes, Kyrgios has won seven singles titles on the ATP Tour and rose to a high of 13 in the world in 2016.

His finest performance was on the grass at Wimbledon in 2022, when he reached the championship match, losing in four sets to Novak Djokovic.

Despite his natural talents that is as good as it got, with a series of injuries taking their toll.

In January he admitted he would never be the player that he once was.

World.title: Anthropic signs $35B computing deal with startup backed by Nvidia
World.content:
NEW YORK - Anthropic signed a $35 billion deal for access to cloud computing power from a US-based startup backed by Nvidia, adding to a string of such deals clinched by the artificial intelligence (AI) developer amid fierce competition for advanced computing power.

The San Francisco-based AI lab has agreed to a six-year deal with Lambda, a source familiar with the deal told AFP.

Based in San Jose, California, Lambda provides access to AI cloud computing services.

Lambda will secure access to a data centre being built by another company, Hut 8, which mines bitcoins and builds data centres, including one in Texas that Anthropic will tap for computing power, according to media reports.

Nvidia, which has invested in both Anthropic and Lambda, will lease the data centre from Hut 8, and Lambda will then pay Nvidia an unknown amount to get access to the data centre, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.

Anthropic also recently signed a similar six-year-long deal worth $45 billion with Nscale, a cloud provider based in London, which will give Anthropic capacity at a facility in West Virginia, a source confirmed to AFP.

Just this year, Anthropic has signed various computing deals worth at least $135 billion.

The company is in a race with AI lab OpenAI to win customers and grow revenue; the rivals are both barreling toward initial public offerings as well.

Demand for chips and advanced computing power has skyrocketed over the past couple of years as leading AI model developers compete with each other for customers and capacity.

Meanwhile, that demand is also crunching global supply chains for chips across sectors, including consumer electronics.

Apple has already increased prices for certain devices, such as Macs and iPads, due to memory and chip costs; the company is expected to increase prices for the newest generation of iPhones which it will unveil at an event in September.

World.title: Drones in Ithaca: Azov's Odyssey turns Ukraine war into modern myth
World.content:
KYIV - In a theatrical adaptation of the Odyssey by Ukraine's Azov military corps, Penelope beats a suitor to death with plastic grocery bags.

An attack drone flies over the stage to chase a soldier, while Odysseus shouts for battlefield updates over a radio.

Men sleep in khaki sleeping bags.

"We are not doing Homer, that's very important. Our Odyssey is about our heroes, though we draw on archaic, mythical, and profoundly significant themes," says Darya Legeyda, who plays Penelope.

The longing for home at the heart of Homer's Odyssey resonates in Ukraine, where Russia's invasion has displaced millions and sent hundreds of thousands to fight, with tens of thousands still missing or held captive.

While the epic has found audiences worldwide with Christopher Nolan's blockbuster, Kyiv has staged its adaptation: a collaboration between the Ivan Franko Theatre and the Azov military corps.

Written and performed by Azov service members, the play is part of the unit's cultural outreach, and ticket funds go to an organisation supporting prisoners of war.

World.title: Naomi Watts to receive lifetime award at top Spain film fest
World.content:
MADRID - Hollywood star actor and producer Naomi Watts will receive a lifetime achievement award at Spain's top film festival next month, organisers announced on Monday.

The San Sebastian Film Festival said the British-born Australian, a two-time Oscar nominee, would take the "Donostia" prize as "one of the most talented and recognised actresses of her generation".

Watts, 57, first made a name for herself in David Lynch's 2001 movie "Mulholland Drive" and has played versatile roles in both auteur cinema and big productions.

She earned Oscar nominations for her performances in "21 Grams" (2003) by Mexican director Alejandro Gonzalez Inarritu and "The Impossible" (2012) under Spain's Juan Antonio Bayona.

Inarritu's "Birdman" (2014), "You Will Meet a Tall Dark Stranger" (2010) by Woody Allen and Michael Haneke's "Funny Games" (1997) feature among her other standout roles.

Watts was nominated for an Emmy Award for her work in Ryan Murphy's mini-series "Feud: Capote vs. The Swans", where she was also an executive producer.

Watts has also stood out in recent times for raising awareness about women's health and menopause.

The prize ceremony will take place on September 19 in the northern coastal city of San Sebastian, where the Spanish-speaking world's most prestigious film festival will run from September 18-26.

A showing of the new film "The Housewife" will follow, where Watts stars as the enigmatic wife of a suspected former Nazi official living in 1960s New York.

German director, scriptwriter, producer and actor Werner Herzog is also due to take home a Donostia award this year.

The illustrious list of previous winners includes Gregory Peck, Bette Davis, Lauren Bacall, Francis Ford Coppola, Woody Allen, Oliver Stone, Agnes Varda, Catherine Deneuve and Pedro Almodovar.

World.title: I accept the challenge | Mosimane officially takes charge of Bafana
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - It’s official. Pitso Mosimane has been announced as Bafana Bafana’s new head coach, following the departure of Belgium’s Hugo Broos.

Mosimane is set for a second permanent stint in charge of the national team, having previously led Bafana from 2010 to 2012. He also served as caretaker coach in 2007.

His first permanent spell ended after South Africa failed to qualify for the 2012 Africa Cup of Nations.

The South African Football Association (SAFA) made the announcement on Tuesday.

Accepting the challenge, Mosimane said it was a special day in his career.

"I have been given the privilege of leading our national team again. I take this responsibility knowing that I still have something to give in football, especially in my country," he said.

"I know this is simply not a coaching job; it is bigger than Pitso Mosimane. I understand the weight of this role, the expectations that come with it, and what this team means to South Africa. With pride and determination, I accept the challenge," Mosimane said.

World.title: SASSA Black Card migration leaves 20,000 KZN beneficiaries behind
World.content:
DURBAN - More than 20,000 KwaZulu-Natal SASSA beneficiaries have still not migrated to Postbank’s Black Cards.

eThekwini has the largest group of beneficiaries yet to make the switch. The deadline to migrate from the Gold Cards was on Monday.

Postbank migration sites in the province remained quiet on Monday’s deadline.

Nationally, more than 1.8 million beneficiaries have switched to the Black Card, surpassing 80 percent of the target before the deadline.

Beneficiaries who missed the deadline are urged to visit their nearest Postbank card replacement site as soon as possible to complete the migration process and restore access to their social grant payments.

Human rights advocacy group Black Sash says the number of beneficiaries seeking to migrate could rise as more people are forced to make the switch to access their grants.

World.title: Rosemary Ndlovu, co-accused sentencing postponed
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The sentencing of convicted serial murderer Nomia Rosemary Ndlovu and her co-accused, former police officer Nomsa Mudau, has been postponed.

The pair appeared in the Kempton Park Regional Court on Tuesday, where sentencing proceedings were postponed to 15 September.

They were found guilty in May of offering to pay a hitman to kill Mudau’s ex-husband.

During the trial, the court heard that the alleged hitman instead warned the intended victim about the plot to have him killed.

Ndlovu is already serving six life sentences, as well as an additional 125 years, following her conviction in 2021 for a series of murders linked to insurance payouts.

The latest case forms part of a wider investigation that exposed a series of killings allegedly motivated by funeral and life insurance benefits.

World.title: Tribunal suspends Nicco Movers Sacco licence
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Tribunal says Nicco Movers had failed to demonstrate adequate compliance with road safety requirements. [Fiole, Standard]

Nicco Movers has suffered a major setback after a tribunal has suspended its PSV operator licence following two fatal accidents and widespread safety breaches across its fleet.

In a judgement rendered by the Transport Licensing Appeals Board Tribunal led by Hillary Kangogo, Adrian Kamotho, Benson Gichohi and Jackline Omiti has also overturned the National Transport and Safety Authority’s decision to revoke the operator’s licence but substituted it with an immediate suspension.

The four member Tribunal said the operator had failed to demonstrate adequate compliance with road safety requirements after two fatal incidents involving vehicles operating under its licence.

The first accident occurred on January 11, 2026, when a Nicco Movers vehicle, registration number KDQ 655D, was involved in a crash along Thika Superhighway near Kenyatta University/Kahawa Sukari, where a pedestrian was knocked down and died.

The second incident occurred on June 5, 2026, when Eugene Mutivi Mutuku, a Kenya Medical Training College intern, fell from moving Nicco Movers vehicle KDV 713J along Thika Superhighway near Waumini Radio Station and died.

The Tribunal noted that the deceased’s mother, Jacinta Nzilani Mutuku, claimed the conductor ejected her son from the moving vehicle.

Nicco Movers, however, maintained that the passenger jumped off the vehicle.

The driver and conductor were not produced before the Tribunal.

According to the judgment, the mother’s account was that the two abandoned the scene and had not been brought to justice.

The safety concerns extended beyond the two fatal incidents.

NTSA’s compliance analysis found that 30 vehicles had been recorded operating above the prescribed 80kph speed limit.

A further 11 vehicles were not transmitting speed-limiter data, one was operating without a speed limiter, 10 had no speed-limiter records while three had expired inspection certificates.

The Tribunal later directed the operator to present 51 vehicles for inspection.

Only six passed while 45 failed.

The defects included missing and defective passenger seat belts, missing door and window locks, faded or undersized chevrons and reflectors, defective horns and lamps and damaged body panels.

Some vehicles also lacked first-aid equipment and fire extinguishers.

The Tribunal said the evidence pointed to systemic compliance concerns rather than isolated incidents.

“There were two fatalities within six months on the same corridor,” the Tribunal stated.

It added that 30 vehicles had been recorded above 80kph, while speed-limiter data was missing or not being transmitted across a significant part of the fleet.

Despite upholding NTSA’s power to regulate the operator, the Tribunal found that revocation of the entire licence was disproportionate.

“Revocation fails the third and fourth inquiries,” the Tribunal ruled.

It said the law provides NTSA with a range of sanctions, including removing specified vehicles from a licence, reducing the maximum number of vehicles and suspending a licence before resorting to revocation.

“The statute therefore itself ranks the available tools: vehicle-level surgery first, suspension next, revocation last,” the Tribunal stated.

The Tribunal also rejected Nicco Movers’ argument that NTSA could not take regulatory action while police investigations into the fatal accident were ongoing.

“Regulatory licensing and the criminal process serve different ends and apply different standards,” it said.

“Nothing in the NTSA Act or the Fair Administrative Action Act makes a pending police file a bar to licensing action.”

The Tribunal further held that the operator had been allowed to respond to the allegations before the licence was revoked.

It found that the dating of NTSA’s revocation letter, which was dated June 9 despite the hearing taking place on June 12, was a clerical error and did not prove that the decision had been predetermined.

“On a balance of probabilities, the Board finds that the decision was taken after the hearing and that June 9, 2026 is a clerical error,” the Tribunal ruled.

“It is not proof that the Committee had finished the case before the Appellant spoke.”

The Tribunal nevertheless faulted the operator’s compliance record, finding that NTSA had power, duty and cause to act after the inspection and safety findings.

In its final order, the Tribunal said the appeal dated June 15, 2026 partially succeeds and is allowed.

It set aside NTSA’s revocation and substituted it with a suspension of the PSV operator licence with immediate effect.

Nicco Movers has been given seven days to address 10 compliance concerns identified by NTSA.

The Tribunal warned that if the concerns remain unresolved after 14 days from the date of the judgment, NTSA may issue another notice to show cause and subsequently revoke the operator’s licence.

“If the ten (10) ‘concerns and way forward’ items in order (b) above remain unsatisfied at the expiry of fourteen (14) days from the date of this Judgment, the Respondent may, after a further notice to show cause, revoke the operator licence,” the Tribunal ruled.

The Tribunal also discharged and vacated all interim orders previously issued in the appeal.

While expressing condolences to the family of Eugene Mutivi Mutuku, the Tribunal stressed the importance of preventing similar tragedies.

“Regulatory proceedings cannot restore a life. They can, and in this case they must, reduce the risk that another family will land in a similar predicament,” it stated.

World.title: Trumpets of reforms blow louder as Kenya marks 16 years under 2010 Constitution
World.content:
The Constitution, Kenyan flag and the National anthem. [PCS]

On Thursday, August 27, a group of people largely composed of the youth gathered under some trees at Jeevanjee Gardens in Nairobi, carrying Kenyans flag, and banners and placards inscribed with "implement the constitution. Kenyans first" words.

These were in protests against what they believed is deliberate failure of those in authority to fully implement the 2010 Constitution.

World.title: Ruto allies hit back at Gachagua over IEBC tender concerns
World.content:
The Kenya Integrated Elections Management System (KIEMS) kit. [File, Standard]

President William Ruto’s allies led by National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula have launched a scathing attack on former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua and the Opposition over their criticism of the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC), citing blackmail by the Opposition.

The leaders warned that attempts by politicians to dictate how the electoral agency procures technology and other election materials could undermine public confidence in the 2027 General Election.

World.title: IEBC rejects Gachagua's claims, defends 2027 polls preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC dismissed Gachagua's claims of political interference, graft and voter suppression in 2027 polls.

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has dismissed allegations of political interference, corruption and voter suppression surrounding preparations for the 2027 General Election, terming the claims false, unsubstantiated and aimed at undermining public confidence in the electoral body.

In a statement issued on Thursday, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the allegations followed statements made by Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a press briefing on Wednesday.

The commission specifically rejected claims that politicians had purchased a house for its chairperson to influence him, saying the allegation had changed from an alleged Sh80 million property to one worth Sh200 million.

"The allegations that a house has been purchased for the Chairperson of IEBC by some politicians for purposes of influencing him are unfortunate, unfair and unsubstantiated to date," Ethekon stated.

The commission also challenged Gachagua to provide evidence, including the location of the property, sale and transfer documents, payment receipts and details of the parties involved, and submit them to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission for investigation.

The electoral body also dismissed claims of improper staff changes, saying deployment and redeployment of employees was part of its normal administrative functions and was guided by its human resource policies and public service regulations.

"The Commission complies with its Human Resource policies, guidelines and other relevant instruments under the larger public service when engaging employees," the statement read in part.

It further denied allegations of malpractice against the chairperson and vice-chairperson, describing them as fabricated claims intended to damage the reputation of the commissioners and the commission.

Magarini by-election

On the Magarini by-election, IEBC said the poll was conducted in a free, fair and credible manner and was not challenged through an election petition. The commission added that it had successfully conducted several by-elections and was prepared to oversee the 2027 General Election.

At the same time, IEBC also defended its procurement process for election technology and ballot papers, saying all tenders were being conducted in accordance with Chapter 12 of the Constitution and the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015.

"Two key tenders, one for the Integrated Elections Management System, hardware and accessories, and another for ballot papers and other election materials, have temporarily been halted following a request for review filed before the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board," IEBC stated.

According to IEBC, documents for the technology tender were uploaded on its website and the Public Procurement Information Portal on August 11, 2026.

The commission said the technical specifications were generic and performance-based and open to all qualified suppliers. It stressed that the procurement process was still at its initial stages and that no company had been awarded the tender.

Voter register protected

The commission also dismissed claims that voter registration data could be manipulated or shared with external parties, insisting that the Register of Voters remained under its exclusive custody.

"Voter registration involves several stages, including in-person registration, verification of identity, collection of biometric and biographical data, transmission to a central database and automated biometric deduplication," IEBC added.

Flagged records are subjected to data cleaning, validation and adjudication before valid records are incorporated into the register.

The register will subsequently undergo a 30-day biometric verification exercise, followed by an independent audit before it is finalised and certified for use in an election.

IEBC said allegations of bribery, predetermined tender awards and voter suppression were false and potentially harmful to public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: Ruto hands Sh2.6bn to Mau Forest evictees
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto also announced the lifting pf the caveat that had been placed on land bordering the Mau Forest. [PCS]

President William Ruto has announced the payment of Sh2.6 billion to 13,000 families evicted from the Mau Forest in Narok six years ago, marking what he described as the closure of a long chapter.

Each beneficiary received Sh200,000 through M-Pesa to help them resettle and rebuild their lives away from the water tower.

Speaking at Sogoo in Narok South Constituency on Wednesday, during the final day of his two-day tour of Narok County, Ruto said the Government had taken steps to address the longstanding Mau Forest resettlement problem.

He noted that in 2023, the Government gave Sh300,000 each to 2,000 families living in tents in the Mau Forest to enable them to leave the water tower and purchase land elsewhere.

“We are today officially closing the long and painful chapter of people who were removed from the Mau Forest, which the County Government of Narok will now manage,” Ruto said.

The President criticised politicians who, he said, had continued to politicise the Mau Forest issue without providing lasting solutions.

“Many politicians have talked of the Mau question, but I talked of the Mau answer. This is why we are here today closing this chapter,” he said.

Ruto also announced that the Government had purchased 5,800 acres of land to settle families who have been living as squatters on property previously owned by the family of former Provincial Commissioner Isaiah Cheluget.

“We are processing title deeds of the people living on the land after buying the Cheluget farm,” he said.

Construction of Johanna Ng'eno University

The President also announced the allocation of Sh1.2 billion for the construction of Johanna Ng’eno University in Emurua Dikirr Constituency.

Speaking during the laying of the foundation stone, Ruto said the institution would fulfil a pledge to residents while expanding access to higher education for students from across the country.

“You told me, as residents of Emurua Dikirr, that you want a university. Today, I have brought KSh1.2 billion to construct the university that will be named after our brother Johana Ng'eno,” he said.

He said the university would create employment opportunities and attract new investments to the region.

At the same time, Ruto maintained that his administration had fulfilled at least 80 per cent of the pledges contained in its 2022 campaign manifesto.

“Kenyans will elect leaders based on their development record. Sloganeering will not make Kenyans vote for them. They have a long way to go,” he said.

The President further launched the construction of the 18-kilometre Mogondo-Cheramgoi-Mogor-Soit road in Emurua Dikirr, saying the project would improve connectivity and unlock economic opportunities in the region.

“This new road will strengthen connectivity and unlock greater economic opportunities in the region,” Ruto said.

World.title: Gachagua to Duale: You don't own pastoralists
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and delegates from Isiolo and Marsabit at Wamunyoro, Nyeri County on August 25, 2026. [Ali Abdi, Standard]

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) Leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale of allegedly doing nothing for pastoralist communities in the country.

Mr Gachagua said Duale, while being the only CS from northern Kenya and claiming to be the spokesperson of the group, had instead been a liability to pastoralists.

“You, the Borana who are here, along with the Turkana and Somali, are all complaining like other Kenyans. You suffer from runaway insecurity and widespread underdevelopment. We must join hands to vote out this rogue government (in next year's general election),” the former Deputy President told a delegation of grassroots leaders and residents from Isiolo and Marsabit who paid him a courtesy call at his Wamunyoro rural home in Nyeri.

“Duale thinks that the pastoralists are his property, his children or servants. What has he done for the people of Isiolo and Marsabit? (He has) only rhetoric, shouting pastoralists everywhere, every day,” he said.

Gachagua questioned how Duale would be able to marshal ‘millions’ of votes for President Ruto in the 2027 General Elections while he (Duale) could only raise 7,000 votes for the UDA presidential candidate in the 2022 polls in his Garissa Township Constituency backyard.

Despite his little contribution to the Kenya Kwanza administration's victory, Gachagua said Duale was appointed as the only CS from northern Kenya but had ended up doing nothing for the region and pastoralist communities.

“He only gave him (Ruto) 7,000 votes in Garissa Township. It's Central Kenya that propelled this government,” Gachagua told the gathering.

“Duale was appointed CS and he has nothing to show apart from empty words, going round shouting (the name of) pastoralists, and you (the pastoralists) are suffering. If you love them, then why are their livestock stolen every day?” He asked the CS.

“These pastoralists are killed every day and their cows and goats stolen. What have you done for them and you are in the government?” Gachagua posed.

The Opposition leader claimed that the government was ill-prepared for the heavily forecasted El Niño rainfall, pointing out that those living in flood-prone areas like the Tana Delta and Garissa are exposed to danger.

“Now, going into El Niño, what plan has been put in place to save people from death as a result of floods and how livestock will survive?” he asked the State.

During the event, Gachagua revealed that Yusuf Huka Jillo from Isiolo would represent Upper Eastern at the DCP secretariat and serve as a member of the National Executive Committee (NEC) in an acting capacity.

Gachagua said the mountain was now complete, with Isiolo and Marsabit forming Mt Kenya North.

The locals alleged that the Health CS was interfering in Isiolo County politics, with elder Hussein Jama claiming that Duale and the Office of the DCI were shielding a section of leaders accused of corruption and criminal activities.

Speakers claimed that there was massive corruption at the local lands registry office, while Mr Jillo faulted the State for the slow pace of registration of community land in Isiolo.

Jama said Isiolo International Airport, which was constructed during the administration of President Kibaki to help in the export of miraa and horticultural goods from the Mt Kenya region and livestock products, mainly meat and hides, lies idle because the expansion of the runway from 1.5 metres to 3 metres had not been done.

In response, Gachagua said the airport was meant to create employment and wealth, but the Kenya Kwanza administration had instead left it in ruin deliberately, claiming the move was aimed at sabotaging the economy of Mt Kenya and pastoralists’ economies.

“What was the good about destroying the Imenti forest to construct an airstrip for an individual while there is an international airport meant partly to serve the entire region just a few kilometres from Meru town?” Asked the DCP leader.

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: PM discusses with Fujairah officials steps to complete implementation of “Fujairah-Alamein” oil, gas company project
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly affirmed on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, the attention that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi is giving to the establishment of Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company, describing it as a promising strategic project whose agreement was recently signed.

He noted that completing the procedures for establishing Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company and holding its inaugural general assembly meeting at the Al-Hamra Petroleum Port, affiliated with the Western Desert Petroleum Company (WEPCO) in New Alamein, comes within the framework of the firmly rooted strategic relations between Egypt and the UAE.

Madbouly made the remarks during a meeting at the government headquarters in the New Capital with Director of the Fujairah Amiri Diwan Mohammed Saeed al Dhanhani to follow up the procedures and steps required to complete implementation of the project following the establishment of Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company.

The meeting was attended by Petroleum and Mineral Resources Minister Karim Badawi.

Madbouly stressed the vital importance and the project’s multiple developmental dimensions in the energy sector.

He also emphasized the importance of accelerating efforts and intensifying joint work to expedite the establishment of a special free zone under the name “Fujairah Alamein Oil and Gas Company” in New Alamein City. The company will engage in the storage and trading of petroleum products and crude oil and enter actual operational phases, in a manner that serves the mutual interests of both sides and reflects the depth of the firmly rooted strategic relations between Egypt and the UAE.

For his part, Dhanhani thanked Madbouly and his government for their efforts on this matter and particularly to the Ministry of Petroleum and Mineral Resources for its support for the establishment of the company.

Dhanhani expressed the keenness of Sheikh Hamad bin Mohammed Al Sharqi, Member of the UAE Supreme Council and Ruler of Fujairah, to strengthen ties of cooperation with the Egyptian side.

He affirmed the commitment to expediting implementation of the project.

The meeting reviewed the project’s implementation steps, which come within the framework of supporting and enhancing Egypt’s role as a regional hub for energy trading and handling.

The project aims to develop Al-Hamra Port through cooperation and integration with the Fujairah Oil and Gas Corporation. It also includes the transfer of expertise and the application of the latest systems and technologies in use, thereby enhancing the port’s efficiency and bringing it up to international standards.

The project will also involve storing crude oil using the storage facilities at Al-Hamra Petroleum Port in New Alamein, maximizing the economic benefits and returns from Egypt’s infrastructure and capitalizing on the port’s unique location and advanced infrastructure to make it a strategic hub for crude oil storage and transportation.

For his part, Badawi stressed the importance of the project and the substantial government support provided by both the Egyptian and the UAE sides to ensure the success of this project on Egypt’s Mediterranean coast and to replicate the successful experience of the existing project in the Emirate of Fujairah.

Badawi explained that ensuring the success of this major project is a top priority.

He affirmed that joint teams from both sides are working in full and continuous coordination to achieve this objective, complete the procedures and steps necessary for implementation and establish a specific timetable for the various stages of execution.

He stressed that the ministry would provide all necessary support and overcome any challenges that might arise during implementation.

World.title: President al-Sisi: Together for more prosperous future for Egyptian, Chinese peoples, humanity
World.content:
This year we celebrate the 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the Arab Republic of Egypt and the People’s Republic of China. Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with China in 1956, as an extension of the civilizational and historical ties between two nations whose roots extend deep into history.

As we mark this special anniversary between our two friendly countries, we also celebrate the visit of Chinese President Xi Jinping to Egypt as an honored and cherished guest.

Throughout history, Egypt and China have been united by enduring bonds of friendship and a shared legacy of civilizational achievement, embodied by the Nile River, the birthplace of Egyptian civilization and the lifeline of its people, and the mighty Yangtze River, the cradle of Chinese civilization and a timeless source of Chinese wisdom, culture, and philosophy.

Through the knowledge, sciences, and innovations they cultivated, these two ancient civilizations made profound contributions to human progress, creating an enduring arc of achievement stretching from the Pyramids of Egypt to the Great Wall of China.

Egyptian civilization made seminal contributions to fields such as medicine, engineering, and astronomy, while Chinese civilization pioneered transformative innovations that were remarkably advanced for their time.

The knowledge and discoveries generated by these civilizations were transmitted, developed, and built upon by successive generations of scholars and scientists, helping to lay foundations for the Industrial and Technological Revolutions and the unprecedented advances that followed.

Without this cumulative intellectual and scientific heritage, humanity could not have attained its present level of development across such a broad range of fields.

This shared legacy reinforces the legitimate aspiration of Egypt and China to participate fully and equitably in contemporary technological progress and to benefit from its advances, which will advance comprehensive and sustainable development for the peoples of both countries and other nations, and enable Egypt and China to continue their historic contribution to the advancement of human civilization.

The two countries were connected by a historic trade route that contributed to the movement of people and goods and extended from the Chinese Silk Road to the Red Sea and the Egyptian Suez Canal, the lifeline of global trade.

Along this route, missions and trade caravans journeyed from the coasts of China and Asia to Egyptian ports on the Red Sea and the Mediterranean, which continue to serve today as an indispensable link between East and West.

For centuries, Egyptian ports served as major commercial hubs for the exchange of goods among Asia, Europe, and Africa.

These vital routes also enabled the exchange of cultures, knowledge, and ideas between the two peoples, further strengthening the historic bonds between Egypt and China and laying the foundations for centuries of extensive people-to-people, commercial, and cultural interaction.

This long history of engagement ultimately culminated in the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries seven decades ago—a landmark moment that opened a new chapter in bilateral relations and paved the way for their continued development and flourishing.

Egypt was the first Arab and African country to establish diplomatic relations with the People’s Republic of China, at a pivotal moment when Egypt affirmed its support for the right of peoples to freely choose their own political and economic systems.

Egypt thereby paved the way for Arab and African relations with China, which have expanded and flourished over the decades, culminating in the establishment of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation.

Egypt has consistently adhered to the One-China principle and rejected interference in China’s internal affairs. It supported the restoration of China’s permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council, while China supported Arab rights and the right of the Palestinian people to establish their independent state.

These historic positions remain deeply engraved in the collective memory of both nations as enduring milestones in their relationship.

As the Egyptian and Chinese peoples commemorate this cherished anniversary, they recall this shared history not only with pride, but also as a lasting foundation for solidarity and a source of renewed momentum for deeper cooperation, mutual support, and partnership in the years ahead.

Over the past seven decades, Egypt-China relations have witnessed remarkable development, culminating in the establishment of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries in 2014, during my first official visit to the People’s Republic of China.

At that pivotal juncture, Egypt was determined to broaden and deepen its relations with countries across the world, diversify its foreign policy, and reach out to its friends and partners to forge stronger and more comprehensive partnerships founded on mutual respect, solidarity, and mutual benefit.

Egypt also exerted efforts to advance joint development in infrastructure, investment, trade, manufacturing, and technology transfer. China was among the first countries to demonstrate its keenness to consolidate relations with Egypt on the basis of these firmly established principles, which constituted the solid foundation for enduring and longstanding relations that have succeeded in achieving benefits for the two peoples and safeguarding the interests of the two countries.

Accordingly, the comprehensive strategic partnership established by the two countries has brought about a major transformation in bilateral relations. China has become a major trade and economic partner for Egypt, and Chinese direct investments have increased, including in the Suez Canal Economic Zone SCZONE, which has provided tremendous opportunities for Chinese investors to generate returns and benefit from the significant advantages available to foreign investors in the zone.

The SCZONE contains industrial areas hosting numerous factories of international companies from various countries seeking to benefit from these opportunities, as well as from Egypt’s geographical location at the heart of the world, as an essential link between East and West.

Chinese companies have also contributed to numerous major national projects, such as the construction of the Central Business District in the New Capital, the launch of the electric railway to the Tenth of Ramadan City, the construction of renewable energy power plants, the development of ports, and other projects that formed part of the Egyptian state’s national plans to overhaul its infrastructure, which Egypt undertook with the cooperation with a number of different countries, including China.

This has contributed to Egypt’s globally advanced position in the field of infrastructure, which is pivotal to laying the foundations for an advanced and integrated industrial base, and transforming Egypt into a global logistics hub for industry, trade, and services.

This significant progress in strengthening and modernizing Egypt’s infrastructure has reinforced its position as an attractive destination for major industrial investments from around the world. China has been among the leading countries keen to expand its industrial presence in Egypt and capitalize on the country’s strategic location, advanced infrastructure, and the significant investment opportunities and competitive advantages it offers.

Egypt and China share a common commitment to harnessing the synergies between Egypt’s strategy for industrial localization and China’s strategy for high-quality development, with a view to attracting greater Chinese industrial investment to Egypt. Priority sectors include electric vehicles, energy-storage batteries, renewable energy, electronics, components for seawater desalination plants, shipbuilding, and other advanced industries.

This cooperation also extends to promoting technology transfer in telecommunications, artificial intelligence, and space sciences, which represent key priorities for economic and technological development and promising avenues for expanding Egypt-China cooperation in the next phase of our strategic partnership.

China’s development and its ability to achieve remarkable economic progress and eradicate extreme poverty have been an inspiration to developing countries seeking to realize their aspirations for modernization and advancement.

Egypt views this development positively, while at the same time believing that developing countries have a tremendous opportunity to achieve economic advancement in accordance with a development model suited to their respective circumstances and compatible with their historical and cultural contexts.

In this vein, it is important to underscore the need to create an appropriate international environment that enables these countries to achieve this desired objective.

From this standpoint, Egypt has played its constructive regional and international role over the past decades and adhered to the principles and purposes of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and the rules-based international order. Egypt has worked to contribute to supporting international organizations in carrying out their essential role in safeguarding international peace and security.

It has made tangible contributions to peacekeeping and peacebuilding operations and participated, alongside all parties of the international community, in efforts to enhance the role of international economic organizations in achieving global sustainable development and advancing the United Nations development goals.

Egypt has firmly maintained its position in support of strengthening the voice of the Global South and promoting its representation in international institutions, in a manner that respects the right of these countries to express their will and takes their concerns into consideration.

Egypt has joined a number of emerging institutions and joined BRICS in 2024, as well as the New Development Bank affiliated with it and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

It also joined the Shanghai Cooperation Organization as a dialogue partner, out of its keenness to strengthen South-South dialogue and openness to broad and diverse partnerships with all countries of the world.

I therefore take this opportunity to congratulate China on assuming the BRICS presidency next year, and wish to express that Egypt looks forward to continued coordination and consultation with China in this regard.

Egypt has also adhered to a policy of strategic balance as a guiding principle of Egyptian foreign policy at a time when waves of polarization and competition are intensifying, emphasizing its independent foreign policy and calling for the international community to coordinate its efforts to overcome the global challenges that have come to threaten the entire world.

Egypt and China have become partners contributing together to enhancing the role of the Global South in the international system, in a manner that achieves greater justice and fairness for developing countries.

From the same viewpoint, Egypt has undertaken intensive diplomatic efforts to de-escalate the situation in the Middle East and prevent the escalation and expansion of the conflict, as the region undergoes a dangerous phase of conflicts that threaten regional security and stability and, indeed, threaten international peace and security.

In this context, Egypt and China agree on the necessity of resolving conflicts through peaceful means, taking into consideration the security concerns of all parties, and respecting the sovereignty of states as a basis for the peaceful settlement of conflicts. It is not in the interest of any regional or international party to widen the conflict or exacerbate armed hostilities.

In the same vein, the Nile River has been the foundation of Egyptian civilization and a vital source of its prosperity throughout history. Egypt and its fellow Nile Basin brothers have benefited from the Nile for thousands of years, with its waters serving as a shared resource and a basis for life, development and human well-being.

Throughout its history, Egypt has remained committed to supporting the development of the countries of the Nile Basin, particularly in the areas of water resources development and dam construction, including in the Sudan and Uganda, and, most recently, through its contribution to the mega-project of the Julius Nyerere Hydropower Project in Tanzania.

Egypt will remain steadfast in advocating for transboundary cooperation in accordance with the principles and rules of international law, rather than unilateral approaches that result in harm to downstream States.

Egypt firmly believes that the sustainable management of shared water resources can only be achieved through prior notification, consultations and consensus among riparian States.

In this regard, Egypt highly values China’s position that has affirmed its recognition of the vital importance of the Nile River to Egypt as its principal lifeline, and reiterates the importance of refraining from unilateral measures and strengthening collaboration in good faith to achieve Win-Win cooperation and mutually beneficial outcomes.

Just as Egypt and China have, over the years, written remarkable chapters in the history of cooperation and friendship between our two countries, we look forward to writing together a new chapter in this enduring relationship, whose roots stretch back thousands of years. We aspire to many more decades of progress and prosperity for our two friendly peoples, and to a future in which the world enjoys greater stability, security, peace, and development.

World.title: At least 8 dead and more missing after ferry carrying hundreds capsizes off Cyprus’ northern coast
World.content:
A search and rescue operation was continuing uninterrupted in the Mediterranean after a passenger ferry carrying nearly 270 people capsized while traveling from northern Cyprus to Turkey, killing at least eight people.

Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman said 241 people had been rescued alive, but 18 people are still missing.

The Filo Jet was carrying 259 passengers and eight crew members from Girne, also known as Kyrenia, to Taşucu in southern Turkey when it began taking on water just a few miles off the coast of Cyprus, according to the Turkish Interior Ministry.

Erhürman said search operations for the missing are continuing uninterrupted with teams sent from Turkey.

Turkey had sent additional search and rescue assets to the scene, deploying three aircraft, four unmanned aerial vehicles, six helicopters, four Coast Guard boats, a fast attack craft, a frigate and a patrol vessel to the operation, according to Turkey’s state-run news agency Anadolu.

“Priority is with the search and rescue but concurrently the police are carrying out their investigation. Any comments on the cause will just be speculation at this time,” Erhürman added.

After capsizing the ship sank and is now lying at a depth of 514 meters (1,686 feet), he said.

The prime minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Ünal Üstel, said the ferry’s capsizing was “the biggest maritime disaster Cyprus has ever experienced,” adding that the vessel’s captain and seven crew members have been detained.

The Turkish Cypriot Council of Ministers declared three days of national mourning for those killed and missing in the disaster, according to Anadolu.

The ferry was one of several shuttle sea services that link north Cyprus, a breakaway unrecognized Turkish Cypriot state, with Turkey daily.

Video from the scene of the ship’s capsizing showed dozens of people on the side of the vessel and others in life-jackets in the water.

One survivor described a chaotic scene as water began entering the vessel before it capsized. Efe Multici told CNN Türk that passengers alerted crew members after noticing water seeping into the ferry but said their concerns were not initially taken seriously.

“I was downstairs, and water started seeping in. We told the crew. It was really windy,” Multici said. “The ship kept coming up and then crashing down. When the water started seeping in, we told the crew. They didn’t take it seriously.”

According to Multici, the situation rapidly deteriorated after crew members informed the captain. He described difficulties finding life jackets and reaching emergency exits as the vessel listed sharply to one side.

“Some people couldn’t find the life vests, so they had to jump off without them. It was a huge issue: the life vests,” he said. “The ship went sideways at some point. It rolled toward the left. Some people broke the windows, some doors didn’t open.”

Multici said he eventually found a life vest and reached an inflatable raft.

Turkish Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş, said in post on X that he extended his condolences to those who had lost their lives in “this exceedingly tragic incident.”

Four coastguard vessels from northern Cyprus and a passenger vessel took part in rescue operations, the Turkish Interior Ministry said, as well as two coastguard helicopters to the area.

From the south of the island, the Greek-aligned Republic of Cyprus also expressed condolences and offered assistance following the disaster.

Greek Cypriot government spokesperson Konstantinos Letymbiotis said authorities were following developments “with deep sorrow and concern” and reiterated the government’s readiness to contribute to search-and-rescue efforts and mobilize any necessary resources. “At a time like this, the preservation of human life is paramount,” he said on X.

The US diplomatic mission in Turkey also expressed condolences following the disaster.

In a statement posted on X on Sunday, the US Embassy in Turkey said it extended its “heartfelt condolences” to the families of those who lost their lives and added that its thoughts remained with those still missing and everyone affected by the incident.

The United Nations’ top representative in Cyprus, Khassim Diagne, expressed his condolences on Sunday, saying he was “deeply saddened” following the capsizing of the passenger ferry.

“Our thoughts are with all those impacted by this tragedy and with the rescue teams continuing their efforts to save lives,” Diagne said on X.

Video from the scene showed at least one helicopter hovering above the capsized vessel.

The vessel was seen north of Girne on Sunday morning, according to MarineTraffic tracking data, before transmissions of its position ceased.

A live stream from Girne showed people who had reached the port by helicopter and on rescue boats – amid the sound of ambulance sirens. Several ambulances were shown lined up at the harbor.

This is a developing story that has been updated.

World.title: The US says it’ll crack down on countries doing business with Iran. Who’s buying Iranian oil?
World.content:
New York — US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday vowed an “economic D-Day” for countries that buy oil from Iran. Experts say that means one country in particular: China.

Bessent didn’t name China on Monday, but he left little room for doubt.

“We find that the best way to engage with countries is through quiet diplomacy, and we are level-setting with every country to tell them our expectations,” Bessent said on Monday. “We know who they are. They know who they are.”

But while Bessent’s threat could put China front and center, the repercussions could reach across the world – even for American consumers, who could find their own energy costs rising as a result.

Tehran likely shipped $3.9 and $4.2 billion worth of oil in September 2025, one analysis found; China, the world’s largest energy consumer, buys the vast majority.

“Chinese purchases account for roughly 90 percent of Iran’s exported oil, providing tens of billions of dollars in annual revenue that supports Iran’s government budget and military activities,” the U.S.-China Economic and Security Review Commission said earlier this year.

Monday’s announcement was a “warning shot,” Bessent said. While some entities and individuals were sanctioned, he did not announce broad measures aimed at any specific nations.

On Monday, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian said: “Sanctions and pressure tactics do not help in resolving issues. They will only lead to escalation that serves no one’s interest.”

During a regular press briefing, Lin also hinted that China could take its own measures: “China is closely following relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its own rights and interests.”

Thirty-eight percent of China’s oil and 23% of its liquified natural gas transits through the Strait of Hormuz, a focal point of the Iran war, according to a Nomura report in April.

China has already reduced its Iranian oil intake. Its Iranian crude imports averaged around 1.4 million barrels per day before the war but have fallen to around 700,000 in recent months due to lower refinery runs and drawdowns from onshore inventories, according to Emma Li at energy analytics firm Vortexa.

“A complete halt (in imports of Iranian crude) would probably have a limited immediate impact on China’s overall oil security, because imports from Iran have already fallen substantially and China still holds relatively large crude inventories,” Tianyue Hu, an analyst at energy intelligence firm Rystad, told CNN.

US reasury Secretary Scott Bessent speaks during a press conference to outline further sanctions against Iran, at the Treasury Department in Washington, DC, on Monday, August 24. Evelyn Hockstein/Reuters

But new sanctions could further erode the Trump administration’s rocky relationship with China. The two nations were in a blistering trade war last year at the height of President Donald Trump’s tariffs rollout. And they recently revived a tit-for-tat exchange of sanctions.

“China, by far, is the most impactful one if you really wanted to make a dent in Iran’s ability to continue to finance their activities,” Daniel Tannebaum, a nonresident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, previously told CNN.

It’s not the first time the United States has threatened sanctions on Iranian trade partners.

India once was a major importer of Iranian oil. The two maintained a $1.1 billion trade relationship between April and December 2025 for goods like rice and sugar, but India stopped importing Iranian oil in 2019 due to US sanctions. (India bought Iranian oil in April of this year amid an energy crisis.)

Muddy waters

It’s hard to determine how much US sanctions could impact China or any other countries that depend on Iranian oil.

Wall Street analysts haven’t even been able to get a straight answer on how much oil is leaving the Strait of Hormuz. While US Energy Secretary Chris Wright asserted that the strait is open and oil is flowing, Iran says the opposite. And third-party ship-tracking data showed about half the amount Wright claimed.

Then there are shadow fleets, used often by countries under sanctions. These oil tankers hide their owners, origins and destinations, making them hard to track. Ship tracking platform Kpler said this month that shadow transit made up around 50% strait traffic in recent weeks, up from around 12.5% a month ago.

But the lack of oil flows affects everybody. Large oil reserves kept the world from entering a major oil shortage when the war with Iran started in February.

And periodic ceasefires during the war sent global oil prices lower – only to rise again whenever those agreements have lapsed or run out.

American consumers have already seen the effects of higher oil prices because of the war. The current national average price for gas is $4.10 a gallon, compared to last year’s average of $3.15, according to AAA.

“No one is above the reach of US sanctions,” Bessent said Monday. But he sidestepped announcing end dates for any decisions. And Chinese leader Xi Jinping is expected to visit the US next month.

“I’m not going to set timelines, but we do not have infinite patience here,” Bessent said.

CNN’s Simone McCarthy, Jennifer Hansler, Adam Cancryn, Sylvie Zhuang and David Goldman contributed to this report.

World.title: Israel’s far-right competes for votes with increasingly extreme visions
World.content:
Far-right Israeli minister Itamar Ben Gvir has made it a point to post videos of himself on social media taunting or mocking Palestinian prisoners. He boasted of threatening the most high-profile Palestinian prisoner. He showed off activists from a Gaza flotilla bound on the floor. And he is proud of a new law he pushed to expand the death penalty for Palestinians convicted of terrorism.

But as elections near, his messaging has grown more extreme. His latest AI-generated campaign video shows rows of numbered Palestinian prisoners in brown uniforms moving along a conveyor belt into a fenced compound with watchtowers; the inmates appear well-fed at the start and thinner and distressed after passing through the industrial-style processing line. The post says, “We promised – we delivered.” The video was removed from Ben Gvir’s account on X after amassing more than four million views.

The minister has long called for conditions of Palestinian security prisoners to be reduced to “the minimum required by law.”

Ben Gvir is perhaps the best known of Israel’s far-right politicians, a provocateur with his hands on the country’s levers of power. As the minister of National Security, he is in charge of the police and the prisons as his politics have become a defining feature of Israel’s image abroad.

With two months until the elections, Israel’s far-right field is becoming increasingly crowded, packed with small parties vying for a finite pool of votes. To stand out, politicians are unabashed in their messaging and their vision for the country.

The far-right is a dominant feature in Israeli politics – and a key component of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition. Political parties need to garner 3.25 percent of the vote to cross the electoral threshold and enter the next parliament.

Those that fall short are excluded, and their votes effectively thrown out.

That electoral arithmetic is intensifying competition for right-wing voters and pushing politicians to adopt even harder-line positions.

Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich repeatedly celebrates the expansion of Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, openly boasting of destroying the possibility of a Palestinian state. A cornerstone of his election campaign is called “Yes. Let’s Judaize!” – a plan which aims to change the demographic reality in the Negev and Galilee, areas of Israel with substantial Arab populations, by applying settlement strategies from the West Bank: bringing a million additional Jewish residents and establishing about 40 new communities alongside dozens of individual farms.

Meanwhile, Ofer Winter recently launched his new “Your People Israel” party. The retired brigadier general is popular among Israel’s right-wing and religious Zionist movement. At the party’s launch event in late-August, he said, “There will never be a Palestinian state here. The solution in Gaza is simple – emigration.”

His party’s number two is Yoseph Haddad, an Arab Christian who is a pro-Israel activist and provocateur. Haddad, who has set his sights on becoming the minister of Public Diplomacy in the next government and the first Arab member of the Security Cabinet, said, “It is time the Arab community has representatives who work for them, not for Gaza, Jenin, and Ramallah. I hold them in contempt.”

Avi Maoz, who leads the far-right “Noam” party, has railed against gay Pride parades in Jerusalem, secularism , and feminism. On his own, he is not expected to cross the electoral threshold. Nor is Moshe Feiglin’s “Identity” party. Feiglin, a veteran far-right libertarian political activist and occasional member of Netanyahu’s Likud party, has advocated for the destruction of Gaza and the “voluntary” emigration of Palestinians to third countries. “Every child in Gaza is the enemy,” he said last year on Israel’s Channel 14. “We need to occupy Gaza and settle it, and not a single Gazan child will be left there.”

For Netanyahu, the abundance of far-right parties creates a real risk of losing tens of thousands of votes. If any of these parties fall under the electoral threshold, Netanyahu has warned that the right-wing risks losing the election.

The prime minister has released several video and social media messages in recent weeks, publicly pleading with Ben Gvir, Smotrich and Winter to unite as one bloc instead of running as smaller parties. But so far, the right-wing parties are focusing on their own campaigns and leaning into a message that is becoming more extreme.

World.title: Ukraine racing to develop new interceptors as Russian drones and missiles ravage the country
World.content:
Ukraine is urgently trying to develop interceptors capable of countering a new generation of Russian jet-powered drones that have wreaked havoc across the country in recent months.

Along with the Kremlin’s ballistic weapons and a new type of cruise missile, the jet-drones have caused massive damage in and around the capital, Kyiv.

They have also been used to target warehouses, gas stations, postal facilities and factories in what is becoming a much broader war in terms of targets.

The jet-powered Shahed drones – known as the Geran-4 and Geran-5 – are more difficult to intercept because of their speed and number. They are three times faster than the original Shaheds that Russia procured from Iran.

“Drone attacks are constant, with many jet-powered Shaheds,” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Sunday. Almost 1,500 drones of all types were fired at Ukraine over the previous four days, more than half of them jet-powered, he said.

The mass deployment of the jet-powered drones has accelerated over the past two months. About 1,500 were used in July, and more than 2,500 in August, according to Serhiy Beskrestnov, an adviser to Zelensky .

They were “being launched at Ukraine practically straight from the factory,” he said in a Facebook post at the weekend. Ukraine’s Defense Intelligence alleges that the jet-powered drones contain hundreds of components made by foreign companies, including in the US, UK and China.

Many of the jet-powered drones have been fired at the capital as Russia has moved to barrages against Kyiv both day and night. On Saturday, the Ukrainian military said Russia fired 224 drones at Ukraine in daylight hours – most of them jet-powered. On Sunday, Kyiv experienced eight air raid alerts between midnight and dusk.

The Kremlin’s goal is to exhaust Ukrainian air defenses and sap the morale of civilians, as it expands its list of targets to food warehouses and stores and continues strikes against energy infrastructure, say Ukrainian officials.

“The enemy is trying to paralyze economic activity in the capital and major cities, so our approaches and response mechanisms must change,” Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said over the weekend.

The intensity of Russian daytime strikes also comes just as children are preparing for the new school year.

The Kyiv city office said Monday it was likely that lessons will be disrupted and urged parents to discuss with their children “some simple yet important issues – how they should act in the event of an alert, where they should take shelter, and what they should do if they are caught in a dangerous situation on their way to school.”

“In the current circumstances, this is just as much a part of preparing for the new school year as packing a school bag or getting the school uniform ready,” it said.

The Chess Game of Innovation

For now, Zelensky has acknowledged, it is mainly combat aircraft that protect against the jet-powered drones. But Ukraine’s small air force is already stretched, and using fighter jets against the drones is expensive.

And so the race is on in yet another episode of the leapfrog technology race that has characterized the nearly five-year war.

Four companies have developed relevant interceptor drones, one of which had “the most successful technology,” Zelensky said on the weekend. Field trials have already begun on all four contenders, according to Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara. “The aim is to bring these solutions up to the required level as quickly as possible and scale up production to thousands of units,” he said on Saturday.

But devising the technology and deploying it are two very different challenges. “Offensive capabilities always stay one step ahead of defensive ones,” said the deputy head of the President’s Office, Pavlo Palisa, on Friday. “We will certainly have to adapt. This will take time.”

One of the Ukrainian-made interceptors that is showing promise, called the Sting, is reported to have brought down two of the jet-powered drones in recent days.

Another Ukrainian company, F-Drones, has updated its interceptor. “Russia is now deploying jet-powered Shahed drones, so we built LITAVR+. The upgraded interceptor reaches speeds of over 400 km/h,” it said on X.

Countering jet-powered drones is also at the top of the agenda of former Ukrainian Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, who has begun a visit to the United States to explore areas of cooperation with defense technology companies “and organizations that can become partners in our new projects and help strengthen Ukraine.”

“We also plan to build new ventures from scratch around the technologies that are critically needed on the battlefield today,” Fedorov posted on X, including robotics to “remove personnel from the most dangerous front-line sectors,” and low-cost AI-guided missiles.

Russian Banderol targets Ukraine’s maritime corridor

The battle to win a technological edge in the conflict is never-ending. While Ukraine has successfully expanded its range of mid- and long-range strike drones, Russia has developed a cheap cruise missile it has dubbed the Banderol.

The five-meter- (16-foot-) long missile has a maximum speed of 385 to 405 miles per hour (620–650 kilometers an hour) and a reported range of up to 310 miles (500 kilometers). It carries a 330-pound (150-kilogram) warhead.

The debris of a Russian S8000 Banderol cruise missile lies on the ground outside an apartment block in the Saltivskyi district of Kharkiv, Ukraine, on August 9. Viacheslav Madiievskyi/NurPhoto/AP

Its range is sufficient to cover much of southern Ukraine when launched from helicopters over Crimea. Dozens of Banderols have been used against the port of Odessa in recent weeks, interrupting Ukraine’s grain exports.

Since the beginning of August, Ukraine has exported 1.4 million tons of grain and oilseeds, according to Taras Vysotskyi, minister of agrarian policy – only about one-third of the potential export volume.

The Banderol attacks have significantly slowed operations along Ukraine’s maritime corridor through the Black Sea, Ukrainian Navy spokesman Dmytro Pletenchuk said early in August. The constant attacks are making insurance for grain shipments too expensive, according to industry sources.

Analysts say the Russian military may be preparing to launch the Banderol from ground-based platforms as well as drones and helicopters.

Former Defense Minister Fedorov, who was dismissed by Zelensky in July and is now working in a private capacity, has warned that Ukraine is “gradually, slowly losing” the war.

While in Washington, he told the Financial Times that the situation changed month-to-month, but he warned that Russia’s recent air strikes and ever-intensifying use of missiles and advanced drones were critical challenges.

“Right now, if we don’t respond to these issues, they will smash us,” he said.

World.title: Public Prosecution issues decision following fraud at New Cairo school
World.content:
