World.title: A look back at Estonia's presidential elections | Episode 7: Alar Karis, 2021
World.content:
Five years ago, Alar Karis emerged from a crowded field of potential candidates to win Estonia's presidency, backed by a cross-party search for a politically unaffiliated figure capable of securing broad support in the Riigikogu.

Kersti Kaljulaid, who became president in 2016, decided not to run in the 2021 presidential election.

"Good politics has no home. Today, the Riigikogu is not a home for good politics. And if you're one of the players on the field, then everything you say is simply part of the competition. But if you're a little removed from the field, you have an opportunity to comment on the game. And it seems to me that Estonian politics needs people like that as well," Kaljulaid told ETV's "Ringvaade" when asked why she no longer wanted to run for president.

During the first half of 2021, Riigikogu President Jüri Ratas was discussed as a possible presidential candidate. In June, Ratas announced that he did not intend to run for president.

Kallas and Ratas first approach Jüri Raidla

In July, attorney Jüri Raidla acknowledged that Prime Minister Kaja Kallas and Riigikogu President Jüri Ratas had jointly asked him to run for president. Raidla turned down the proposal, saying the president should be competent in foreign policy, an area in which he lacked expert knowledge.

In August, Jüri Luik said that although several political parties had approached him about becoming a presidential candidate, he would stick to his earlier plan to leave domestic politics and take up the post of Estonia's ambassador to NATO in September.

Other names floated as possible candidates included Henn Põlluaas, Tarmo Soomere, Kaimar Karu, Indrek Laul and several others. Of these, Soomere was perhaps the most seriously considered. He met with four Riigikogu parliamentary groups: Isamaa, the Social Democratic Party, the Reform Party and the Center Party.

Tarmo Soomere meeting with Isamaa MPs. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

The leaders of those parties met on August 6, after which Jüri Ratas said Soomere did not have enough support in the Riigikogu to be elected president, which would require 68 votes in favor. Soomere's lack of political experience, particularly in foreign policy, was cited as a weakness.

On August 17, Alar Karis, then director of the Estonian National Museum, acknowledged that Center Party Chairman Jüri Ratas had asked him to consider running for president. In addition to the Center Party, the leaders of the Reform Party, Isamaa and the Social Democratic Party supported the proposal. At the time, Kaja Kallas' first government, a coalition of the Reform Party and the Center Party, was in office. A day later, Karis agreed to become a presidential candidate.

On August 27, the Reform Party and Center Party's 59 members of the Riigikogu formally nominated Karis for president. Under their agreement, they were to support Karis through the end of the Electoral College process.

Isamaa and the Social Democratic Party left the decision on how to vote up to each of their members. About half of the MPs in each party's parliamentary group supported Karis.

The Riigikogu convened to elect the president on August 30. Alar Karis received 63 votes in the first round, five short of the number needed to be elected. As many as 16 unmarked ballots were cast. EKRE's 19 MPs, as well as Siim Kallas and Helir-Valdor Seeder, who were hospitalized, did not collect ballots. One MP who collected a ballot also did not cast it.

It was believed that some of the blank ballots in the secret vote came from Isamaa MPs, with several also coming from the ranks of the Social Democrats.

A day later, on August 31, the second round of the presidential election was held in the Riigikogu. The number of unmarked ballots fell from 16 the previous day to eight. The number of votes in favor of Karis rose to 72, exceeding the minimum of 68 required. Alar Karis was elected president of Estonia.

Alar Karis on ETV's "Esimene stuudio" talk show. Source: Kairit Leibold/ERR

The new president took office on October 11. Alar Karis was 63 when he became president.

In March this year, public trust in the presidency rose to 76 percent, its highest level in three years. A nationwide Emor survey commissioned by the Government Office found that support for the president increased among both ethnic Estonian respondents and respondents of other ethnic backgrounds.

Everyone keen to avoid repeat of 2016 fiasco

Erkki Keldo, the Reform Party's secretary general at the time, said that in 2021 there was a clear determination to avoid a repeat of what happened in 2016 when a president could not be elected by either the Riigikogu or the Electoral College and the Riigikogu ultimately agreed to elect Kersti Kaljulaid.

"There was a clear desire to try to find a candidate right away in the Riigikogu who would not be seen as the candidate of any particular party," Keldo said.

Keldo said that because the Reform Party and Center Party were in government at the time, the search for a presidential candidate was led primarily by the parties' then-leaders, Kaja Kallas and Jüri Ratas, as well as the chairs of their parliamentary groups.

Ballots being counted at the first round of the 2021 presidential election. Source: Erik Peinar, Chancellery of the Riigikogu

Ratas: Cooperation with Kallas was smooth

Jüri Ratas recalled that his cooperation with Kaja Kallas went very smoothly. "I rate it very highly. The cooperation with Kaja Kallas was very good and based on trust, both in finding a presidential candidate and in negotiations with the Riigikogu parliamentary groups, so that was important," Ratas said.

According to Keldo, it was difficult to secure opposition support for many of the candidates. For example, it became clear that it would not be possible to muster the 68 votes needed for Tarmo Soomere.

Ratas, who was also president of the Riigikogu at the time, said that when he proposed Karis as a possible candidate to the party leaders, he encountered no opposition to Karis.

Lauri Läänemets, the current leader of the Social Democratic Party who was a member of the party's parliamentary group at the time, also said the Social Democrats had no reason to oppose Karis because they had no prospect of putting forward a candidate who could attract broad support. "Besides, Karis was a pretty good candidate and there was no point in playing any games," Läänemets said.

Keldo said it was also important that Karis was not associated with any political party. "Alar Karis' name had come up before as well. We also had people who had worked with Alar many times before in various positions. Alar's strength was that he had served multiple terms as a university rector, had been auditor general and at the time he was head of the Estonian National Museum. He had held a great many positions in public life. It was important that he was clearly impartial and not associated with anyone," Keldo said.

Helir-Valdor Seeder, who was Isamaa's leader and parliamentary group chair at the time, said that because the president had to unite people and provide balance, they naturally sought someone who was not affiliated with any political force.

President Alar Karis' inauguration on October 11, 2021. Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

But what might explain why Alar Karis failed to secure the required 68 votes in the first round? "Because the vote is secret, politicians, particularly those in opposition, often like to play around a little and see whether the coalition's votes will actually hold. Once they saw that enough votes had been cast and that the coalition's votes were holding, the opposition and others also came on board in the second round and duly voted him in," Keldo said.

Ratas said that by the second round, members of the Riigikogu had recognized their responsibility to elect the president in parliament. "I suppose that in the first round, some members of the Riigikogu still wanted to test things out, play around a little and make things more interesting, but I think a sense of responsibility brought enough votes behind Karis," Ratas added.

Ratas said that because they were confident Karis had sufficient support in the Riigikogu, they did not undertake more extensive efforts to secure the support of Electoral College members.

Alar Karis and Sirje Karis. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

World.title: Dentist: Let's take tooth‑brushing partly out of parents' control
World.content:
Dentist Anastassia Kuldmaa says that supervised tooth‑brushing in kindergartens takes oral hygiene partly out of parents' control, because a child cannot be responsible for whether their mother or father considers dental care important. Teeth also need rest, and the biggest problem today is constant snacking.

"With sadness I must admit that morning and evening tooth‑brushing does not happen effectively in every home. One brushing is simply skipped, or the classic scenario — the child is pushed into the bathroom with a toothbrush and expected to manage alone, but the child doesn't know how," said Dr. Anastassia Kuldmaa, member of the Tallinn Dental Clinic and the Estonian Dental Association board.

Experiences from other countries show, Kuldmaa said, that tooth‑brushing under the supervision of a responsible adult is very effective and strongly supports oral hygiene at home.

A fresh study was published, tracking 600 five‑year‑olds across Estonia. "Children were selected by kindergarten groups. The results have gotten slightly worse compared to the 2018 study. Simple counseling is not enough — changing behavior is very difficult. An adult who does not brush carefully themselves will not monitor the child's brushing to ensure the full two minutes."

Hambahari Autor/allikas: pexels free

Dentists have decided to step in to help children. "Two‑thirds of five‑year‑olds need dental treatment. Children snack too much, there is too much food around us, it is too tempting and too easily accessible. At home, not enough attention is paid to removing dental plaque," the dentist noted.

A child mirrors the home — reflecting the family's behavior patterns in eating, hygiene, and everything else. "Supervised tooth‑brushing, which we hope to expand to all kindergartens, would become a mandatory part of the educational program, just like hand‑washing and basic hygiene practices. We help parents by taking tooth‑brushing partly out of their control, because a child cannot be responsible for whether their mother or father considers oral hygiene important. Since we cannot reach every home to stand beside the child, kindergartens will have an additional brushing session where the teacher supervises two minutes of brushing and ensures the toothbrush actually stays in the mouth for those two minutes. This produces wonderful results."

In Scotland, they managed within ten years to get practically all children brushing their teeth in kindergarten, and children's dental treatment costs dropped nearly threefold. "England has now adopted the same system, and they already see a downward trend," Kuldmaa said.

Kindergartens have generally given positive feedback. "We provide all toothbrushes, stickers, toothbrush holders — the teacher only needs to follow the instructions, and usually they do. Sometimes parents intervene, worrying that a third brushing might wear down the teeth too much. Overall, we receive very positive feedback."

A toothbrush should be replaced every three months, or earlier if the bristles become frayed. "I recommend an electric toothbrush — it makes brushing easier. Teeth should ideally be brushed half an hour after eating, but the important thing is to brush at all, and if that's not possible, brushing immediately after eating is fine. On rushed mornings, brushing before breakfast is a good option," the dentist noted.

Teeth need rest, and the biggest problem right now is snacking. "Three hours between meals, and during the break only plain water — not cucumber water or berry water. In the evening, the toothbrush should be the last thing that goes into the mouth."

World.title: Estonia sends new border guard rotation to Latvia
World.content:
A new unit of Estonian border guards was sent to Latvia at the start of the week to combat illegal migration and protect the European Union's external border.

The new ESTPOL11 rotation replaced the team who have been working in Latvia for the last two weeks.

The 11-member team will take part in border patrols in areas where migration pressure is highest. Estonia has sent officers, service dogs, drones and other specialised equipment.

Last month, Veiko Kommusaar, deputy director general of the Police and Border Guard Board, said Estonia will continue supporting Latvia because migration pressure in the region remains high.

He said that Latvian authorities have prevented more than 9,000 illegal border-crossing attempts this year.

"Our aim is to prevent a temporary migration route from developing into a permanent one. To this end, we are taking part in border patrols on the Latvian-Belarusian border together with our Latvian colleagues to prevent illegal border crossings, while at the same time working to ensure that people who have entered Estonia illegally are returned and that people smugglers and their accomplices are caught," Kommusaar said.

World.title: A look back at Estonia's presidential elections | Episode 6: Kersti Kaljulaid, 2016
World.content:
Estonia's 2016 presidential election became an unprecedented political deadlock, with failed votes in both the Riigikogu and Electoral College ultimately paving the way for compromise candidate Kersti Kaljulaid.

The 2016 presidential election was unusual in that, after unsuccessful rounds in both the Riigikogu and the Electoral College, the election returned to the Riigikogu.

As with this year's presidential election, when several people were put forward as candidates through public initiatives or put themselves forward, there was also a significant number of such prospective candidates ahead of the 2016 election. Names floated during the presidential race included Ilvi Jõe-Cannon, Kaur Kender, Jaak Jõerüüt and Kristiina Ojuland, among others.

The first round of the presidential election was held in the Riigikogu on August 29. A total of 99 MPs took part in the vote; Center Party MP Rein Ratas was absent for health reasons. Three candidates were nominated: Mailis Reps, Allar Jõks and Eiki Nestor.

First round of the 2016 presidential election in the Riigikogu. Source: ERR archival footage

Nestor, the joint candidate of the Social Democratic Party (SDE) and the Reform Party, received 40 votes; Center Party candidate Reps received 26 votes; and Allar Jõks, the joint candidate of IRL and the Free Party, received 25 votes. As none of the candidates secured the required two-thirds majority of all Riigikogu members — at least 68 votes — no president was elected in the first round and a second round was called.

The second round of the presidential election was held a day later, on August 30. The Social Democrats and Reform Party now nominated Siim Kallas as their candidate. Reps and Jõks ran again. Kallas received 45 votes, Reps 32 and Jõks 21. As a result, no president was elected in the second round either and a third round was held the same day.

Only the names of the two candidates who received the most votes in the second round — Siim Kallas and Mailis Reps — could appear on the ballot in the third Riigikogu round. Kallas received 42 votes and Reps 26. As many as 30 ballots were left blank. As neither candidate secured sufficient support in the third round, the Riigikogu failed to elect a president and the Electoral College was convened.

'It was clear by late May that the Riigikogu rounds would fail'

Eiki Nestor (SDE), then speaker of the Riigikogu and himself a presidential candidate in the first Riigikogu round, said no one was under any illusion that any candidate could secure the necessary support in the Riigikogu.

"It was clear by around the end of May that the election in the Riigikogu would most likely fail," Nestor said.

According to Nestor, the parliamentary groups were unable to agree on a presidential candidate who could attract cross-party support. "Reform Party parliamentary group chair Urve Tiidus said that Reform had two good candidates — which one do you support? At that point, it was clear that nothing would come of it. There wasn't even an attempt to find a candidate who could get 68 votes," Nestor said.

"The first Riigikogu round was essentially a mandatory round. It would have looked extremely bad if there had been no candidates. All three of us had already spent the summer traveling around Estonia, knowing that we weren't going to be elected and we still had to take part in that round," Nestor said.

Two Reform Party candidates

Annika Arras, who worked on Siim Kallas' campaign for the Reform Party, said the party was internally divided at the time and then-Foreign Minister Marina Kaljurand was also seen as a potential presidential candidate. Kaljurand, now a Social Democrat, had been brought into politics by then-Prime Minister Taavi Rõivas.

Polls showed Kaljurand was the most popular candidate among the public. She proposed that Kallas run first in the Riigikogu, but later resigned as foreign minister and was formally nominated as a presidential candidate for the Electoral College with 26 signatures of support.

The second round of the presidential election in the Riigikogu. Siim Kallas, seen from behind, speaks to reporters. Source: Ülo Josing / ERR

"It was a somewhat difficult time within the Reform Party. They simply couldn't reach an agreement. It was as though they decided to give both candidates a chance and let the better one win, but at the same time that split the votes. There were teams made up of people from the same party, but backing different candidates. That certainly created a problem," Arras said.

Arras recalled that at the time, the Reform Party had been in power for 17 consecutive years and held all the key positions in the country, which meant other parties did not want Reform to secure the presidency as well. "To get the presidency on top of all that may simply have been too much in the context of the time," Arras said.

Arras also recalled that the campaign began very early. Siim Kallas' candidacy was already public knowledge in early April, five months before the first round of voting in the Riigikogu. Other candidates launched their campaigns fairly soon afterward.

The Electoral College convened for its first round on September 24.

Five candidates were nominated in the first round. Kallas and Reps were placed on the Electoral College ballot based on the results of the third round of voting in the Riigikogu. Marina Kaljurand, Mart Helme and Allar Jõks were also nominated.

In the first round, Allar Jõks received 83 votes, Siim Kallas 81, Mailis Reps 79, Marina Kaljurand 75 and Mart Helme 16. A total of 334 electors received ballots, meaning at least 168 votes were needed to win. All five candidates fell well short of that threshold and a second round of the Electoral College vote was called, with the two candidates who received the most votes in the first round advancing.

Second Electoral College round of the 2016 presidential election. Source: ERR archival footage

Politicians were fairly open about the fact that Center Party Chair Edgar Savisaar had backed Kallas rather than his own party's candidate, Reps, in the first round. Several Center Party members themselves also acknowledged this.

Infighting at Center gives Kallas the edge

At the time, there was fierce rivalry between different camps within the Center Party and Mailis Reps had supported Kadri Simson who ran against Edgar Savisaar at the Center Party congress that same year. Reps had also defeated Savisaar, who had likewise sought to become the party's presidential candidate, in a secret ballot of the party council. The internal power struggle ultimately led to Savisaar's ouster, Jüri Ratas becoming Center Party chair and, in turn, a change in the governing coalition.

Jaak Aab, who worked on Reps' campaign at the time, said Savisaar publicly expressed support for Reps during the campaign but worked against her behind the scenes.

"In the first round of the Electoral College, he [Savisaar] delivered 10 to 15 votes from his loyal supporters to Siim Kallas. It was immediately apparent and widely known because Siim Kallas was the first person to rush from the Electoral College at the Estonia Concert Hall to Center Party headquarters to thank Edgar," Aab said.

Siim Kallas meeting Center Party MPs. Source: Reform Party

According to Aab, Reps would have won the first round had those votes not gone to Kallas.

Aab said Savisaar's actions also meant that Reps' supporters did not subsequently rally behind Siim Kallas, even though Center Party members considered him a worthy candidate. "The political game Edgar played eliminated any chance of a president being elected by the Electoral College," Aab said.

Martin Kukk, who was part of Siim Kallas' campaign team, said he had no factual information indicating that Savisaar had arranged votes for Kallas. "I am, however, convinced that many people from other parties supported Siim Kallas' candidacy simply because they personally liked him as a presidential candidate," Kukk said.

The two candidates who received the most votes in the first round, Allar Jõks and Siim Kallas, advanced to the second round. Kallas received 138 votes and Jõks 134. There were 57 unmarked ballots and three invalid ballots.

As 333 electors received ballots, at least 167 votes were needed to elect a president. Neither Kallas nor Jõks reached that threshold.

Enters Kersti Kaljulaid

After the rounds of voting in both the Riigikogu and the Electoral College failed to produce a president, there was widespread public condemnation of the entire presidential election process. People were angry that those in power had failed to accomplish the task before them. This also put greater pressure on MPs to finally find a candidate who could secure broad cross-party support.

Eiki Nestor said that after the election returned to the Riigikogu, the Riigikogu's Council of Elders met the following Monday to discuss various potential presidential candidates, including some who had been considered previously. Kersti Kaljulaid's name was among them. "It became clear that if anyone had a chance of getting 68 votes in the Riigikogu, it was Kersti Kaljulaid," Nestor said.

Kersti Kaljulaid during the 2016 presidential election in the Riigikogu. Source: Siim Lõvi /ERR

"I called her on Monday and invited her to the Riigikogu building on Tuesday to arrange possible meetings. Time was short. At that point, she was the longest-serving Estonian member of the European Court of Auditors and was standing in for the departing head of the court, so she had to return to Luxembourg to carry out her duties there," Nestor said.

Nestor said politicians with government experience knew Kaljulaid well. "She had become very well known across different parties as an active and constructive adviser to Prime Minister Mart Laar. I don't remember anyone saying that their party knew nothing about her. There was no one like that," Nestor said.

Annika Arras likewise said Kaljulaid's previous work as an adviser to Mart Laar had demonstrated her intelligence, resourcefulness and strong character, creating confidence that she understood governance and responsibility and had sufficient substance and determination of her own. "That was probably also why a compromise could be reached at all, because the candidate was strong enough," Arras said.

According to Martin Kukk, the upheaval within the Center Party also helped pave the way for Kersti Kaljulaid's election as president.

"The change of leadership within the Center Party made the party a viable coalition partner. That, in turn, meant that the parties that later formed a government without the Reform Party were also able to agree among themselves on a presidential candidate," Kukk said.

The election resumed in the Riigikogu on October 3, with just one candidate nominated: Kersti Kaljulaid. Kaljulaid received 81 votes for, which remains the highest number of votes ever cast for a presidential candidate in the Riigikogu.

Kaljulaid took the oath of office before the Riigikogu on October 10, 2016. She was 46 at the time, making her the youngest of Estonia's presidents upon taking office.

The presidential handover ceremony in the Riigikogu. Kersti Kaljulaid takes the oath of office in 2016. Source: ERR/Ülo Josing

World.title: Iraq weighs oil-backed U.S. bank loan to tackle liquidity shortfall
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi government is preparing to formally engage official U.S. banking institutions to secure an emergency sovereign loan facility backed by future crude oil export revenues, an informed official source disclosed to local news agencies.

The financing initiative is designed as a rapid intervention to bridge expanding state cash-flow deficits and secure public sector payroll obligations without resorting to domestic currency printing.

Financing Structure & Diplomatic Coordination

Inter-Ministerial Formulation: The Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs are coordinating the joint terms of engagement to present formal loan requests to designated American banking institutions.

Oil Revenue Collateral: Debt-service installments and loan principal repayments are structured to be settled directly from Iraq’s international crude sales proceeds in global energy markets.

Inflation Prevention Policy: Securing foreign currency credit provides an alternative to unbacked domestic monetary expansion, mitigating risks of dinar devaluation and consumer price inflation.

Emergency Legislative Framework

To implement the credit facility, the executive branch is finalizing specialized fiscal legislation for parliamentary ratification:

Draft Borrowing Law: The proposed Borrowing, Grants, and Subsidies Law serves as a statutory spending bridge to sustain vital state operations in the absence of a comprehensive annual budget framework.

Parliamentary Finance Committee Review: Lawmakers are awaiting the official submission of the cabinet’s draft bill to establish clear spending ceilings, debt sustainability parameters, and compliance with national fiscal targets.

Key Macroeconomic & Monetary Indicators

Indicator Metric / Trend Economic Impact Monetary Base (M0) – May 2026 113.560 Trillion IQD Expanded by 13.761T IQD (+13.8%) since Dec 2025 Primary Cash Outlay Drivers Civil service salaries & core operating expenses Rapid depletion of available treasury cash reserves Target Financing Mechanism Oil-collateralized U.S. credit line Restores liquidity without inflating domestic money supply

The decision to pursue external commercial borrowing underscores Baghdad’s focus on maintaining monetary discipline amid regional geopolitical volatility and oil price fluctuations.

By utilizing structured sovereign credit instead of domestic quantitative easing, the Ministry of Finance aims to preserve liquidity reserves, meet mandatory salary disbursements on schedule, and protect the exchange value of the Iraqi Dinar.

World.title: Iraq ranks 61st globally in PPP minimum wage at $626: Report
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq ranks 61st globally out of 130 countries in monthly minimum wage adjusted for Purchasing Power Parity (PPP), recording $626 per month, according to an international comparative index published by Visual Capitalist.

The ranking adjusts statutory wage baselines to account for local price levels, subsidized consumer baskets, and relative costs of living across economies, providing an accurate metric of real purchasing capacity rather than nominal dollar conversions.

Global and Regional Comparative Standings

Iraq placed in the upper-middle tier of the 130-nation survey, closely outpacing emerging and regional economies:

Adjacent Global Peers: Iraq ($626/mo) marginally led South Africa (62nd at $620/mo) and Guyana (63rd at $619/mo).

Regional & Major Economy Comparisons: Iraq recorded higher real purchasing capacity at the baseline wage floor than China (73rd at $544/mo) and Tunisia (77th at $513/mo).

Global Leaders:Switzerland led the index with a PPP-adjusted minimum wage of $3,804 per month, followed by Germany, the United Kingdom, and the Netherlands, while the United States ranked 25th at $1,257 per month.

Lower-Tier Rankings: Developing economies at the base of the index included Niger (121st at $196/mo), Ghana (127th at $100/mo), and Gambia (130th at $67/mo).

Global Minimum Wage Rankings (PPP-Adjusted Monthly USD)

Rank Country Monthly Minimum Wage (PPP USD) Economic Context 1 Switzerland $3,804 Global highest wage floor — Germany / UK / Netherlands Upper Tier High productivity & social wage floors 25 United States $1,257 Federal baseline minimum wage ($7.25/hr) 61 Iraq $626 Upper-middle tier; leading regional peers 62 South Africa $620 Major emerging market peer 63 Guyana $619 Expanding energy-driven economy 73 China $544 Baseline regional statutory wage average 77 Tunisia $513 North African comparison 121 Niger $196 Sub-Saharan baseline 127 Ghana $100 Lower-tier wage floor 130 Gambia $67 Lowest ranking among 130 surveyed nations

The $626 PPP valuation reflects how local price subsidies, utility price caps, and domestic living costs expand the real-term domestic purchasing capacity of Iraq’s statutory minimum wage (nominally set at 350,000 IQD per month by the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs).

While nominal conversion rates place Iraq’s minimum wage near $268 USD, purchasing power adjustments demonstrate that baseline earners retain greater domestic absorption capacity than several larger industrial peers where basic living expenses and utility tariffs are considerably higher.

World.title: Iraq’s Zidane Iqbal signs with Blackburn Rovers from FC Utrecht
World.content:
Lancashire (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi international midfielder Zidane Iqbal has finalized a permanent transfer to English Championship side Blackburn Rovers, arriving from Dutch Eredivisie club FC Utrecht ahead of the close of the European summer transfer window.

The 23-year-old playmaker is scheduled to travel to England on Wednesday to complete medical evaluations and formalize contractual paperwork before integrating into the first-team squad at Ewood Park.

Player Profile & Career Trajectory

Manchester United Academy Roots: Developed through Manchester United’s youth academy system, where he made history as the first British-South Asian player to appear for the club’s senior team in the UEFA Champions League.

Dutch Eredivisie Spell: Joined FC Utrecht in 2023, gaining valuable European top-flight experience and refining his transitional passing and tactical distribution.

International Pillar: A core playmaker for the Iraqi national team (Lions of Mesopotamia), representing Iraq across World Cup qualifiers and the AFC Asian Cup.

Return to English Football: Iqbal’s move to the EFL Championship provides a central platform to secure consistent starting minutes in a fast-paced, high-intensity league system.

Historical Profile: Blackburn Rovers FC

Characteristic Detail / Historic Record Founding Year 1888 (One of the 12 founding members of the English Football League) Home Ground Ewood Park, Blackburn, Lancashire (Capacity: ~31,367) Premier League Title 1994–1995 Champions (Managed by Kenny Dalglish; led by Alan Shearer and Chris Sutton) Major Honours 6x FA Cup Winners, 1x Football League Cup Winner, Multiple UEFA Cup / Europa League campaigns

Iqbal’s transition to Blackburn Rovers reinforces the presence of Iraqi talent across tier-one and tier-two European football leagues.

By competing regularly in the 46-game EFL Championship calendar, Iqbal aims to elevate his physical match tempo and tactical leadership, directly benefiting Iraq’s national team as they navigate crucial competitive windows in Asian and international fixtures.

World.title: Iraq launches 1M residential plot drive, unlocks $15B in refinery savings
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Chief of Staff of the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office, Ihsan Al-Awadi, announced on Tuesday, September 1, 2026, the official on-the-ground launch of a sovereign initiative to distribute one million serviced residential land plots to Iraqi families who do not own property, under the direct directive of Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi.

In a video statement received by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Al-Awadi also revealed that the government has enacted structural economic reforms within the Iraqi Oil Refining Company during its first 100 days, projecting annual federal budget savings of approximately $15 billion.

Core Pillars: Housing Initiative & Fiscal Savings

1,000,000 Serviced Residential Plots: Targeted exclusively at low-income and propertyless citizens across Iraqi governorates to alleviate housing shortages and urban overcrowding.

300,000 Plots Prepared: Over the administration’s initial 100-day window, government teams finalized site surveying, legal allocations, and infrastructural planning for 300,000 residential plots, which are now ready for allocation.

September 1 Ground Launch: Implementation and field execution officially commenced on September 1, fulfilling cabinet directives framed as a “national project for every citizen.”

$15 Billion Annual Budget Savings: Implementation of a modernized economic operating model for the state-owned refining sector, designed in collaboration with Ministry of Oil economists and engineers, which optimizes operational efficiency without affecting employee salaries, bonuses, or entitlements.

Key Milestone Breakdown

Milestone / Policy File Target Scope Current Achievement / Projected Impact Land Distribution Initiative 1,000,000 Plots nationwide 300,000 plots fully demarcated and serviced within 100 days Target Demographic Propertyless Iraqi households Direct land title allocations for home construction Refining Economic Model State refinery operations ~$15 Billion/year saved for the federal budget Workforce Protection Ministry of Oil personnel Zero cuts to wages, allowances, or baseline benefits

Al-Awadi emphasized that expedited cabinet resolutions and executive decision-making under Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s direct supervision enabled municipal and oil sector bodies to reach these milestones within the administration’s first 100 days.

By linking high-volume residential land grants with fiscal efficiency gains in downstream oil refining, the government seeks to direct newly unlocked state liquidity toward municipal services, road networks, and utilities required for the newly demarcated residential zones.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate increases against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced an increase on Monday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,541.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,540 Iraqi dinars on Sunday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,545 Iraqi dinars and 1,535 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate increased, fluctuating between 1,541.5 and 1,541 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraqi judiciary sentences kidnapper of US journalist to 15 years in prison
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Central Criminal Court sentenced Amir Rahim Jabar Lazim, a member of the Iran-backed group Kataeb Hezbollah, to 15 years in prison under the country’s anti-terrorism law for kidnapping US journalist Shelly Kittleson on March 31.

Kittleson was kidnapped during the daytime on Saadoun Street in central Baghdad. Armed gunmen pushed her into a silver vehicle, while another getaway car crashed during the escape. Iraqi security forces intercepted the crashed car and arrested Lazim.

The US journalist was kept hostage for more than a week when Kataeb Hezbollah freed her in early April ahead of a US-Iran ceasefire.

Kittleson, who has extensively covered the Middle East for publications like the BBC and Politico, expressed her gratitude to the Iraqi justice system on X and affirmed her right to seek compensation.

This decision marks a rare court step against a major, Tehran-aligned armed group in Iraq.

The verdict comes at a critical time for Iraq’s new government, led by Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, which is under intense pressure from Washington to disarm pro-Iran militias and place all weapons under strict state control.

The effort to disarm Kataeb Hezbollah has pushed Iraq into a severe security and political crisis, as the group has rejected the government’s disarmament mandates and vowed to expand its military arsenal.

World.title: Iraq discusses oil and gas development with BP, ConocoPhillips
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair and representatives from British Petroleum (BP) and Texas-based ConocoPhillips discussed on Monday the development of Iraq’s oil and gas industry.

The meeting held in Baghdad included BP’s Iraq director Zaid al-Yasiri, Nader Zaki, Ariel Flores, and ConocoPhillips representative William Arnold, as well as senior Iraqi officials in the oil sector.

The discussions addressed strategic advancements to maximize the utilization of Iraq’s hydrocarbon resources, optimize field development, and upgrade extraction technologies, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The Iraqi Oil Ministry activated in early August its Kirkuk oilfield contract with BP, a project aiming to elevate crude oil production from its current capacity of 320,000 barrels per day to a peak target of 420,000 barrels per day.

The deal expands crude extraction while capturing associated gas to eliminate gas flaring and provide fuel for power plants.

The activation of the Kirkuk project represents a major step in Iraq’s broader energy strategy to achieve natural gas self-sufficiency and reduce reliance on imported fuel.

ConocoPhillips has agreed to purchase a 42 percent share in BP’s Kirkuk project, boosting its position in Iraq by redeveloping four key oil resources in the northern Iraqi province.

ConocoPhillips Chairman Ryan Lance said that the investment aligns with the company’s conservative approach by offering access to a big, high-quality, and long-life resource base while needing very little expenditure.

The agreement represents another initiative by Iraq to attract foreign investments and boost production from its aging oil assets, as well as to strengthen partnerships with prominent global energy companies.

World.title: India to receive first Iraqi oil shipment in five months
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – India is preparing to receive its first shipment of Iraqi oil in five months, a development reflecting the return of Iraq’s crude oil flows to one of Asia’s largest oil markets, despite ongoing shipping challenges across the Strait of Hormuz.

India’s Bharat Petroleum expects to receive the shipment within the next few days. The tanker carrying Iraqi oil has already passed through the Strait of Hormuz and arrived in Fujairah, UAE, for a ship-to-ship transfer, according to Reuters.

Bharat Petroleum’s Chief Financial Officer, Vetsa Ramakrishna Gupta, said that the company secured a vessel to load the Iraqi shipment and transport it to Fujairah. There, the oil will be transferred from ship to ship before reaching the company’s refineries.

These arrangements reflect the efforts of Asian refiners to find flexible logistical solutions for securing crude oil at a time when transportation cost, insurance, and tanker availability have become crucial factors in determining the viability of purchasing shipments from the Gulf region.

The Indian company typically requires around two million barrels of Iraqi oil per month, making a consistent supply from Baghdad crucial to meeting its refinery’s crude oil needs.

Bharat Petroleum has not disclosed the name of the vessel used to transport the shipment but stated that the ship’s owner agreed to load the crude and proceed to Fujairah for a ship-to-ship transfer.

Iraq is one of the countries most affected by disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz, given that a significant portion of its oil exports depend on ports located on the Arabian Gulf.

World.title: OBC creamy layer status: Supreme Court agrees to hear Centre's plea against parents' income-only criteria
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

on Tuesday agreed to hear the Centre's plea challenging the retrospective application of its ruling that parents' income cannot be the sole criterion for determining the creamy layer among Other Backward Classes (OBC) candidates.

Also read:

The ruling had held that the status and category of a parent's job must also be considered, along with the Income/Wealth Test, while determining whether a candidate should be excluded from OBC reservation.

The matter concerns the criteria used to determine the creamy layer, which identifies relatively advanced sections among OBCs who are excluded from the benefits of reservation.

More details awaited.

World.title: NMC opens eligibility certificate window for FMGE aspirants from Sept 1
World.content:
NMC opens FMGE Eligibility Certificate portal from September 1 to 30. Photo credit: IANS

NEW DELHI: The National Medical Commission (NMC) will open its online portal for applications for the Eligibility Certificate (EC) for Foreign Medical Graduate Examination (FMGE) aspirants from 10 am on September 1 to 6 pm on September 30, giving candidates who have not yet obtained the certificate an opportunity to apply.The EC is mandatory for candidates required to appear for the FMGE. The NMC has said candidates without an Eligibility Certificate issued by the commission will not be permitted to apply for the screening test. The next FMGE may be scheduled by the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) in the coming months.The NMC, in its public notice and advisory, has advised candidates to carefully verify all details against their original documents before submitting their applications. It has also cautioned candidates against using proxies and advised them to keep their documents ready before beginning the application process.Candidates have been asked to provide an active mobile number so that any deficiency in their application can be communicated promptly. The commission has advised applicants to rectify any deficiency at the earliest to avoid delays in processing.For queries regarding the status of an application, candidates must mention the File Tracking Number generated at the time of submission. The NMC said no response would be sent in the absence of the File Tracking Number.Candidates who have already submitted an application for the Eligibility Certificate to the NMC in the past need not apply again, the commission clarified.

World.title: WHO revises typhoid vaccine advice
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Nearly 5 million typhoid cases were estimated in India in 2023, with children bearing much of the burden. Amid rising antibiotic resistance, the World Health Organization (WHO) has updated its guidance on typhoid conjugate vaccine (TCV), recommending the first dose at 9-24 months in settings with high or very high typhoid incidence.

A Lancet Regional Health â Southeast Asia study estimated 4.9 million cases, 7.3 lakh hospitalisations and 7,850 deaths from typhoid in India in 2023. About 6 lakh, or 82%, of hospitalisations were linked to fluoroquinolone-resistant typhoid.

Children accounted for most estimated treated cases, with those aged 5-9 years accounting for 36%, followed by 10-14 years at 27% and 6 months to 4 years at 25%.

âGiven Indiaâs very high typhoid burden and the emergence of drug-resistant Salmonella Typhi, including reports of carbapenem-resistant strains, routine introduction of TCV is justified and urgent.

NTAGIâs 2022 recommendations and repeated cost-effectiveness analyses already support this,â said Dr Kamini Walia, senior scientist at ICMR.

She said India could consider giving TCV at the existing 18-month vaccination visit, alongside the second measles-containing vaccine dose. âEven as a single dose without a booster, TCV is expected to have a significant impact on disease burden. A school-entry booster, particularly in high-burden urban areas, may be considered if surveillance shows waning protection,â she said.





WHO recommends TCV in settings with high or very high typhoid incidence, high case-fatality rates or a high burden of antimicrobial-resistant Salmonella Typhi. It also recommends catch-up vaccination when TCV is introduced, with children below 15 years potentially targeted depending on local disease burden and programme feasibility.

On booster doses, WHO says countries with very high typhoid incidence should consider a booster around five years after the first dose given at 9-24 months.

In high-incidence settings, a booster may be considered if there is evidence that protection is waning. Decisions should take into account disease burden, antimicrobial resistance, cost-effectiveness and feasibility.

The updated advice comes amid growing concern over antibiotic-resistant typhoid, which can limit treatment options and increase reliance on more expensive injectable or last-resort drugs.

TCV is not a new WHO recommendation. The agency recommended its routine use in children in typhoid-endemic countries in 2017 and prequalified the first vaccine in 2018. The latest guidance updates recommendations based on newer evidence, including vaccination age, catch-up programmes and booster use.

For India, the issue is particularly relevant. The study notes that the National Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation (NTAGI) recommended including TCV in the Universal Immunisation Programme in 2022.

WHO also stresses that vaccination cannot replace basic measures such as safe water, sanitation, hygiene, food safety and timely diagnosis and treatment, which remain essential to controlling typhoid.

World.title: India's GDP growth: BJP hails 'economic resilience'; Congress asks where are the jobs?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The BJP and Congress on Tuesday traded sharply contrasting assessments of Indiaâs economy after official data showed GDP growth of 7.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 quarter.

While the BJP hailed the performance as evidence of resilient economic management, the Opposition questioned whether the growth has translated into jobs, higher incomes and wider prosperity.

BJP leader Ravi Shankar Prasad held a press conference where he described the latest growth figures as âparticularly significantâ. He argued that India had expanded rapidly despite heightened geopolitical and economic uncertainty during the quarter, including the Gulf crisis, disruptions to oil supplies and supply-chain pressures.

âToday is a very encouraging day. The latest report shows that Indiaâs GDP growth stood at 7.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 quarter. The figure of 7.8 per cent is particularly significant because, during this period, the Gulf crisis had intensified. There were concerns over oil supplies, disruptions in supply chains, and uncertainty across the global economy. Despite all these challenges, Indiaâs economy grew by 7.8 per cent,â Prasad said at a press conference in Delhi.





Prasad also compared Indiaâs performance with growth recorded by several other major economies, saying Canada grew by around 1.5 per cent, Germany by 1 per cent, the UK by 2.1 per cent, Malaysia by about 6 per cent, South Korea by around 3.7 per cent and the US by roughly 2 per cent during the same period.

He attributed Indiaâs performance to what he called effective economic management and praised Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs leadership.

âToday, I would like to congratulate and commend Indiaâs economic management. I also wholeheartedly congratulate the honourable Prime Minister for his vision, wisdom and leadership,â Prasad said.

The Congress, however, challenged the BJPâs interpretation of the GDP figures, arguing that headline growth alone does not adequately capture the economic conditions faced by ordinary Indians.

Congress leader Pawan Khera questioned how the 7.8 per cent growth figure was benefiting young people and farmers, while also pointing to concerns over employment, manufacturing, education and income distribution.

âThe Prime Minister comes up with a reel, a video. Ask him: the largest demographic in this country is the youth. How does this GDP growth affect the youth? How does it address the issues that young people face? The largest occupation in this country is agriculture. How does this GDP growth affect the agricultural sector? If it doesnât benefit these two sectors, how does it affect the dwindling manufacturing sector? Look at the manufacturing data.

So, what is he even talking about? A handful of people contribute to the growth of this country, but where is the redistribution of income? Where is the distribution of income? So, letâs talk about these fundamental issues. 80 per cent of this country depends on free ration. Is that what good GDP growth does for the country? Thatâs our question.â

Khera had earlier taken his criticism to X, arguing that a single quarter of strong GDP growth should not be treated as evidence of broad-based economic prosperity.

âOne quarter of 7.8% growth is not an economic spring. If India has truly "bloomed," why do rampant unemployment, leaked exam papers, and a crumbling education system define the ground reality? Why is the republic's prosperity not translating into the prosperity of its public? GDP measures national output - not jobs, not wages, not opportunity. If it measured any of those, the future of India's youth would not look so bleak.

Modi can manage his headlines. For India's youth, the question remains the same as ever: Where are the jobs?â

At his press conference, Khera also questioned whether the strong GDP reading had resulted in tangible improvements in the cost of living and employment conditions.

âOn one hand, they say, "Look at the GDP of a single quarter and applaud." On the other, they say, "Don't buy gold, don't host lavish weddings." They themselves sit abroad while telling the country's citizens not to travel overseas and to save money.

80% of the population relies on free rations, but keep applauding... Regarding this 7.8% figureâwhat benefit is the country's largest sector, agriculture, deriving from it? The youth constitute the country's largest demographic; what benefit are they getting? Have their issues been resolved? Have milk prices dropped? Is there no longer a need for free rations? Have you rectified the employment situation to reverse the 45-year record low? Is manufacturing back on track? What happened to the MSME sector? What happened to the unorganized sector? If you have answers showing a positive outcome, then we, too, will applaud.

..â

The competing responses underline the political divide over how India's economic performance should be assessed. While the BJP has used the 7.8 per cent quarterly expansion to highlight India's relative resilience amid global disruptions, the Congress has focused on whether headline GDP growth is being reflected in employment, household incomes and opportunities for India's young population.

World.title: CJP calls off Sept 5 march after SC quashes all FIRs against protesters on Centre's request
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party on Tuesday withdrew its call for a march on September 5 after

, on the Centre's request, quashed all FIRs registered across the country against students who participated in the NEET protests.

"I want to state that in view of the positive assurances of the government of India and the judicial sanctity bestowed upon them today, and in view of the order being passed by this court, the

deems it appropriate to withdraw the call for the march on September 5 and looks forward to compliance with today's order," CJP co-convener Sourav Das said during a hearing in the Supreme Court.

This comes after Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Centre and Delhi Police, informed the apex court that the Centre remains committed to fulfilling all three assurances given to the leadership of CJP during the meeting between the Centre and the party.

What were the three assurances

The first assurance was that the Centre would not pursue FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25.

The second assurance was that no fresh FIRs would be registered in connection with the matter.

The third assurance was that the government would pay compensation to students who died by suicide allegedly in connection with the NEET paper leak.

"Centre is committed to honour the assurance given to the CJP leaders to provide compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after NEET exam cancellation; however, 3 months needed to work out the modalities," Mehta told

.





"As of now, we are committed to fulfilling all three assurances," he added.

Earlier on Monday, Centre moved the apex court seeking to quash FIR's registered against the student protesters with alleged violence during protests over the NEET paper leak in Delhi and other states.

Solicitor general Tushar Mehta mentioned the plea before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday, seeking the courtâs intervention in the matter.

The Centre has urged the Supreme Court to exercise its extraordinary powers under Article 142 of the Constitution to quash the FIRs registered against the protesting students.

Why CJP had called for Sept 5 march

CJP had called for a protest march in Delhi on September 5, Teachers' Day. It had accused the Centre of failing to honour the promises made on July 25 to persuade the group to withdraw its 36-day agitation against irregularities in exams and the NEET paper leak.

World.title: Indian consulate in UAE issues warning over biometric fraud targeting nationals
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The consulate general of India in Dubai has warned Indian nationals in the UAE, particularly blue-collar workers, against handing over biometric data. The warning advised the workers against unauthorised agents claiming to help with visa regularisation, Emergency Certificates, Exit Permits, Emirates IDs or employment, after reports of fraud involving the misuse of fingerprints and facial scans.

In an advisory issued on Monday, the consulate said it had received information about individuals and agents allegedly exploiting Indians seeking assistance with immigration and documentation procedures. The fraudsters reportedly ask victims to provide fingerprints or face scans, which can then be used without their knowledge to conduct financial transactions, open bank accounts or obtain loans and credit cards in their names.

The consulate cautioned that such misuse could leave victims liable for financial obligations or transactions they did not authorise. In some cases, those affected could also face multiple fines, travel bans and even imprisonment.

The advisory urged nationals not to share their passports, Emirates IDs, biometric data, including eye, face or fingerprint scans, or personal and financial credentials with unauthorised individuals or agencies under any circumstances.





It also clarified that biometric information required for procedures such as exit permits, Emirates IDs or visa regularisation must be provided only at official UAE Government facilities or counters. People were specifically warned against submitting such information through private individuals, agents or third-party service providers claiming to be authorised by UAE authorities.

The consulate also sought to dispel a potential source of confusion by stating that biometric information is not required for certain consular services.

The advisory said the Consulate General of India in Dubai and the Embassy of India in Abu Dhabi "DO NOT require any fingerprint scan or face/eye scan from applicants for the issuance of a passport or emergency certificate."

It warned that any person or agent demanding such information while claiming to represent the Indian Embassy or consulate would be engaging in fraudulent activity and should not be entertained.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Indians approached by unauthorised individuals seeking biometric data or Emirates IDs have been advised to contact the Pravasi Bharatiya Sahayata Kendra through the toll-free number 80046342, WhatsApp or SMS at 00971543090571, or email pbsk.dubai@mea.gov.in to verify credentials or seek assistance.

The consulate urged Indian nationals living in or visiting the UAE to exercise caution, independently verify the credentials of anyone offering immigration or documentation-related services, and report suspicious activity to the Indian consulate and the relevant UAE authorities.

World.title: Flyers asked to give handwriting samples after threat note causes Air India Express international flight to divert
World.content:
Representative image (PTI photo)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian security establishment have finally decided to take the menace of hoax bomb threats that cause expensive diversions head on. An Air India Express Dammam-Delhi nonstop was forced to divert to Ahmedabad after a tissue paper with the words âbomb red 430â written on it and a box, both in black ink, drawn on it was found in the lav. After landing in Ahmedabad and following the required protocol, the security authorities additionally decided to conduct a handwriting test on all the 32 passengers and see if the expensive prank was played by one of them.âThey asked the airline to give the same tissue paper and then organised the same colour pen. Six tissues were sought for each passenger. Now let us see if they find a match,â said sources. It is not yet known if this test managed to nab the person who allegedly wrote this threat note.The standard protocol for such situations is taking the aircraft to a remote parking bay; checking all passengers and cabin and check-in baggage thoroughly before clearing it to take off again. All this was followed on Monday too at Ahmedabad. The handwriting test was conducted on top of that.An Air India Express spokesperson said: âOne of our flights from Dammam to Delhi was diverted to Ahmedabad as a precaution and in keeping with security protocols after being notified of a specific bomb threat.The government-appointed bomb threat assessment committee (BTAC) was alerted immediately, and all security procedures promptly initiated. The flight landed and all guests have been disembarked safely. The aircraft will be released for operations after necessary security checks are completed.âIndian carriers have suffered huge losses due to hoax threats in recent years. While tracking a call making such a claim is difficult due to advancement in technology, tackling on board threatening notes if written by someone onboard the affected flight could help tackle this menace. Mondayâs handwriting test decision, say sources, was taken by BCAS and CISF. âWhy the same has not been done in the past beats us,â said a senior pilot.Airlines and airports in India had received 999 hoax bomb threats between Jan 1 and Nov 14, 2024 â more than 10 times the number in 2023. The threats to both domestic and international flights were made mostly through social media and had disrupted air travel in India.

World.title: SC asks Centre, states why retail acid sale cannot be completely banned to curb attacks
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday asked the Centre and the states why retail sale of acid should not be banned after an acid attack survivor complained that the SC-prompted 2013 guidelines of the Union government remain on paper even as girls continue to suffer physical disfigurement and lifelong mental trauma from acid attacks.

Continuing with its strong stance against those jilted lovers accused of throwing acid on girls leading to severe physical disfigurement, loss of eyesight and lifelong mental trauma, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked the Centre and states to respond within four weeks on a policy decision to either ban retail sale of acid or impose strict restrictions on it.

This direction came after acid attack survivor Shaheen Malik, who runs an NGO to help girls who suffered trauma and scars of acid attacks, told the bench that every day three girls face a similar fate and there should be a complete ban on the retail sale of acid.

She cited a case of three girls, two from Okhla in Delhi and one in Haryana, who were blinded by acid attacks. âHow many more girls must suffer,â she asked while pushing for a complete ban.

Accepting that acid should be supplied for the purpose of research and educational institutions, the bench said banning across-the-counter sale is the first option. In the alternative, it proposed whether retail sale of acid can be restricted only to those who are above 50 years of age after they give in writing the purpose behind such purchases.





The data should be collated on a dashboard for ready reference of law-enforcing agencies on acid available in private hands.

Senior advocate Saurabh Kirpal told the bench that strict guidelines framed by the SC in the Laxmi case in 2013 said acid continues to be available across the counter. The bench said the 2013 guidelines must have become obsolete now and asked additional solicitor general Archana Pathak Dave to submit fresh guidelines from the Centre on this issue.

World.title: Nepal must make climate justice top national priority, says Environment Minister
World.content:
Nepal’s Forestry and Environment Minister Gita Chaudhary has called for climate change and environmental issues to be made a top national priority, local media reported on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).

Follow the updates of the Nepal flash floods on September 1, 2026.

Her comments came days after devastating flash floods killed around 1,000 people in Nepal and left nearly 4,000 missing. The floods, triggered by a collapse or avalanche of ice and rock near the Nepal-Tibet border, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.

She also said the country must assert its rights and claims on climate justice at international forums.

Speaking at a consultation with experts at the ministry before leaving to attend a ministerial conference of the least developed countries, Ms. Chaudhary said that Nepal must work to establish mountain issues on the global agenda.

The discussions also covered domestic and international initiatives to seek compensation for the severe damage caused by the recent floods, according to Nepal News.

“Unless we can present this agenda as our right and our claim, we cannot give it the priority it deserves,” she was quoted as saying by the Onlinekhabar news portal.

Nepal is a mountainous country and home to Mount Everest, the world’s highest peak, she noted, stressing the need for the country to lead the mountain agenda and establish it globally.

Ms. Chaudhary said it would be difficult to give priority at the national level to the damage and problems caused by the climate crisis unless climate justice was established as a right before the international community.

She said climate change should not be confined to one or two government programmes or international conferences.

Ms. Chaudhary also called for cooperation among civil society, experts, the media and other stakeholders, saying government efforts alone would not be sufficient to address climate and environmental challenges.

World.title: Vande Mataram sung in full twice at Kerala University Sports Day event with Governor, Ministers on stage
World.content:
The full rendition of Vande Mataram was sung twice during the National Sports Day celebrations organised by Kerala University on Tuesday (September 1, 2026). Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar and State Ministers were among those present on the stage.

The ceremony was attended by Mr Arlekar, Higher Education Minister Roji M. John, Sports Minister O.J. Janeesh and Kerala University Vice-Chancellor (in-charge) Mohanan Kunnummal.

According to university officials, Vande Mataram was included in the programme following a specific instruction from the Governor’s office in view of his participation in the event.

Vande Mataram and the right to dissent

The song was performed in its entirety at the beginning of the programme and was repeated at its conclusion. The national anthem was also sung after Vande Mataram.

Mr. Janeesh, when asked about the decision, said he understood that a protocol existed when the Governor attended an official function. He indicated that the inclusion of Vande Mataram was connected with that protocol, while acknowledging that he did not have complete clarity on the circumstances.

The issue comes shortly after a similar controversy erupted during the concluding ceremony of the Onam Week celebrations in Thiruvananthapuram, where Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan was present. Vande Mataram was sung in full during that function as well.

At the time, Tourism Minister P.C. Vishnunadh had explained that the Vice-President’s participation in an official ceremony entailed a specific protocol that had to be followed.

However, the CPI(M) targeted the government, with party State secretary M.V. Govindan claiming that Vande Mataram was a ‘Hindu song’ when rendered in full and could not be considered a secular composition. He also alleged a “deal” between Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS).

Senior CPI(M) leader and former Minister V. Sivankutty also questioned the government’s approach and alleged that the move reflected a political accommodation with the BJP.

World.title: Vande Mataram politics returns to centre stage in Keralam as Onam festivities end
World.content:
Politics over Vande Mataram resurfaced in Keralam again as Onam holidays drew to a close on Monday (August 31, 2026). A choir rendered the six-stanza version of the song at the conclusion of the Keralam government-sponsored Onam week pageantry, flagged off by Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan from an elevated VIP podium erected for the occasion in front of the Lok Bhavan on Sunday evening, re-igniting the controversy.

Vande Mataram sung in full twice at Kerala University Sports Day event with Governor, Ministers on stage

Keralam Governor Rajendra Arlekar, Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan and Tourism Minister P.C. Vishnunadh were on the dais with Mr Radhakrishnan when the colourful procession swept past the Lok Bhavan and slowly meandered down the arterial M.G. Road, overwhelmed by holiday crowds.

The flag-off ceremony debatably marked a departure from the Keralam government’s decision not to sing Vande Mataram in full during the Independence Day celebrations on August 15.

Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretary M V Govindan accused the Congress of “playing second fiddle to the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)’s project to build a civilisational polity defined by Hindutva ideology”, which he claimed sought to relegate minorities and marginalised sections of society to a subaltern status.

He said the Congress had no qualms about rendering the “profoundly schismatic” song in full during the recent Independence Day celebrations at the All India Congress Committee’s (AICC) headquarters in New Delhi.

Mr Govindan also slammed the AICC leadership for giving the go-by to the 1937 Congress Working Committee’s decision to limit the rendering of Vande Mataram to the first two lines of the composition on the premise that the later stanzas contained overt Hindu religious iconography.

Mr Govindan said the Keralam government’s “latest acquiescence to the RSS’s Hindutva agenda has yet again pulled the veil back on the Congress-Bharatiya Janata Party covert ideological and political axis.”

Local Self-Government Minister K M Shaji told reporters that the Vice-President’s office had fixed the protocol for the event. The State government had no jurisdictional authority to alter the official etiquette set by the offices of those holding high constitutional positions, including that of the President and the Vice President. He noted that Vande Mataram was not rendered in full, if at all, in Keralam government’s official events.

Mr. Vishunadh also struck a similar note.

Former Education Minister and CPI(M) State Committee member V Sivankutty said protocol offered “a perfect foil” for the UDF government to play a subordinate facilitator role to the RSS’s Hindutva agenda. “Protocol is a convenient pretext to swirl dandas (staff used by RSS workers for customary martial training), polish shoes and sing songs”, he quipped in a Facebook post.

World.title: NEET protests: SC quashes FIRs against protestors under Article 142
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) directed all FIRs concerning NEET-UG protests registered between July 20 and July 25 be quashed under Article 142 of the Constitution.

As the Bench assembled to hear the Delhi Police’s application to invoke plenary powers under Article 142, Cockroach Janta Party’s Saurav Das informed the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant that the outfit has decided to call off its planned September 5 protest march. Mr Das said that the decision was taken after “assurances” from the Centre regarding withdrawal of FIRs and compensation to victims.

Also read | NEET-UG protests case: Petitioners seek re-constitution of high-powered enquiry committee

The Bench then proceeded to hear Solicitor General Tushar Mehta who urged the Supreme Court to use its powers to close all FIRs against NEET protesters between July 20-July 25 across country.

He told the bench that the Centre is committed to honour the assurance given to the CJP leaders and provide compensation to the families of students who ended their lives after the cancellation of the NEET exam.

Mr. Mehta told the court that it will pay compensation to families of the students who died and sought three months to work out the modalities.

The Bench then directed the quashing of all relevant FIRs registered between July 20 and July 25 and said that “any other FIRs registered with regard to incidents which happened between July 20 and July 25 in any other States/Union Territories, including those not formally brought before the court, shall not be investigated and be closed for all intents and purposes.”

Noting that the Centre shall be at liberty to ask the States and UTs to not register any fresh FIR, the Bench allowed Delhi Police to file fresh FIR against 28,73 individuals without prejudice to the rights of these individuals.

Compensation for protestors injured in police action

The Supreme Court also asked the Centre formulate the modalities for compensation scheme for protestors who were injured in police action. The scheme, once finalised shall be adopted by the States and UTs as a regular mechanism in such situations.

NEET protests in Delhi: CJP calls off September 5 protest march after ‘assurances’ from Centre over withdrawal of FIRs

The Centre shall pay compensation to the families of students, who took their lives due to the NEET-UG paper leaks, within three months.

The Supreme Court had earlier constituted a high-powered enquiry committee headed by former Supreme Court Judge Justice R. Subhash Reddy to probe issues and allegations, including those of police excesses against students surrounding the nationwide protests against NEET-UG paper leaks.

(With inputs from PTI)

World.title: Modi government destroyed ‘lifeline of poor’ MGNREGA; conspired to snatch employment guarantee: Congress
World.content:
The Congress on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) accused the Modi government of destroying the "lifeline" of the country's poor, MGNREGA, and claimed that its real policy is to fill the coffers of crony capitalists by snatching the last morsel of bread from the poor.

Congress general secretary in-charge communications Jairam Ramesh shared a media report on X, which claimed that the job card holders in Ballia district are becoming disillusioned with the Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin), a trend clearly reflected in departmental statistics.

"The Modi government has destroyed the lifeline of the country's poor, MGNREGA, in the name of 'VB G RAM G'. The BJP made grand speeches in Parliament, but on the ground, all those claims are proving to be empty hot air," Mr. Ramesh said in his post in Hindi on X.

What the Congress had stated at the time of changing this scheme is now coming to light, he said.

The Modi government has ended the right to employment for the poor and the deprived, which had been ensured by the Congress, Mr. Ramesh claimed.

It is now clear that the Modi government had deliberately plotted to end the most successful and historic poverty alleviation scheme, MGNREGA, by enacting a new law, he said.

This was not just a matter of changing the name; it was a calculated conspiracy to snatch away the employment guarantee of the poor, Mr. Ramesh alleged.

In Ballia, against a target of 1.76 lakh man-day work, only 10,669 days of work were provided in two months. This story is being repeated in every district of the country, he said.

"In this back-breaking era of inflation, snatching the last morsel of bread from the poor to fill the coffers of crony capitalists is the real policy of the anti-poor Modi government," Mr. Ramesh said.

As the VB-G RAM G Act came into effect earlier this year, the Congress had demanded the repeal of the rural employment scheme and that a strengthened MGNREGA be brought back, claiming the wages under the new law are unjustifiably low.

The Opposition party had asserted that a just minimum wage for India's workers would be ensured by adopting the 2019 recommendation of the expert committee headed by Dr Anoop Satpathy and accommodating the increase in prices since then.

The Viksit Bharat Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, or the VB G RAM G Act, came into force across the country from July 1, replacing the two-decade-old Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), introduced by the Congress-led UPA.

World.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay opens Mettur Dam releasing Cauvery water for irrigation in State
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay opened the sluices of Stanley Reservoir in Mettur for delta irrigation on Tuesday (September 1, 2026).

Around 10.15 a.m. on Tuesday, the Chief Minister reached Salem Airport at Kamalapuram. Then, he reached Mettur on road via Thoppur, Mecheri, and Kunjandiyur and released Cauvery water from the dam at 11.30 a.m. and threw flowers on the water that gushed out.

Mr. Vijay also interacted with farmers and received petitions from them. The farmers urged him to open water from the dam for more days instead of the announced 45 days and also sought steps from the government to divert Mettur’s surplus water to water bodies in Thalaivasal.

Later, he inspected the photo exhibition organised by the Water Resources Department (WRD) and officials explained the ongoing works in the delta region. He also inspected the dam powerhouse. Then, Mr. Vijay left for Salem airport from the inspection bungalow at Mettur around 2 p.m.

Dam opened after 80-day delay

Traditionally, water is released from the Mettur dam on June 12 every year and the dam is closed on January 28 after 230 days of discharge of water for irrigation. While a total of 330 TMC is required for irrigation, the date of opening the dam’s sluices changes depending on the availability of water in the dam.

This year, owing to inadequate water in the Stanley Reservoir, the reservoir was not opened on the customary date of June 12. After a 80-day delay, water has been discharged from the Mettur dam on September 1 for samba cultivation in the delta region.

Officials attached to the Water Resources Department (WRD) said that for the next 45 days, until October 15, water would be discharged from the dam based on its availability. Initially, the Chief Minister opened 3,000 cusecs of water from the dam and it will be increased to 7,000 cusecs by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, officials added.

62nd instance of late release

It is notable that in the 93-year history of the Mettur Dam, water has been discharged for delta irrigation 20 times on its scheduled date, June 12. For 11 times, water was released from the dam before the customary date. This year, for the 62nd instance, water has been discharged after the customary date.

Likewise, this was the fourth time water discharged for delta irrigation in the month of September. Earlier in 2002, 2012, and 2016, water discharged from the Mettur dam for delta irrigation in the month of September.

Water level

On Tuesday at 8 a.m., water level at Mettur Dam stood at 91.56 feet against its full reservoir level of 120 feet. The storage level stood at 54.45 tmcft compared to its full capacity of 93.47 tmcft. Inflow into the dam reduced to 10,857 cusecs from 11,501 cusecs.

In a press release, the Tamil Nadu government said it would take all steps to get the water share for Tamil Nadu from Karnataka. To ensure the rights of Delta farmers, the government is taking all legal and administrative steps, it added.

People throng to see CM

From 8 a.m., TVK cadre and the public gathered on the stretch of road from Kamalapuram to Mettur to see and greet Chief Minister Mr. Vijay. The police installed barricades on both sides of the roads stretching up to 40 km to prevent the public from entering into the roads.

Over 3,800 police personnel led by ADGP Anbu were deployed in protection duty from Salem Airport to Mettur Dam. Following the chief minister's visit, vehicles headed to Salem from Mettur diverted via M. Kalipatti, vice versa.

At the airport, Water Resources Minister N. Anand, Transport Minister A. Vijay Tamilan Parthiban, MLAs Palanivel, Lakshmanan, and Sivakumar, District Collector K. Elambahavath, and Deputy Mayor Saradha Devi welcomed the Chief Minister.

World.title: Man dies after being assaulted for seeking repayment of loan in Arsikere
World.content:
