If a buyer can save 20% of their salary, it would take around 50 years to accumulate the full cost of the property. To save the down payment required under a standard mortgage, which in this case would be around 28,000 manats (about $16,500), would take almost eight years.

The average wage also does not reflect the incomes of all workers. According to data from the State Statistics Committee, during the first five months of the year, average monthly wages were 763 manats (about $449) in retail, 825 manats (about $485) in education, and 800 manats (about $470.50) in tourism and catering. For workers in these sectors, a mid-range flat in Baku is equivalent to around 18–19 years of their combined earnings.

Does a mortgage make housing more affordable – or more expensive?

The maximum amount available under a standard mortgage from the Mortgage and Credit Guarantee Fund is 150,000 manats (about $88,235), with a loan term of up to 25 years, an annual interest rate of 8% and a minimum down payment of 15%. However, 85% of the 177,775-manat price of the flat exceeds the loan limit, meaning the buyer would have to provide at least 27,775 manats from their own funds.

If the remaining 150,000 manats were borrowed for 25 years at 8% interest, the monthly payment would be around 1,158 manats (about $681.20). Over the full term, the borrower would repay more than 347,000 manats (about $204,000) to the bank. Including the down payment, the total cost would exceed 375,000 manats (about $220,600). Insurance, property valuation, notary fees and other associated costs are not included.

A monthly payment of 1,158 manats is almost equal to the average salary across the country and represents 78% of the average salary in Baku. Under the Fund’s rules, mortgage payments must not exceed 70% of borrowers’ combined income after tax. This means that a Baku resident earning a single average salary would find it practically impossible to service such a mortgage alone.

In a household where two people earn the average Baku salary, the monthly mortgage payment would account for 39% of their combined nominal income. After tax, the share would exceed 40%. According to OECD and Eurostat methodology, housing costs exceeding 40% of disposable income are considered an excessive housing burden.

Under the subsidised mortgage scheme, the annual interest rate is 4%, the loan term can be up to 30 years, and the maximum loan amount is 100,000 manats (about $58,820). Although the monthly payment would be around 477 manats (about $280.60), buying a 65-square-metre flat at Baku’s average price would require around 78,000 manats (about $45,882) in the buyer’s own funds. The lower interest rate therefore does not solve the main problem for families without substantial savings.

Is renting cheaper?

The median advertised rent in Baku is 11 manats (about $6.50) per square metre per month. Renting a 65-square-metre flat would therefore cost around 715 manats (about $420.60) a month – 443 manats (about $260.60) less than the monthly payment on a standard mortgage. However, this still amounts to around 48% of the average salary in Baku, excluding utility bills.

If an investor bought such a flat for 178,000 manats and rented it out for 715 manats a month, the gross annual rental yield would be around 4.8%. After accounting for maintenance, periods when the property is vacant and other associated costs, the actual return would be even lower. Buying a flat with a mortgage and then renting it out therefore generally does not allow the owner to cover the full cost through rental income alone. The model may make sense primarily for investors with substantial capital who are betting on further increases in property prices.

What is driving prices higher?

The Chamber of Appraisers attributes the rise in new-build prices to strong demand in the mid-to-upper and premium segments, the availability of mortgage financing and the perception of housing as an investment asset. The Chamber’s land price index also points to rising prices and limited supply in premium areas. This may put additional pressure on the cost of newly built homes.

At the same time, according to the State Statistics Committee, investment in residential construction fell by 2.7% in real terms in the first half of the year. These figures strengthen the suggestion that demand, growing faster than household incomes, is running up against limited supply.

State-backed mortgages make housing more affordable for some families: in the first half of the year, 2,242 families received mortgage loans worth a total of 226.3 million manats (about $133.1 million). Since 2019, just over 10,000 families have used the rent-to-own scheme. However, it remains unclear whether these programmes are large enough to curb the overall rise in property prices.

Buying a home in Baku today is therefore more affordable for a household with two stable official incomes, substantial savings for a down payment or another property that can be sold than for someone living on a single average salary. Those who qualify for subsidised mortgages and have tens of thousands of manats in savings are also in a stronger position.

For everyone else, the choice is essentially between increasingly expensive rent and taking on long-term, substantial debt.

Buying a home in Azerbaijan

World.title: ‘Occupation is off’: Russian state media RIA Novosti on Georgian PM Kobakhidze’s remarks
World.content:
RIA Novosti on Russia-Georgia relations

Russia’s state-run news agency RIA Novosti has responded to remarks by Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, saying that Tbilisi had decided to reassess the history of its relations with Moscow.

The article, published on 24 August 2026 under the headline “Occupation is off”: Another country refuses to consider Russia an enemy, focused on Kobakhidze’s remarks about the Treaty of Georgievsk.

Background

On 18 August 2026, Georgian Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze said that Georgia’s decision to sign the Treaty of Georgievsk had been a “civilisational choice”.

His main argument was that King Erekle II’s decision ultimately ensured the physical and political survival of the Georgian nation. According to Kobakhidze, Christian Georgia, surrounded by Muslim states, chose to align itself with Orthodox Russia.

Kobakhidze argued that the decision was not only justified but also “the only correct and only possible” choice at the time. He said Russia honoured the terms of the treaty during Erekle II’s lifetime:

“While Erekle II was alive, he ensured that the agreement was upheld to the end, and almost 20 years passed between the signing of the Treaty of Georgievsk and the annexation of Georgia. For two decades, our country effectively survived.”

The Treaty of Georgievsk was an agreement between the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti and the Russian Empire, signed on 24 July 1783. Under the treaty, King Erekle II accepted the protection of Russian Empress Catherine II, while Russia pledged to defend the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti and preserve its territorial integrity. The treaty formally preserved the internal independence of the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti and did not declare it part of the Russian Empire. However, in 1801, the Russian Empire abolished the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti and incorporated it into its territory.

What RIA Novosti says in its article

The Russian state-run news agency says Kobakhidze presented Georgia’s decision to accept the Russian Empire’s protection as the only way for the Georgian people to survive Ottoman and Persian aggression.

The article quotes the views of several political experts, including Nino Skvortsova, whom the agency describes as a “Tbilisi-based political analyst”.

According to Skvortsova, Kobakhidze’s focus on the reign of Erekle II serves not only to reinterpret history but also to justify the government’s current policies.

“Kobakhidze is trying to place Erekle II back in his historical context. For him, the king is important as a ruler forced to choose between major powers while his country’s existence was under threat,” the expert says.

In her view, this approach allows parallels to be drawn with the current policies of the ruling Georgian Dream party:

“Modern Georgia is also caught in competition between major powers, while the authorities justify their actions by the need to preserve peace, sovereignty, traditional identity and freedom of foreign policy manoeuvre.”

RIA Novosti also quotes another expert, Artur Ataev, who says that Georgian Dream is trying to raise a new generation free from old stereotypes. Ataev argues that the opposition, in turn, wants Georgia to follow the example of Ukraine, the Baltic states and other former Soviet republics.

“Today, this is one of the main topics of debate in Georgian society. There are even calls to recognise the independence of Abkhazia and South Ossetia,” Ataev says.

He argues that Georgian society and the political elite are gradually changing, but that the restoration of diplomatic relations with Russia is unlikely in the near future.

“After all, most Georgians still see Russia as an occupier,” the expert concludes.

RIA Novosti on Russia-Georgia relations

World.title: Saturday March in Tbilisi: growing emigration. “Protests in Georgia” video podcast
World.content:
For more than a year and half – since November 2024 – continuous protests have been taking place in Georgia, with demonstrators demanding that the country return to the path of European integration. The results of the parliamentary elections held in autumn 2024 are still not recognised by part of Georgian society.

Every evening thousands, and often tens of thousands, gather in Tbilisi and several other cities. Over this time dozens of participants have been detained, many have faced criminal charges, and some have been sentenced to prison terms.

For the first time in the history of independent Georgia, the country has up to 150 prisoners of conscience, including women. Among them is Mzia Amaglobeli, founder of the popular outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti.

In 2025 she was sentenced to two years in prison for slapping a police officer. Protesters demand the release of all political prisoners and the repeal of all anti-democratic laws adopted over the past two years.

To suppress the protests, the ruling Georgian Dream party has increasingly tightened repression against civil society and the media. However, protests in various forms continue.

World.title: Abkhaz blogger who spoke of ‘shared future’: Who was late Daur Buava?
World.content:
Abkhaz blogger found dead in Georgia

Young Abkhaz blogger Daur Buava has been found dead in the Georgian capital, Tbilisi. According to neighbours, they raised the alarm after Buava had not been seen for several days. Emergency services called to his rented flat found his body inside.

The cause of his death has not yet been established, and an initial examination of the body found no signs of violence. Georgia’s Interior Ministry has opened an investigation under the article covering “incitement to suicide”.

Who was Daur Buava?

Daur Buava, 32, was an Abkhaz blogger who attracted public attention for his open and unconventional views on Georgian-Abkhaz relations. On social media, particularly TikTok, he regularly posted videos advocating peaceful coexistence, dialogue and the rebuilding of trust between Georgians and Abkhaz.

Buava was born in Abkhazia in 1994. The Georgian-Abkhaz war had ended a year before he was born, meaning his understanding of the conflict was largely shaped by what he had been told by those around him. In 2021, Buava travelled to Tbilisi in an attempt to examine that version of events for himself.

“Later, I realised that it was the truth as seen by only one side. I learned the other side’s truth here,” he told Georgian media outlet Netgazeti that same year.

Within months, Buava had become one of the most recognisable Abkhaz bloggers on TikTok. His videos focused primarily on relations between Georgians and Abkhaz, the war, peace and Abkhazia’s future. He had tens of thousands of followers, including young people in Abkhazia.

Buava’s public activities were not confined to social media. He gradually became one of the few Abkhaz voices openly advocating dialogue with Georgians. It was this position that made him a target of persecution in Abkhazia.

Meeting the “enemy”

Buava said that before travelling to Tbilisi, his views of Georgia had been based largely on the information he received in Abkhazia.

One of the reasons he decided to visit Georgia was a TikTok livestream in which Georgians and Abkhaz called each other enemies and exchanged insults. For Buava, this became another reason to see for himself the place he had been taught since childhood to regard as hostile.

He said that in both societies there was a small group of people fuelling hatred, while most people wanted to communicate with one another.

Daur Buava

Persecution in Abkhazia

Buava’s activities did not receive unequivocal support in Abkhazia from the outset. In late 2021, he said that many people criticised his presence and activities in Tbilisi, although he also received messages of support from Abkhazia. Over time, however, criticism was followed by threats.

According to Buava, his supporters also faced pressure. He said that people who posted positive comments during his livestreams were identified and, in some cases, people even went to their homes. Buava also said that several of his supporters had been beaten.

In June 2022, Abkhazia’s de facto security service opened a criminal case against Buava on charges of “high treason”.

The agency said that videos posted by Buava on TikTok contained appeals that undermined Abkhazia’s “sovereignty, territorial integrity, state security and defence capabilities”. It also accused him of promoting the idea of Abkhazia existing as an autonomous republic within Georgia.

The case against Buava was opened in absentia. He remained in Tbilisi and no longer planned to return to Abkhazia.

‘Amra’ and idea of shared future

In Tbilisi, Buava and his Georgian friend Mikheil Kvatashidze founded the Amra youth movement. The name means “Sun” in Abkhaz. The organisation aimed to create opportunities for young Georgians and Abkhaz to communicate with one another.

In December 2022, Buava obtained Georgian citizenship, which he said was granted under a simplified procedure. This became another source of criticism against him within Abkhaz society.

In 2023, Buava was invited to the European Parliament, where he spoke about relations between young Georgians and Abkhaz, the free exchange of information and overcoming the conflict.

“We must move forward and build a shared future,” he said.

At the European Parliament, Buava also addressed Russia’s role. In his view, Moscow had contributed to the escalation of the Georgian-Abkhaz conflict and was continuing to obstruct dialogue between Georgians and Abkhaz.

That same year, Buava opposed the adoption of the so-called “apartments law” in Abkhazia, saying he did not want Russians to buy property and settle in Abkhazia in large numbers. He regarded the main threat to Abkhazia as not the restoration of relations with Georgians, but the loss of its own demographic and cultural identity.

World.title: Georgian president pardons nine activists, one may face deportation to Russia
World.content:
Georgian president pardons nine activists

On the occasion of the Orthodox feast of Mariamoba (the Dormition of the Mother of God), Georgian President Mikheil Kavelashvili pardoned 226 prisoners. They included nine people detained during various protests. Georgian civil society groups and several organisations consider them political prisoners.

According to pro-government media, those pardoned include Denis Kulanin, a Russian citizen who, according to his lawyer, faces possible deportation.

List of pardoned activists:

Fridon Bubuteishvili — sentenced to five years in prison on 20 January 2025 on charges of injuring a firefighter-rescuer and damaging the gates of the parliament building. On 8 May 2026, it was reported that he had petitioned the president for a pardon.

On 8 May 2026, it was reported that he had petitioned the president for a pardon. Simon Makharadze — detained in connection with the storming of the presidential palace in October 2025. Several months ago, he reached a plea agreement and was sentenced to one year in prison and a further three years suspended.

— detained in connection with the storming of the presidential palace in October 2025. Several months ago, he reached a plea agreement and was sentenced to one year in prison and a further three years suspended. Davit Khomeriki — sentenced to four years and six months in prison on 15 August 2025 on charges of preparing to commit a crime and transporting or placing explosives or other devices or substances posing a danger to life and health.

— sentenced to four years and six months in prison on 15 August 2025 on charges of preparing to commit a crime and transporting or placing explosives or other devices or substances posing a danger to life and health. Saba Jikia — sentenced to four years and six months in prison on 10 July 2025 on charges of assaulting a police officer.

— sentenced to four years and six months in prison on 10 July 2025 on charges of assaulting a police officer. Daniel Mumladze — sentenced to three years in prison on 2 June 2025 on charges of damaging a CCTV camera.

— sentenced to three years in prison on 2 June 2025 on charges of damaging a CCTV camera. Guram Khutashvili — sentenced to three years in prison on 2 June 2025 on similar charges of damaging a CCTV camera.

— sentenced to three years in prison on 2 June 2025 on similar charges of damaging a CCTV camera. Tornike Mchedlishvili — detained in connection with the storming of the presidential palace and sentenced to five years in prison.

— detained in connection with the storming of the presidential palace and sentenced to five years in prison. Avtandil Topchishvili — also detained in connection with the storming of the presidential palace. Several months ago, he reached a plea agreement and was sentenced to one year in prison and a further three years suspended.

Сase of Denis Kulanin

Pro-government Georgian media report that those pardoned also include Denis Kulanin, a Russian citizen who lived in Georgia and took part in pro-European protests. He was detained on 28 March 2025 during a protest outside parliament on charges of breaking the window of a police vehicle and was sentenced to two years in prison.

However, according to his lawyer, Dimitri Nozadze, Kulanin has not been released. The lawyer believes that Kulanin is being held by the immigration authorities and is being prepared for deportation to Russia.

Nozadze says deporting Kulanin to Russia would be unacceptable and dangerous because, while in prison, he published a letter in which he wished Ukraine glory and peace. The lawyer says the letter could give the Russian authorities grounds to bring criminal charges against him.

Адвокат поясняет, что недавно был принят закон, наделяющий силовые ведомства полномочиями выдворять из страны иностранцев, совершивших преступление в Грузии.

На вопрос о том, обращался ли Денис Куланин к президенту Михеилу Кавелашвили с прошением о помиловании, адвокат ответил, что ничего об этом не знает.

World.title: Moscow posters: Are radical nationalists acting independently of Kremlin in Azerbaijan row?
World.content:
Protest at Azerbaijani embassy in Russia

On 27 August, at a time when independent political protests have become rare in Russia, a group of radical nationalists staged a protest outside Azerbaijan‘s diplomatic mission in Moscow. Participants put up three posters, filmed the action and posted the video on the group’s Telegram channel, which has tens of thousands of subscribers.

Azərbaycanın Rusiya səfirliyinin qonaq evi qarşısında naməlum şəxslər tərəfindən Azərbaycan əleyhinə təxribatın videosu pic.twitter.com/3CkEXuYacp — Unikal.az (@UnikalOrgPortal) August 27, 2026

Although the protest was small, it raises a question: can radical nationalists in Russia, where public expressions of opposition are tightly restricted, intervene in relations between Baku and Moscow without the Kremlin’s knowledge?

There is no clear answer so far. The issue is not whether the Kremlin learned about the protest after the event, but what boundaries the authorities set for the activities of such groups.

There is no evidence that the protest was organised at the request of the Russian authorities. However, the fact that the same group has now targeted Azerbaijan for a second time, coupled with the authorities’ differing treatment of public expressions of political views, raises questions about whether such groups may receive preferential treatment.

What accusations appeared on the three posters?

According to Azerbaijan’s Foreign Ministry, the posters were placed not outside the main embassy building but in front of its guest house. The protest was covered by the Telegram channel Direct Action Z, which describes itself as an information resource of Eduard Limonov’s Other Russia party.

The posters accused Azerbaijan’s State Security Service of torture and President Ilham Aliyev of covering it up. They also carried the slogans “Russian blood is on your hands” and “Hands off Russian citizens”.

In a statement, the organisers portrayed the detention of eight Russian nationals in Azerbaijan, criminal proceedings against Ivan Knyazev, Semyon Uralov and Alexei Chadayev, Baku’s position on Ukraine and the deaths of Russian peacekeepers in Karabakh in 2023 as manifestations of a single “anti-Russian policy”. They also accused the Azerbaijani diaspora of running “shadow businesses”.

Azerbaijan’s Foreign Ministry described the incident as an “unacceptable provocation” and said it could be a continuation of what it alleges is a campaign against Azerbaijan by a number of Russian media outlets. Baku called on Moscow to investigate the incident and ensure the security of its diplomatic mission.

Azərbaycan Respublikasının Rusiya Federasiyasındakı Səfirliyinin qonaq evi qarşısında təxribatla bağlı açıqlama



⬇️⬇️⬇️https://t.co/YPLnFLJ4Mx



Statement on the provocation in front of the Guest House of the Embassy of the Republic of Azerbaijan in the Russian Federation… pic.twitter.com/D9TwDicyqr — MFA Azerbaijan 🇦🇿 (@AzerbaijanMFA) August 27, 2026

Same group staged protest exactly one year ago

One detail that makes it difficult to dismiss the incident as a random street protest is the date. On 27 August 2025, three members of the same movement staged a protest outside the Azerbaijani consulate in St Petersburg. They were detained by police.

The accusations made at the time differed from those voiced now. The protesters opposed Baku’s alliance with Ankara, its support for Ukraine and Azerbaijan’s competition with Russia on the energy market. In the following months, individual pickets were also held outside the consulate under the slogan “Russophobia is a disease”.

The fact that the second protest took place exactly a year later gives the impression that it may be a continuation of the earlier campaign. However, the organisers did not say whether the date had been chosen deliberately.

Close to Kremlin or opposed to it?

The Other Russia of E. V. Limonov is an unregistered political organisation founded by former members of the National Bolshevik Party, which a Russian court designated as extremist and banned in 2007. Its ideology combines Russian nationalism, “Soviet nostalgia” and imperialist ideas.

Its members support Russia’s war against Ukraine, and some have fought on the Russian side. The movement’s Interbrigades unit has operated in Donbas since 2014. In this respect, the group’s foreign policy rhetoric does not contradict the Kremlin’s broader line.

However, this does not mean the organisation is directly controlled by the Kremlin. National Bolshevik activists have also protested against the Central Bank, Roskomnadzor and other state bodies. In October 2025, four members of the movement were detained during a protest outside the Central Bank. In February 2026, activists from the organisation placed a lock on the door of Roskomnadzor’s Moscow office before leaving the scene.

On 18 August, the Russian Foreign Ministry said that statements by Knyazev, Uralov and Chadayev did not reflect Moscow’s position towards Azerbaijan. In their latest statement on Azerbaijan, the National Bolsheviks, in turn, accused the Foreign Ministry of failing to defend the three men. The group claimed that the state was putting the interests of “foreign entities” above those of Russian citizens.

In other words, the protest was directed not only against Baku but also against Moscow’s own policy, which the organisers regard as “not tough enough”.

Question of preferential treatment

National Bolshevik activists themselves are also periodically detained and given administrative jail terms. It would therefore be an oversimplification to portray them as an untouchable group carrying out the Kremlin’s orders.

On the other hand, it is clear that political protests in Russia are not treated equally. According to the latest available data from OVD-Info, more than 20,000 detentions for expressing anti-war views were recorded between February 2022 and July 2025. At the same time, groups that support the war in Ukraine but call on the authorities to take a tougher line have been able to hold public events, raise donations and operate actively on social media.

The Counter Extremism Project, which researches extremist movements, describes the relationship between the Kremlin and the National Bolsheviks as an “uneasy alliance”: the group criticises the authorities and its members are periodically detained, but its activities in Ukraine and pro-war campaigning are generally treated with considerably greater tolerance.

This pattern does not prove that the protest outside Azerbaijan’s diplomatic mission was organised at the state’s behest. However, it once again raises the question of which protests the authorities immediately suppress and which they allow to proceed without intervention.

Defending rights or exerting ethnic pressure?

The situation of the Russian nationals detained in Azerbaijan continues to raise questions that remain unanswered. In footage released after their detention, some appeared to have visible signs of violence on their faces. There have also been reports that the psychological condition of convicted Russian national Dmitry Fedorov has deteriorated and that he has stopped recognising his relatives.

However, the National Bolsheviks’ statement goes beyond defending the rights of individual detainees. It combines human rights concerns with rhetoric about “Russian blood”, criticism of Azerbaijan’s support for Ukraine and accusations directed at the Azerbaijani diaspora as a whole.

World.title: Food prices help Kazakhstan curb inflation in August
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 1. Kazakhstan's annual inflation slowed to 9.8% in August 2026, while monthly inflation stood at 0.6%, the country's Ministry of National Economy said.

The monthly increase in prices was 0.4 percentage points lower than in August 2025, when prices rose by 1%.

"The slowdown in inflation is supported by the implementation, on the instructions of the Head of State, of a set of measures by the Government jointly with the National Bank and the Agency for Regulation and Development of the Financial Market aimed at containing price growth, ensuring macroeconomic stability and improving the well-being of the population," the ministry said.

The main contribution to the slowdown in inflation continues to come from lower food price growth. Annual food inflation slowed to 9.5% in August, compared with 10.1% in July 2026.

Meanwhile, prices for socially significant food products increased by only 2.1% as of August 26, 2026, which was 7.4 percentage points lower than a year earlier, when the increase stood at 9.5%.

"This result was ensured by a set of measures, including expanding the list of socially significant food products from 19 to 31 items, continuous monitoring of compliance with the maximum 15% trade markup, identifying and reducing unproductive intermediaries, increasing the supply of domestically produced goods to the domestic market and ensuring food affordability," the ministry said.

The ministry noted that the slowdown in overall inflation continued despite factors related to the gradual liberalization of the fuel market and the expiration of the moratorium on increases in regulated utility tariffs.

World.title: South Caucasus region, once a zone of long-lasting conflict, is becoming a zone of peace - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BISHKEK, Kyrgyzstan, September 1. A little over a year ago, Azerbaijan and Armenia initialed the text of the peace agreement, putting an end to a 30-year conflict, said President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev in his speech at the SCO Plus format meeting, Trend’s special correspondent reports.

The head of state noted that, thus, the South Caucasus region, which was once a zone of long-standing conflict, is becoming a zone of peace.

World.title: Treaty on Allied Relations has elevated Azerbaijani-Kyrgyz relations to the highest level - President Ilham Aliyev
World.content:
BISHKEK, Kyrgyzstan, September 1. I am glad to visit once again brotherly Kyrgyzstan. A month ago, the Treaty on Allied Relations was signed during my state visit, said President of Azerbaijan Ilham Aliyev in his speech at the SCO Plus format meeting, Trend's special correspondent reports.

The head of state noted that this historic document has elevated Azerbaijani-Kyrgyz relations to the highest level.

World.title: Azerbaijan reveals updated statistics on Karabakh war missing persons
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 1. As of 31 August 2026, 4,010 Azerbaijani citizens remain registered as missing in connection with the First and Second Karabakh Wars: 4,004 from the First Karabakh War and 6 from the Second Karabakh War.

This was reported in a statement by the State Commission on Prisoners of War, Missing Persons, and Hostages of the Republic of Azerbaijan as of August 31, 2026.



Of those missing from the First Karabakh War, 3,222 are military personnel, and 782 are civilians, including 71 children, 288 women, and 319 elderly persons.



The State Commission of the Republic of Azerbaijan on Prisoners of War, Hostages and Missing Persons continues systematic search, recovery, identification and family handover efforts.



During August 2026:

5 sets of human remains were found and exhumed, bringing the total to 910

21 identified persons were handed over to their families and buried, bringing the total to 267

The total number of missing persons identified through DNA and forensic methods remains 328

32 mass graves have been discovered to date



In January-August 2026 alone, 79 sets of human remains were recovered, 57 missing persons were identified, and 64 were handed over to their families for dignified burial.



Today, 3,682 persons are still considered missing.



Meanwhile, the State Commission continues its efforts to search for missing persons and to locate, exhume, identify, and return human remains to their families.

World.title: Global stability increasingly depends on responsible AI development, Tokayev says
World.content:
BISHKEK, Kyrgyzstan, September 1. Global stability increasingly depends on the responsible development of artificial intelligence (AI), Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said, Trend's special correspondent reports.

Tokayev made the remarks while addressing the SCO Plus summit in Bishkek.

"Decisions being made are already shaping a new technological order and the future architecture of international relations. Universal rules are needed to unlock the constructive potential of artificial intelligence, prevent its uncontrolled use and reduce the digital divide. At Kazakhstan's initiative, the UN ESCAP Asia-Pacific Center for Digital Solutions will be established in Almaty. The Center can and should contribute to scaling up best practices, primarily in the interests of developing countries. We believe that technological progress is intended to serve the benefit of all humanity. There can be no so-called exclusive clubs here," Tokayev said.

The President also noted that water security is one of the priorities on the global agenda. According to him, reliable access to water determines food, energy and social stability as well as economic development. However, global water governance remains fragmented.

"Dozens of United Nations structures deal with water issues, but there is still no universal intergovernmental organization with a comprehensive mandate. Therefore, Kazakhstan has put forward an initiative to establish an international water organization under the auspices of the United Nations. Its task is not to duplicate existing mechanisms, but to coordinate efforts, ensure continuous intergovernmental dialogue, mobilize resources and develop coordinated solutions. A regional complement to this global initiative could be the SCO Water Issues Analysis Center. I count on the support of SCO member states in establishing both the International Water Organization at the UN platform and the Water Issues Analysis Center of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization," Tokayev said.

World.title: President Pezeshkian highlights SCO Plus role in emerging multipolar world
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 1. Thanks to their geographic reach, as well as their economic and political capabilities, the countries of the “SCO Plus” format can play an important role in shaping a multipolar world, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said.

This was announced by the press service of the Iranian President, citing Pezeshkian's statement at the summit of heads of state in Bishkek within the framework of the “SCO Plus” format.

“The participation of member states of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, observer states, and partners within the framework of the ‘SCO Plus’ format is of great importance. Thanks to its geographic reach and political and economic potential, this format can become one of the key foundations for cooperation and dialogue among countries actively shaping the future international order,” he noted.

Pezeshkian stated that the role of the UN as the main pillar of a just international order and the contribution of the “SCO Plus” countries to the formation of a multipolar world pose a fundamental question for everyone.

''The world is changing. A new distribution of economic, political, and technological power is taking shape. Many countries want to play a more effective role in international decision-making. The mechanisms that took shape in previous decades no longer correspond to the realities of the new international order. But how should these changes be managed?

Iran believes that the solution cannot be found by replacing one center of power with another. The goal should not be to transfer hegemony from one power to another. A multipolar world can lead to the creation of a just structure characterized by effective multipolarity, equality of power among states, and the rule of law.

Iran does not view the UN as an institution belonging to a specific historical period that will be pushed into the background due to a shift in the balance of power. On the contrary, it wants the UN to become an institution that can better represent the new realities of the world and fulfill its primary mission of preventing wars, maintaining international peace and security, and peacefully resolving conflicts. “To achieve this goal, the UN and the Security Council must play a fair and effective role in global processes,” he noted.

World.title: Kazakhstan's political and economic reforms to see further development - Tokayev
World.content:
BISHKEK, Kyrgyzstan, September 1. Kazakhstan's political and economic reforms will continue to develop in the future, President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said, Trend's special correspondent reports.

Tokayev made the remarks while addressing the SCO Plus summit in Bishkek.

"Rapid changes in the world require states not only to adapt in a timely manner, but also to have the ability and capability to act proactively. Our country's response to modern challenges has been a fairly large-scale political and economic reforms, which will undoubtedly continue to develop in the future," Tokayev said.

The President noted that the New Constitution, which entered into force on July 1, laid a solid foundation for the country's sustainable socio-economic development.

"The provisions of the Constitution have formed a qualitatively new system of state power. These transformations are aimed at strengthening socio-economic stability and building a just and progressive Kazakhstan. A new legislative body - a unicameral parliament - has begun its work. This is the first example in the history of our state. Such a parliament did not exist before," the President said.

Tokayev also reaffirmed Kazakhstan's balanced, constructive and peaceful foreign policy course.

Kazakhstan's nationwide referendum on the adoption of the new Constitution was held on March 15, 2026. The new Constitution officially entered into force on July 1, 2026.

Under the new constitutional model, the position of Vice President was introduced, while the Kazakhstan People's Council (Qazaqstan Khalqy Kenesi) was established as the supreme constitutional advisory body representing the interests of the people of Kazakhstan. The bicameral parliament, consisting of the Mazhilis and Senate, was transformed into a unicameral Kurultai.

World.title: Kyrgyzstan, Egypt discuss expanding bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Photo: Press Service of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 1. Kyrgyzstan and Egypt discussed ways to expand political, trade, economic, investment, industrial and cultural cooperation.

According to the Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers, the issue was discussed during a meeting between Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers and Head of the Presidential Administration Adylbek Kasymaliev and Egyptian Deputy Prime Minister Hussein Mohamed Ahmed Eissa.

Adylbek Kasymaliev highlighted the importance of Egypt’s participation in the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) as a dialogue partner, noting that Kyrgyzstan attaches importance to cooperation with Egypt within the organization.

According to him, such engagement contributes to expanding the SCO’s international outreach and strengthening ties between Central Asia, the Arab world and Africa.

The Kyrgyz official also recalled the results of Kyrgyz President Sadyr Zhaparov’s official visit to Egypt in November 2025, saying that the visit provided fresh momentum to bilateral relations.

He also pointed to the opening of the Kyrgyz Embassy in Cairo as a sign of intensified bilateral dialogue.

Furthermore, Adylbek Kasymaliev emphasized the need to maintain the pace of cooperation established by the two countries’ leaderships, with a focus on strengthening intergovernmental contacts and implementing practical joint initiatives.

For his part, Essa expressed Egypt’s readiness to further develop bilateral relations in the political, trade, economic, cultural and humanitarian spheres.

The Egyptian official is visiting Kyrgyzstan for the first time and congratulated the country’s leadership and people on Independence Day, the 25th anniversary of the SCO, and the opening of the 6th World Nomad Games.

World.title: Partner of missing Australian in Nepal says waiting for news has been 'hell'
World.content:
A week after the catastrophic Nepal-Tibet flood, 23-year-old Sarada Viswanathan is refusing to give up on her partner Rishab Iyer, also 23, who is still missing.

"It's been genuinely just hell for us," she told 7.30.

Mr Iyer was travelling with his parents and brother in Nepal on a Hindu Indian pilgrimage.

They too have not been heard from since last Wednesday.

The Iyer family — son Rudhra, father Sreedharan, mother Lakshmi and son Rishab — was on a pilgrimage tour in Nepal. (Supplied)

"It's been really difficult just not having any answers and not knowing where they are, how they're doing, whether they need help, whether they're drinking water, whether they're eating. Are they injured?" she said.

" It's just 24/7, we're just thinking about them, thinking about ways that we can bring them home. What can we do for them? How can we help them? "

Ms Viswanathan has set up a DIY search operation at her family home in north-west Sydney, scanning location tracking websites, clinging to any detail that might pinpoint the Australians.

Sarada Viswanathan and her friends search online for any signs of the Iyer family. (ABC News: Jerry Rickard)

"We all have them on Find My iPhone and Life360," she explained.

"The last location I have of Rishab is outside that hotel. The last location we have of his brother is slightly up onto the highway."

The Iyers were staying at the Royal Himalaya Hotel & Lodge, close to the river that flooded.

Rishab Iyer and Sarada Viswanathan have been friends since childhood. (Supplied)

"We're just hoping that they managed to climb somewhere and they managed to escape and that they just are in a remote region that's blocked off and they're not able to get in contact with anyone," Ms Viswanathan said.

Other relatives of the Iyer family are already on the ground in Nepal and have been feeding back any scintilla of information to Ms Viswanathan.

But the disaster zone has been difficult to access on foot, and Ms Viswanathan has set up a petition to push the Australian government to send defence force personnel to help with the search and rescue.

Mud covers properties in Trishuli, Nepal, after last week's flash flood. (Reuters: Navesh Chitrakar)

Australia has committed $8 million towards sending aid supplies and has dispatched a crisis response team of 18 people, including consular staff and the AFP.

Ms Viswanathan believes the government should assist with on-the-ground patrols, helicopter searches and thermal drones.

A sniffer dog is used to search for survivors following the floods in Trishuli, Nepal. (Reuters: Navesh Chitrakar)

"You never stop at anything to get your family back when they're missing. We appreciate all of the money and all the humanitarian aid that has been given. We're just hoping that we can get actual people there," she said.

Nepal has already knocked back offers of rescue assistance from foreign governments.

"The Australian government continues to offer search and rescue assistance to the Nepali authorities, but that offer hasn't been taken up," a spokesperson for the Department of Foreign Affairs told 7.30 in a statement.

"We are working with telecommunications companies to support Nepali search, rescue and recovery efforts, and assist us in ascertaining the location of those Australians who remain unaccounted for."

Missing Sydney man due to become an intern doctor

Ms Viswanathan and Mr Iyer have been friends since childhood and both became medical students in Sydney.

Mr Iyer was due to start a new job next year as an intern doctor at Gosford Hospital.

"My search will never end," Ms Viswanathan said.

" I will keep looking for him until anything is confirmed. I will never give up on him, and I know none of us will ever give up on them. "

Mr Iyer and his brother, Rudhra, 20, were keen cricketers and played for West Pennant Hills.

Rishab Iyer and his brother Rudhra were both studying medicine. (Supplied)

Their mother Lakshmi and father Sreedharan ran a childcare business and were well-loved in Sydney's Indian community.

John Kurian, 23, has been friends with Rishab since high school.

"We played cricket together since 2018 and we've lost four grand finals together," he told 7.30.

"So we've always joked around saying that we need to win another premiership. He has tried every season that he can. He's always our best player. He leads from the front verbally and with his bat and the ball."

Mr Kurian has joined Ms Visawanathan in her cause.

Rishab Iyer and John Kurian grew up together and played for their local cricket club. (Supplied)

"I'm here because he's my brother. Rishab and Rudhra are my brothers, and Sreedharan and Lakshmi are also my mum and dad," he said.

"They are out there somewhere right now. Maybe they can't be reached … because they are stuck or the communication towers are knocked down. The least we can do is try and get more people out there to help."

Son flies to India to search for missing parents

Umesh and Krishna Sharma were part of the same pilgrimage group as the Iyers and are also missing. (Supplied)

The Iyer family was staying at the same hotel as another missing Sydney family, the Sharmas, who were all on the same pilgrimage tour.

The two families were close.

Chitrak Sharma, 23, was in Sydney when he heard about the disaster in Nepal.

His mother Krishna and father Umesh are still missing.

"They're true Australians who lived by generosity, inclusivity, and just giving back to the community," Mr Sharma told 7.30.

"The first thing I did was I tried calling. Of course, [I got] nothing.

Chitrak Sharma, pictured left, with his mother Krishna, father Umesh, and brother Chaitanya. (Supplied: Chitrak Sharma)

"I tried calling someone else that I know was with them. No contact was able to be made. Still, I didn't take it too seriously because I mean, just what are the odds?"

Mr Sharma decided to fly to India and is now south of Delhi, where he is deciding whether to continue to Nepal.

"What made me take a flight here? It had been four days and no concrete news, and I figured I may have to head to Nepal very soon for any reason," he said.

"So that's why I'm basically on stand-by mode here in India with the rest of my extended family."

Mr Sharma remained hopeful but said he was prepared for the worst.

"I've thought about it, and just for assumption's sake I have brought some DNA samples with me. I brought hair in case, but I don't want to think too much about that right now," he said.

"My hope is that we find them safe and sound."

Families of the missing face racist comments

Amid their desperation, some of those related to the missing said they had seen racist comments on social media that denied their Australian identity.

Missing Australians A Queensland mother and a Sydney father are among dozens of Australians missing in Nepal following last week's deadly flooding.

"It's been quite disheartening to see a lot of racial comments towards the families that have gone, about 'they're not Australians'," Mr Kurian told 7.30.

"Rishab and Rudthra are as Australian as they come. They've grown up here their whole life, their education, their work, their sport, their academia, everything is here.

"So for anyone that's been saying those things, they need to really have a deep look and reconsider what they're saying."

Mr Sharma said he had also seen racist comments and wished they would stop.

Watch 7.30, Mondays to Thursdays 7:30pm on ABC iview and ABC TV

World.title: Family of Perth man missing in Nepal hoping for 'miracle'
World.content:
The family of a Perth man missing in Nepal say they are hoping for a "miracle" that he will be found alive and well.

Luke Costanzo, 30, was visiting Mount Kailash on a pilgrimage trek with the non-profit, spiritual Isha Foundation.

So far, more than 1,000 people have died, and about 4,400 people remain unaccounted for after the area was hit by a landslide and flash flooding.

Nepali survivors return to unrecognisable villages The ABC sees firsthand the devastation and rescue operation underway in the worst-hit areas of Nepal.

Mr Costanzo's family released a statement on Tuesday announcing that he was one of the Australians still missing.

"It is with heavy hearts that we share our dear son and brother, Luke Costanzo, is one of the Australians still unaccounted for in Nepal following the flooding disaster last week," they said.

"Luke is an extremely strong, compassionate, disciplined and spiritual person.

"Once he makes a decision, he commits to it fully, and he was so excited to be visiting Mount Kailash on a pilgrimage trek."

The family said they last heard from Mr Costanzo from the Gyirong port border crossing, when his group was making its way back to Kathmandu on the final day of their journey.

Queensland mum, Sydney dad among Australians missing in Nepal A Queensland mother and a Sydney father are among dozens of Australians missing in Nepal following last week's deadly flooding.

"This is an unimaginably difficult situation for us, and we request the media please respect our privacy during this time," the family said.

"We truly appreciate all the love and support from friends and family that we've received and ask everyone to keep Luke, and all those affected, in your thoughts and prayers.

"We can do nothing but continue hoping for a miracle that Luke, and the others who remain missing, are found alive and well.

"For those wishing to help in some way — and are in the position to do so — we suggest donating to aid the wonderful people on the ground who continue with rescue efforts."

World.title: Australian missing in Nepal-Tibet floods found alive
World.content:
One of 43 missing Australians has been found alive six days after catastrophic floods hit the Nepal-China border.

In a statement, the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade said it was unable to provide details about the person due to privacy obligations.

The Australian was in Tibet, China.

"It's hard to imagine the sense of relief their loved ones must be feeling after what will have been an incredibly harrowing few days," Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong said in a statement on Tuesday.

More than 4,400 people remain missing in the affected area.

The rescue effort comes after the "golden window" of the first 72 hours for finding a survivor, which experts say offers the best chances of survival without access to clean water.

Cara Severino, who was found alive in Nepal on the weekend. (Supplied)

The Australian has spoken with their family and is receiving support from consular officers.

Another Australian, Cara Severino, was safely located on the weekend, bringing the number of Australians missing following the flash floods down to 42.

Despite the welcome news, the Foreign Affairs Minister warned that the government "must remain realistic about the days ahead".

Rescue teams are battling mud, rock and debris in many hard-to-reach areas. (Reuters: Stringer)

"As each day passes, our grave concerns for those still unaccounted-for inevitably grow," she said.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) did not provide further details when asked about the missing Australian found alive today.

MOFA said it was maintaining close communication with foreign embassies to jointly conduct investigations into missing foreign nationals.

Nepalese and Indian Army rescue personnel search through damaged buildings. (AFP: Prakash Mathema)

Yesterday, the Australian government announced it would increase its humanitarian assistance for Nepal to $8 million.

Assistant Foreign Minister Matt Thistlewaite said this funding would mostly go towards the supply of hygiene kits.

"There's a desperate need for these kits for people in the region and also solar lights," he said.

"Obviously all of the power and telecommunications infrastructure has been wiped out.

"So those kits are being put together; they'll be transported by the Australian Defence Force over the coming days."

World.title: Authorities investigate reports former ADF soldier killed in Ukraine
World.content:
Australian officials are investigating reports a former ADF soldier has been killed while fighting in Ukraine.

The soldier, known by the nickname "Mozzie the Aussie", had been serving as a volunteer and combat medic in the Ukrainian International Legion's Med Team Alpha.

The ABC has been asked not to report his full name out of privacy concerns for his family, but has confirmed the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade is making inquiries with authorities in Ukraine.

His death has not been confirmed by any Australian or Ukrainian officials, but veteran and Shadow Minister for Defence Personnel, Phil Thompson, paid tribute to the former Australian soldier on social media.

In a statement, Mr Thompson remembered his friend as someone "who earned the respect of all who served alongside him".

"He was the kind of bloke who never hesitated to put others before himself. He was a good man, a great soldier, and someone his mates could always rely on when it mattered most," he said.

"Through his courage, skill and selfless commitment to others, Mozzie saved countless lives on the battlefield.

"My thoughts are with Mozzie's family, friends, and brothers in the battalion in both Australia and Ukraine as they mourn this terrible loss."

Former soldier went to Ukraine to help

Mr Thompson said "Mozzie" served in the Australian Army and was a member of the Townsville-based 1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment.

He completed deployments to Papua New Guinea before travelling to fight in Ukraine.

In a video posted online by Med Team Alpha, a masked soldier identifying himself as "Mozzie from Australia" explained why he wanted to fight in Ukraine.

Oscar Jenkins gives first interview since conviction Oscar Jenkins has given his first interview since he was sentenced to 13 years' imprisonment by Russian authorities.

"I have a military background in Australia so a lot of the skills that I had wouldn't transfer over to other jobs," he said.

"So I thought Ukraine would be the perfect opportunity to help out the country as a whole and use my skills to a good use."

The Ukrainian Armed Forces has been contacted for comment.

According to Ukraine's Military Ombudsman, "around 16,000 foreign volunteers from at least 72 countries" are serving alongside Ukrainian forces.

In June, former ADF soldier Samuel Pedrazzini was killed while fighting on the front lines in Donetsk, in eastern Ukraine.

Melbourne man Oscar Jenkins, who was captured by Russian forces while serving in Ukraine's army in 2024, recently gave his first interview since being convicted in what the Australian government has slammed as a "sham trial".

Australian authorities say they have asked Ukraine to prioritise Jenkins in any future prisoner swap with Russia.

World.title: Labor MP has 'no recollection' of serious car crash
World.content:
Labor MP Ed Husic says he feels "very lucky" to have walked away from a serious car crash, revealing the extent of his injuries as he returns from several weeks out of the public eye.

The Member for Chifley was travelling on Sydney's M7 motorway on August 4 when his vehicle was involved in a crash with a truck and another car.

Mr Husic was taken to hospital for assessment and treatment, and was discharged the next day with minor abrasions, fractures, and a concussion.

In his first public remarks since the incident, Mr Husic said he had no recollection of the incident, and said he was trying to piece together what happened on the day of the crash.

"I am completely blanked of my memory from midday of the day in which the accident occurred through to when I regained consciousness in the emergency department," he told ABC's Afternoon Briefing on Monday.

Husic lashes Labor culture A push to recognise claims of genocide in Gaza failed to gain enough support for a debate on the floor of Labor's national conference.

"I sustained a hairline fracture in one of the vertebrae, and a concussion is a new experience for me.

"I can tell you sneezing is a new experience. I always have to brace myself when I'm going to sneeze because the back introduces me to a new kind of pain and ache."

The Labor backbencher said he was fortunate to have had a speedy recovery.

"In terms of the sum of what I went through, I am very, very lucky because I am conscious, very conscious, other people don't necessarily have that type of experience," he said.

"I am very much counting my blessings."

'Keen' to get back to work

Mr Husic returned to work last week and said he was "overwhelmed" by well wishes he received from parliamentary colleagues and across the community.

On Tuesday, he released dash cam footage of the collision, which he has also provided to police.

Labor MP Husic criticises own party for Gaza response In a piece for The Guardian, Mr Husic says Australia "can and should be doing more" to pressure Israel, as it faces criticism from the United Nations and some former allies for only allowing "minimal" aid into war-torn Gaza.

He hoped to attend parliament when it sits next week after he missed the previous sitting fortnight.

"I am very keen to get back doing the work that I need to for my community and also obviously as a parliamentarian getting involved in different issues that I care deeply about," Mr Husic said.

"The key has been to not rush back and to take it easy as a result of concussion.

"I have been told I cannot return to parliamentary basketball. I cannot be involved in contact sports for some time, so I'm out from that."

Mr Husic previously served in cabinet as Industry and Science Minister, but has been sitting on the backbench since the 2025 election.

He was first elected to his seat in Sydney's outer west in 2010.

The outspoken MP tried to gather support for a motion at Labor's national conference in July that aimed to recognise claims of genocide in Gaza.

World.title: Disqualified driver in stolen car jailed for death, injury of motorcyclists
World.content:
A Tasmanian man whose dangerous driving left one man dead and another badly injured has been handed a nine-year prison sentence over offences a judge has described as "morally incomprehensible".

Grant Andrew Crawford, 55, was sentenced in the Supreme Court of Tasmania in Hobart on Tuesday afternoon.

In 2023, Retnakumar Kuppusami died and Suresh Rajakumar suffered severe injuries when Crawford crashed a stolen car into a tour group of 10 Malaysian motorcyclists on December 15, near Yolla in the state's north-west, before fleeing the scene.

Crawford was disqualified from driving at the time, having only been released from prison about six months prior.

The crash occurred at Yolla, in Tasmania's north-west. (ABC News)

Justice Tamara Jago described his offending as "morally incomprehensible".

"You showed no care for anyone but yourself, interested only in fleeing the scene to avoid detection," Justice Jago said.

Crawford pleaded guilty in July to dangerous driving causing the death of Mr Kuppusami and the grievous bodily harm of Mr Rajakumar, among a range of other violence and driving charges.

Justice Jago said Mr Kuppusami was a much-loved husband and father.

"His family's life is filled with [an] unbearable sense of loss and sadness … the emotional and financial turmoil is significant and likely to be lifelong," she said.

Justice Jago said Mr Rajakumar still suffers constant pain and the injuries have impacted his ability to work.

"He can't stand for extended periods, can't walk properly … he is constantly anxious, stressed and worried," she said.

Significant previous offending, judge says

Before the collision took place, Crawford had driven dangerously for about 38 kilometres, including through a worksite where he rammed into a car with a driver inside of it and crashed through gates.

Driver had 43 pages of offences before fatal hit-and-run crash The criminal record of a 55-year-old man whose dangerous driving caused the death of a motorcyclist has been described by a judge as among the worst she has seen.

Near Yolla, after turning onto Murchison Highway, Crawford crashed into the trailer of a car which then became involved in the collision with the cyclists.

"The criminal responsibility of that act rests entirely with you … setting off a sequence of events that were beyond [the driver's] control," she said.

Justice Jago described Crawford's criminal offending history as "significant", including holding more than 40 driving offence convictions.

"This equates [to] you having been disqualified for over 50 per cent of the time you have been eligible to hold a licence," she said.

" It was almost inevitable your driving was going to bring about tragic circumstances. "

Crawford was sentenced to nine years' imprisonment, backdated to when he was remanded in custody on these charges in December 2023.

He will be eligible for parole after six years, which is December 2029.

Justice Jago ordered that Crawford will not be eligible to hold a driver's licence for six years after he is released from prison.

World.title: Alleged parent-killer prayed for forgiveness over 'mortal sin', court hears
World.content:
An Adelaide woman accused of murdering both of her parents was allegedly captured on covert police listening device recordings praying to God for forgiveness for a "mortal sin", a court has heard.

Raelene Polymiadis, 65, is standing trial in South Australia's Supreme Court charged with murdering her parents, Brenda and Lynton Anderson, using lethal doses of insulin.

She has pleaded not guilty.

The court has heard the elderly couple were both aged 94 when they died 14 months apart in March 2022 and May 2023, respectively, and were not diabetic, but that Ms Polymiadis had the condition and managed it using insulin.

In the recordings, which the jury was told were captured inside a car on the morning of June 23, 2023, a woman alleged to be Ms Polymiadis could be heard praying and saying, "please Lord, forgive my sins".

"What I did was a mortal sin," she said in the recording.

"To see my father and my mother begging me … I just wanted them to be in your glory, Lord."

The recordings also capture the woman saying her parents "did their best to raise me", and that she was "terrified and I am frightened and I am so worried for my children".

"I just don't know what to do, Lord. I didn't do it for any reason other than to try and put my mum and dad out of pain, Lord, that was ultimately … what it was about, Lord," she said.

"Ultimately, I wanted my parents to not have to go through the pain.

"Please Lord, please Lord, please Lord."

The jury had previously been played earlier covert recordings, which prosecutors alleged were captured as Ms Polymiadis was driving to an interview with police on June 20, 2023.

In those recordings, a voice was heard saying, "Please Lord, yes I have sinned, I have sinned twice … but I also know with your blessing, Lord, they did not want to go to a nursing home".

Prosecutors have also previously told the jury Ms Polymiadis allegedly wrote a set of notes that were found during a search of her home and car, and which allegedly detailed what she should be saying to police when she spoke with them.

Ms Polymiadis's defence barrister, Marie Shaw KC, previously told the jury that the context of Ms Polymiadis's alleged confession would be an issue in the trial.

The trial is continuing.

World.title: 76yo loses retirement savings as granny flat builder collapses
World.content:
After battling breast cancer, Terri Beard had planned to live in a modular home on her daughter's property to get some family support.

The 76-year-old paid $130,000 to Bella Modular, a Perth-based manufacturer of transportable granny flats and home office buildings.

But just two weeks after handing over the final payment to get the build underway, she found out the company would not be able to complete their outstanding projects due to "financial difficulties".

"I had a meltdown ... I felt terrible because I was homeless at 76, and I have worked hard over the years," she said.

An unfinished modular home pictured at Bella Modular's premises south of Perth. (ABC News: Keana Naughton)

Ms Beard said her retirement savings had been decimated but she still counts herself as "lucky" because she will have a roof over her head, after shelling out more than $140,000 to secure another modular home from a different company.

Warehouse deserted

Affected customers will now be pinning any hopes of getting their money back on Sydney-based BCR Advisory, which was appointed as the liquidator yesterday.

BCR Advisory has been tasked with winding down Bella Modular, investigating the reason behind its failure, as well as realising its assets to see if creditors can be paid back.

Dozens of customers have paid hefty deposits for homes that have not been built, while subcontractors are owed tens and thousands of dollars.

When BCR's consultant Geoff Davis today visited the company's headquarters in Hopeland on Perth's southern fringe to see what could be salvaged, there was just one unfinished modular home at the deserted site.

Geoff Davis pictured at Bella Modular's deserted site, which had been stripped bare of valuable assets. (ABC News: Keana Naughton)

"It certainly doesn't look good. We're not looking to be able to sell physical assets here, we're looking at financial recoveries," Mr Davis told the ABC.

After sitting vacant with no security, Mr Davis said it appeared the site had been stripped of anything valuable, including equipment.

Mr Davis said he would now look at other potential sources of recovery, such as trademarks or other assets that can be converted to cash.

BCR Advisory consultant Geoff Davis has been tasked with winding up the company. (ABC News: Keana Naughton)

He would also investigate whether there had been "unreasonable transactions" and whether the company had been trading while insolvent, which could form the basis of a compensation claim against its directors.

Company refuses to comment

ASIC records show Chloe Pigdon is listed as the sole director of Bella Modular.

Modular builder faces investigation WA's consumer protection commissioner calls on clients of a modular home building company that abruptly closed to lodge formal complaints so it can investigate further.

Her husband Trent Pigdon founded the company and is the day-to-day manager of the business.

Mr Pigdon refused to comment after the ABC made multiple attempts to contact the couple.

A Credit Watch report shows the company has a debt to the Australian Taxation Office of $576,614.68.

Mr Davis would also prepare a confidential report for Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC).

'Heartbreaking' losses

Steve Walczak said 51 people, including 41 clients and six contractors, had contacted him after he set up a Facebook page for people who had lost money to Bella Modular.

He claimed their combined losses amounted to $4.7 million, but this figure has not been verified independently.

Bella Modular's premises in Hopeland, on Perth's southern fringe, have now been vacated by the company. (ABC News: Kate Leaver)

While he and his wife were "lucky" their modular home was 95 per cent completed, he said it was "heartbreaking" to hear how the ordeal had affected so many lives.

"At the moment, the sentiment from the group is that there's not a lot of hope that people will get their money back," he told 102.5 ABC Perth.

Mr Davis urged affected customers and contractors to get in touch so the firm can establish what creditors are owed.

Because the homes are manufactured off-site and clients independently arrange for them to be transported and placed on sites, the contracts are not covered under building indemnity insurance which covers losses when a building company goes out of business.

One of the final buildings completed by Bella Modular on its site in Perth's south-east. (ABC News: Kate Leaver)

Commerce Minister Tony Buti said the Cook Labor government would "explore possible regulatory reforms".

"I have instructed the Department of Local Government, Industry Regulation and Safety to investigate to determine if Bella Modular breached Australian Consumer Law before going into liquidation, with a view to prosecute," Mr Buti said.

The WA Consumer Protection Commissioner has also called on clients to lodge formal complaints, so it could investigate further.

World.title: Former ADF combat medic killed while volunteering in Ukraine
World.content:
WorldEuropeRussia-Ukraine war Former ADF combat medic killed while volunteering in Ukraine David Crowe September 1, 2026 — 8:10pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

London: A former Australian Defence Force soldier hailed as a legendary combat medic has been killed in Ukraine while under fire from Russian forces, drawing praise for his “selfless” commitment to others. The soldier, known by his call sign “Mozzie” in Ukraine where he was fighting as a volunteer, was killed in action last Wednesday, according to his former Australian Army colleague, federal Liberal MP Phillip Thompson. Thompson said Mozzie served with the Townsville-based 1st Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment, and was deployed to Butterworth in Malaysia and Papua New Guinea. The news of “Mozzie’s” death drew emotional reactions from supporters of the volunteer soldiers who have fought for Ukraine. Instagram “He was a valued member of the battalion’s heavy weapons platoon, affectionately known as the ‘Fatboys’, and earned the respect of all who served alongside him,” he said in a statement.



“After leaving the Australian Army, Mozzie travelled to Ukraine where he saw significant combat and later joined Med Team Alpha, serving as a combat medic and support specialist with the 1st Foreign Legion Squadron. “Through his courage, skill and selfless commitment to others, Mozzie saved countless lives on the battlefield. He was the kind of bloke who never hesitated to put others before himself. Loading “He was a good man, a great soldier, and someone his mates could always rely on when it mattered most.” The news drew emotional reactions from supporters of the volunteer soldiers who have fought for Ukraine, including the Protect a Volunteer (PAV) group.



“Mozzie was a legend,” one group member posted on social media site Reddit. Related Article Russia-Ukraine war Government has abandoned Oscar Jenkins in Russian prison: Australian interviewer “The stories about him are crazy but true. He once transfused his own blood, several times over several days, to stabilise a guy and make him able to get evacuated. “Another time he [exfiltrated] himself due to injury then went BACK and saved Fifty. “I never actually met him myself. I only met his teammates because Mozzie was always out in the field. But he holds the all-time record for people contacting PAV just to say good things about him.”



The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has not made any public comment on his death. Mozzie’s full name was not released due to a request from his family for privacy. Related Article Russia-Ukraine war ‘Your typical Aussie cricket boy’: Why Oscar Jenkins went to fight in Ukraine Another former Australian Army soldier, Samuel Pedrazzini, died in June in the Donetsk region of Ukraine. Pedrazzini, 26, had trained Ukrainian soldiers in the United Kingdom, as part of a longstanding NATO project, before resigning from the ADF and travelling to Ukraine to volunteer as a soldier last year. A funeral service for Pedrazzini was held in the western Ukrainian town of Chukalivka, near Ivano-Frankivsk, early in July.



His commander, whose call-sign is Alex, praised the Australian for his military skill, according to a report in The New Voice of Ukraine. “Sam was an excellent machine gunner, a great marksman and a skilled medic. He was a person who could do absolutely everything,” Alex said. Loading “Prior to enlisting, he volunteered at stabilisation points to save wounded soldiers. Samuel deeply loved Ukraine and wanted to stay here. “At some point, he realised that he wanted to fight for Ukraine, defend its freedom and independence, and become a part of this society.”



The news follows the emergence of a video interview with another Australian volunteer fighter, Oscar Jenkins, who was captured by Russian forces in December 2024 and is now in prison. Jenkins was sentenced by a Russian court to 13 years in a penal colony, in a decision that Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described as an outrage. In the interview, Jenkins told Australian interviewer Mark Lowe, a teacher and amateur journalist based in Vladivostok, that he had offered to fight for Russia but had been turned down.
